situations: You read the words printed on the side of a delivery box: 'This side up'. What is that printed text on the box called?
An old stone in the park has a few words carved into it, telling you who it remembers. What do we call those carved words?
Your friend's T-shirt has a funny sentence printed on the front, and you ask what the text on it says.
A colleague asks where you spend most of your time on workdays, and you answer: 'Mostly in the lab on the second floor.'
A police officer in a TV show asks the man where he was on the night of the robbery. He says where he was staying that night.
You are on holiday and your friend asks how long you will be living in this small town for the moment.
A fruit has a smell and a shape that only this fruit has. You say: 'That smell is typical and special for it, you always know it.'
A painter has a very special style, so you can always recognise his pictures at once. Which word describes such a typical feature?
A doctor says a certain rash is a typical sign of one particular illness.
You travel from Europe to Japan and go to the bank, because you need yen instead of euros.
The news says that the dollar became weaker this week compared to other kinds of money used by countries.
At school you learn that each country has its own money system, for example pounds in Britain. What is the word for it?
You see a rainbow with two arcs in the sky, which is rare and hard to explain. Scientists call such a rare event in nature a ...?
A teacher shows the class why the northern lights appear. It is a strange natural event that people have wondered about for centuries.
Your friend says that many young people suddenly use a new app, and nobody understands why it became so popular so fast. It is a social event worth studying.
The doctors work hard every day to stop a dangerous illness from spreading in the country.
A city council puts money into a plan to stop crime on its streets. The goal is to work against it with all means.
A gardener sprays the plants to get rid of insects that are eating the leaves. What is the word for working against pests?
Two companies decide to work together on a new car. They sign a paper about working side by side instead of against each other.
In your group project at university everyone shares tasks and helps the others, so the result is much better.
A sports club and a school plan to share their halls and trainers. Which word means 'working together'?
You arrive on Monday evening and fall asleep quickly. About the day that comes right after that evening, you say it was sunny.
A newspaper writes about a big storm, then reports on the clean-up work on the day that came right after it.
You tell a friend about a party, and then about the week that came after it. Which word means 'coming right after'?
On a walk in late summer you pick small, dark, juicy fruits from a thorny bush by the path. They are almost black and stain your fingers purple.
At the market you buy a small box of berries that are darker than raspberries. They are sweet and a little sour.
Your grandmother bakes a pie with dark purple berries that she picked in the hedge. Which berry is it?
The bus leaves in five minutes, but your little brother is walking very slowly and keeps stopping to look at things.
Your teacher says: 'Please do not waste time and take so long when you pack your bag. We want to leave now!'
Your friend takes forever to get dressed in the morning and always makes everyone late. What do we say about someone who is so slow on purpose?
You and your friends talked about many ideas for dinner for an hour, and when everything was said, you picked pizza.
After weeks of doubts, a student says: 'All things considered, I chose to study medicine.' Which word means 'in the end'?
A tired runner struggled through the whole race and, after the long fight, reached the finish line.
At a concert hall you read a poster about Beethoven and Mozart. They were famous men who wrote music for orchestras.
A friend tells you he wants to write songs and symphonies for a living. What do we call a person with this job?
A film director looks for a person who can write the music for his new movie.
The label on the juice says it has a low amount of sugar inside. What is the word for how much of something a thing contains?
A teacher says that the poem has a deep meaning, even if the words are simple. She talks about what is inside the text.
Water from the mountains has a high amount of minerals. A scientist measures how much of them it holds.

en: to observe, to meet, to keep, to comply with
situations: You promise your boss to finish the report by Friday and you make sure that you do not miss that date.
At the pool there is a sign with rules. Everyone has to follow them, for example no running.
The driver sticks to the speed limit of 50 km/h in the town and does not go faster.
You find a very small ant that is so little you can hardly see it on the table.
The hotel room was so small that there was almost no space for the bed, only a very little bit of floor.
A baby holds your finger with a very small hand. Which word means 'extremely small'?
You plan a ski trip to a country in the Alps with Vienna as its capital, south of Germany and north of Italy.
At the airport the sign says your flight goes to Vienna. In which country will you land?
A friend tells you that Mozart was born in Salzburg. Name the country where this city lies.
A math teacher draws a shape with four corners on the board. Two sides are long and two are short, and all the corners are square.
Your door is a shape with four straight sides, longer than it is wide. Which shape is it?
You cut a sheet of paper in half the long way. It is not a square, because two sides are longer.
A ball falls off the table and moves across the floor under the sofa.
At the airport you pull your suitcase on its little wheels along the hall.
The children push a big barrel down the hill and watch it turn round and round.
A scientist writes down: 'Water boils faster at this height.' It is a short thing she noticed and says out loud.
Your friend says: 'I notice you have a new haircut.' He just says what he has seen. What is the word for such a remark?
A police report lists what the officers found out at the scene.
Your old teacher never let anybody ask questions or disagree. He gave orders and everybody had to obey without discussion.
A father who decides everything alone and never listens to his children is described with this word.
Which word describes a leader who demands total obedience and allows no free opinions?

en: to become closer, to get closer to, to near
situations: You have been working in the same office for a year, and slowly you and your colleague talk more and become real friends.
A storm is far away, but every hour it comes a bit nearer to your town.
At the end of the year the goal of a big project is nearly in reach. You are just a little bit away from reaching it.
A diver in the sea swims past a long line of coral just under the water, full of colourful fish.
A ship captain warns: 'Careful, there are sharp rocks just below the surface near the island!'
On a holiday film you see a long wall of living coral in warm tropical water, near the beach.
A man you have never seen before walks up to your door and asks for the way. He is a person you do not know.
Your mother tells you as a child: 'Do not go with someone you do not know, a man you have never met.'
A man who has just come from another country sits alone in the cafe and looks around, not knowing anyone. The word for him is?

en: to to lock up, to surround, to include
situations: The teacher turns the key and keeps the thief in the room, so he cannot get out.
A wall goes all around the garden and closes it in on every side.
The price for the hotel includes breakfast and parking, so these are also part of what you pay.
You like thin, soft sand on the beach; the grains are very small. You also like the very thin lines in a pen drawing.
At a nice restaurant, the waiter says the dishes are of high quality and made with great care.
A tailor looks at a thin silk thread and says it is delicate and not coarse at all.
At a Christmas dinner there are small green balls on the plate, like tiny cabbages, that some children do not like.
At the supermarket you buy small round green vegetables that grow on a long stem, and you cook them in water.
Your uncle says he hates a certain vegetable that looks like a very tiny cabbage and tastes a bit bitter. Which vegetable is it?
On Sunday morning in church, about thirty people stand together and sing in many voices, led by one person.
At school you join a group of kids who sing songs together, and you practise every Thursday.
A big concert needs an orchestra and a large group of singers standing behind it.
Your little sister cries because her balloon flew away, and you hug her and say: 'Don't be sad, we'll buy a new one.'
A friend fails his driving test and is very sad, so you sit next to him and speak kind words to make him feel better.
After a bad day at work, your partner puts an arm around you. What does she do to help your sad feelings?
An accountant tells a company that a machine loses value every year, and the company can write off a part of the cost in its yearly taxes.
You run a small shop and your laptop is now three years old. For your tax form you can count some of its cost as a loss of value.
In the finance course the teacher explains how the value of a company car goes down on paper each year. Which word means this?
You eat chocolate and waffles in Brussels, and you read the sign that says the beer is from this country between France and the Netherlands.
Your friend comes from Antwerp and says his passport is from Brussels' country. What word describes his nationality?
A cyclist who won the race comes from this small country in western Europe. His team is called after it.

en: of all things, of all times, of all people
situations: It rains on the one day you wanted to have a picnic. You say: 'Why did it rain today of all days?'
Your phone dies at the exact moment your boss calls. You say: 'Why did it have to happen right now, of all times?'
There are twenty cafes in town, but your ex is sitting in exactly the one you chose. 'Why him, of all people?'
At the fair you buy a thin, crispy, sweet snack in a heart shape with powdered sugar.
You eat ice cream and the cold ball of ice sits in a crunchy cone that you can eat as well.
Your friend brings a thin crispy biscuit with chocolate cream between two layers to the coffee break.

en: to find out, to investigate, to determine, to establish, to identify
situations: The police work for weeks to find out who broke into the museum. They gather clues, speak with people and check cameras.
A scientist measures and calculates to learn exactly how old the old bone is.
The bank tries to find out how much your house is worth by checking prices of similar houses.
At home you have a quiet room with a desk, a computer and bookshelves, where you do your paperwork and read in the evening.
Your friend shows you the flat: kitchen, bedroom, and the little room where he works from home.
A writer closes the door of the room with his desk and books so that he is not disturbed.
You sit on your bike and push your foot down on the part that turns the wheel.
In a car, you press your foot on the part on the floor to make it go faster or to stop.
A piano player presses a part of the piano with her foot to make the sound last longer.
Someone asks why you went to Berlin. You answer: 'For the biggest reason, the work, and only a bit for fun.'
The shop sells shoes, but it sells mostly sport shoes. Which word means 'for the most part'?
The most important reason for the delay is the snow on the tracks. The other reasons are small.
You were born in a small village, and you spent your childhood there until you were eighteen.
A famous singer says in an interview that she became an adult in a poor part of the city.
Your friend tells about his childhood with five brothers on a farm. How do we say what happens to a child over the years while he becomes older?
A child in a story book is scared of a big hairy creature with many eyes and sharp teeth under the bed.
In a cartoon, a huge green creature with horns and a loud roar chases the heroes through a cave.
At Halloween, your little cousin dresses up as a scary, made-up creature with fur and fangs.
Before the big exam, you feel very nervous, your shoulders are stiff and you cannot relax.
A doctor says your tight neck is a result of stress and that your muscles are working too hard all the time.
Before the final penalty kick in the match, the whole stadium is silent and everyone feels strong nervous pressure.
On the evening news you hear that two men suddenly came into a shop and took money from the cashier.
In a history film, soldiers come out of the forest at night and surprise the village.
A football team suddenly attacks in the last minute and scores a goal. What does the team do to its surprised opponent?
Your small son holds his hand to the side of his head and cries because it hurts inside, after a cold.
At the doctor you say: 'I have a sharp pain inside my left ear since last night, and I cannot sleep.'
After swimming in cold water, you feel a pain in your ear. What is this pain called?
You find a wallet full of money on the street, and you feel it is right and good to give it back to its owner.
A teacher talks with the class about what is good or bad behaviour, apart from what the law says.
In a film the hero must decide between a right and a wrong choice. Which word describes questions of right and wrong?
Two men in the park sit at a table and move little figures like kings and horses on a board with sixty-four black and white squares.
Your grandfather gives you a wooden board for a game of kings and queens. It has eight rows of squares.
A floor in the hotel hall has black and white squares, like the playing board of a famous strategy game.
A hiking path goes along the river for two kilometres and then turns up the hill.
Your friend asks how the job interview went, and you say that everything went without problems.
The border between the two fields runs along a line of trees. How do we say what a line or a road does when it stretches somewhere?
Your grandmother has a short wise sentence on the wall of the kitchen: 'Home is where the heart is.'
A company prints a short catchy line on a poster to sell its drink. What do we call such a line?
You find a short funny sentence on a birthday card, written inside by the printer.
The white dove is a sign of peace. It does not mean only a bird, it stands for an idea.
The shop owner sold the old chair for one euro. It was not about money, the price had only an idea behind it.
At the ceremony, the mayor hands over a big key to the guest. It is not a real key to a door, it stands for a welcome.
The manager has many good ideas for the office, but now the team must put them into practice in real work.
A translator changes a text from one language to another. This work needs time and care.
The plan looks great on paper, but its carrying out in reality is difficult. Which word names this step?

en: to steer, to direct, to guide
situations: You sit behind the wheel of the car and turn it to go round the corner.
The teacher moves the attention of the class to the board by pointing at it.
A pilot takes the plane in the right direction by using the controls, and so he guides it safely.
You visit London, drink tea with milk and watch a football match. Which part of the United Kingdom are you in?
Shakespeare was born in this country, which lies next to Scotland and Wales.
At school, you learn that the capital of this country, London, is on the river Thames.

en: in between, between them, among them
situations: Two big trees stand in the garden. You say: 'The bench is right there, in the space that is between them.'
You have a lesson at nine and another at eleven. A friend asks what you do at ten, in the time that is between both.
On a bookshelf, you put a small picture where it sits among the two big books. Which word means 'in the middle of two things'?
In the newspaper you look for the part with football results, which has its own title and place on the page.
On a web page there are different parts with headings: sport, weather, culture. You click on the one for weather.
On a form there are boxes for name, age and address. Which word names each of these parts or fields with a heading?

en: to draw up, to write, to compose, to author
situations: A student sits at her laptop and spends two evenings producing a long letter to the city office, with formal words.
A lawyer writes a legal contract for his client and takes care over each word.
A famous author sits in a cafe and works on a novel with his own words. What does he do to the text?
You see a small puppy with big eyes, playing with its tail. 'Aww, look how sweet and lovely it is!'
A baby smiles at you from the pram, and everyone says it looks so adorable.
Your sister buys a tiny teddy bear with a little red hat. A friend says it is very pretty and charming. Which word is this?
In a hospital, a man in green clothes and a mask uses a knife and tools to take out your appendix while you sleep.
A doctor who operates on hearts spends hours in the operating room. What do we call this doctor?
Your uncle trained for ten years to cut and repair parts of the body in the operating room.
You get out of the train in a new city and look at a map to find out where you are and which way to go.
A hiker holds a compass and uses it to find the north direction in the forest.
A new student is lost on the first day at university and looks for signs to get some sense of the place.
At night you look through a telescope and see Mars, a red round object that circles the sun, as the Earth does.
A teacher shows a picture of the solar system. Earth, Venus and Jupiter all go around the sun.
A child asks you what Saturn with its rings is. It is one of eight big round bodies that orbit our sun.

en: college, university, academy, higher education institution
situations: After finishing school at eighteen, you want to study engineering for three years in a big building where you also get a degree.
Your cousin goes to lectures at a school for higher learning where she studies music and gets a diploma.
The sign near the station says: 'University of Applied Sciences'. What kind of place is that, for study after secondary school?
When you come home after a year abroad, the smell of the kitchen and the sound of the old clock feel well known and comfortable.
The two old friends know each other so well that they can talk about everything and feel very close.
You are not new to this software; you already know how it works. Which word means 'well known to you'?

en: to go to see, to visit, to consult
situations: You have a bad cough, so you decide to go and see a doctor to have it checked.
When he came to the city, the writer went to see his old teacher at her home.
If the pain continues, please go to a specialist. Which word means 'to go to a place or person for help'?
You need to sew a button on your shirt, so you put a long thin piece of cotton through the eye of the needle.
A spider hangs on a very thin line from the ceiling, coming down slowly.
A kite flies high in the sky, held by a long, thin cord in the boy's hand.
On a crime TV show, detectives spend weeks collecting evidence about a missing painting. The work they do is called?
The tax office is busy with checking and figuring out exactly how much money you earned last year.
After the accident, experts start looking into the causes to find out what happened.
In a TV court, a woman in a black robe listens to both sides and then decides who is right and who is wrong.
Your grandmother says: 'Do not form an opinion about people before you know them.'
A food critic tries many dishes and gives a decision about which restaurant is best.

en: as it were, so to speak
situations: You describe a very quiet city in the evening and say: 'The streets were empty, so to speak, as if the world had stopped.'
A teacher explains: 'The heart is, as it were, the engine of the body.' She uses a word like 'so to speak'.
Your friend says his dog is, in a way, a member of the family. Which word means 'as it were'?
You slip on the ice and land hard on the body part you sit on, and it hurts for days.
A baby sits on the floor, and his diaper makes the lower part of his body look big.
Which rude, informal word do some people use for the lower back part of a person that you sit on? Use it only among close friends.
On the crowded train, someone pushes you with the sharp, bent part of his arm in the middle.
You fall off your bike and hurt the joint in the middle of your arm. It bleeds, so you put on a plaster.
A doctor asks you to bend your arm and shows where the upper and lower arm meet.
Before you send the email to your boss, you think carefully how to put your request into good words.
The lawyer sits at his desk and finds the exact words for the clause in the agreement.
A speaker has a thought in his head but has trouble putting it into clear sentences.
At a romantic dinner, a man goes down on one knee, takes out a ring and asks his girlfriend a big question about spending life together.
Your friend plans to ask his partner to be his wife in front of the Eiffel Tower. What will he make there?
In a film, she says yes with tears in her eyes when he asks her to marry him. What is his question called?
The weather changes everywhere on Earth, not only in one country. Experts talk about the warming of the whole world.
A company has shops in forty countries on all continents and sells to people all over the world.
The internet connects people across the whole planet. Which word means 'worldwide'?
After your stay in the hotel, you give it four stars and write a few lines on the website for other travellers.
The teacher reads the exams and gives each student a mark. This judging of the work is her job.
A house expert checks the building and says how much it is worth. What is the word for this judgement?

en: to go on ahead, to be fast, to have priority, to come first, to proceed
situations: The ambulance has the right of way, so all cars must let it go first.
You say to your friend: 'You can start walking ahead, I will follow you in a minute.'
The manager explains how to handle the problem step by step, so everyone knows which way to act.
The roads are covered with ice. So, as a result, the school buses stay in the garage today.
You did not study at all, so it is not surprising that you failed the test. Which word means 'as a result'?
The shop is closed on Sundays. You wanted to buy bread on Sunday. You could not buy any, and so you say it with this word.
In the museum you walk through rooms with pictures made with brushes and oil colours on canvas.
Your aunt studies the art of making pictures with colour, and the subject at art school is not sculpture or music.
A guide at the gallery talks about the art that uses brushes, paint and canvas. Which word names this kind of art?
The TV weather woman says what the weather will probably be like over the next three days.
Economic experts say how the unemployment numbers will change next year, and they make a guess about the future.
A doctor tells you how an illness will probably develop in the coming months.
You place the plates one on top of the other in the kitchen, so they take less space.
In the warehouse, workers put boxes up high, one on top of another, until they almost touch the ceiling.
After the cleaning, the books lie on the floor in heaps. How do we describe what you do to arrange them in one tall pile?
For a job interview, you wear a suit and speak politely to the manager, with no jokes or slang.
You write an official letter to the city office and start with 'Dear Sir or Madam'. The style is serious and not casual.
The wedding dinner has strict rules about dress and speeches. Which word describes such an event?
A teacher points to the world map and names the big land masses: Africa, Asia, Europe and others.
You fly from one huge land mass to another across the ocean, from Europe to South America.
Australia is the smallest of the seven large land areas on Earth. What are these big areas called?
A mechanic shows you the metal bar that connects the two wheels of the car and lets them turn.
A teacher shows a globe, which turns around an imaginary line through the North and the South Pole.
In a maths class, you draw a line for the x-values and a line for the y-values on paper.
The train has a delay, and you arrive at the meeting ten minutes after it has started.
Your friend writes: 'Sorry, I will not be on time. I will come at half past eight and not at eight.'
The teacher stands at the door at nine, and a student comes in at five past nine. What happens to the student?
In the forest you see the thick, brown, woody part of the tree that holds up the branches, and a boy cannot put his arms around it.
In a documentary, a group of people in the jungle live together under one chief and share the same language and customs.
The woodcutter cuts the big tree at the bottom, and it falls. Which part does he cut?
You enjoy a cake called Sachertorte, which comes from Vienna. You say it is a dessert from the Alpine country south of Germany.
A ski racer from Innsbruck stands on the podium, and the flag has red and white stripes. What is his nationality?
At the cafe there is a coffee with whipped cream that comes from Vienna. Which word describes its origin?
On New Year's Eve at midnight, people stand outside and watch colourful lights and bangs in the night sky.
At the end of the city festival, there are loud booms and bright sparks high above the river.
Children look up at the dark sky on the fourth of July as red, blue and gold lights explode high over the town.
The boy broke the window with his ball, and finally he says: 'Yes, it was me, I did it.'
In a quarrel you realise you were wrong, so you say: 'OK, you are right, that was my mistake.'
In a TV crime show, the man says to the police that he was at the scene. What does he do?

en: classical antiquity, classical age, classical music
situations: At a concert the orchestra plays music by Mozart and Haydn, from the time before Romanticism.
At school, you learn about the ancient Greeks and Romans and the golden age of their art.
The radio station plays only symphonies and string quartets, never pop. Which word names this kind of music or period?
The newspaper writes about changes that touch all people living together in the country, like the way families live.
Old people lonely at home is a problem for everyone living together, not only for the family.
A speaker says that the topic affects everybody living together in a community. Which word means 'concerning society'?
A man at the next table speaks with an accent from Texas and says he flew here from the United States.
Your new colleague comes from New York, and you say that he is a citizen of the country with the Statue of Liberty.
The man in the baseball cap says he was born in Chicago. What is he called by nationality?

en: to achieve, to reach, to obtain
situations: In the last minute, the striker scores and brings his team the win. A reporter says he reached a goal.
After months of negotiating, the two companies finally got a good result for both sides.
With careful saving over the years, she manages to get good profits. Which word means 'to get a result'?
After the football match, a group of fans start hitting each other in the street, and the police arrive.
At the party, two men argue, and soon they push and punch each other while others try to pull them apart.
The headmaster speaks to two boys because they were hitting each other in the schoolyard. What was the event?
You are tired at the bus stop, so you put your back against the wall.
The old man stands by the window and rests his arms on the sill.
The bicycle is not on its stand. You put it against the fence so it does not fall.
You sharpen your pencil, and now its end is very thin and sharp.
After a long climb, you stand on the highest point of the mountain and look down.
The wedding dress has a fine decorated cloth with small holes, which is made from thread in beautiful patterns.
Two phones from different brands have almost the same size, price and features, so you can put them side by side to choose.
You cannot compare an apple with a car, but you can compare two similar cars. The second case is...?
A teacher says the two essays are of the same standard, so they can be measured against each other.

en: now and then, from time to time, sometimes, occasionally
situations: My uncle is usually quiet, but there are some days, not often, when he tells long stories at dinner.
At the weekend you do not always sleep late, but on certain mornings you do, so you say how often with one small word.
The train is usually on time, but from time to time it has a delay.
You tie your shoelaces, and then they will not come apart because you made a hard tie.
The doctor feels a small hard lump under your skin and wants to check it.
In the harbour, a sailor ties a rope to a pole with a strong, tight loop.

en: to deteriorate, to expire, to decay, to lapse
situations: Your train ticket is no longer valid because the date has passed, so it is of no use.
The old house at the end of the street has been empty for twenty years, and bit by bit it is falling apart.
If you do not use your coupon before the end of the month, you lose it because it runs out.
A sailor in the year 1492 sees a new land that nobody in Europe knew. This finding changed history.
In the lab, a scientist finds a new medicine by accident. The news says it was an important find.
Your child finds a shiny stone in the garden and shouts with joy. What is the word for finding something new?
The library has two books of the same title. You take one of the two, the very book you hold in your hands.
A biologist shows one animal of a rare species that the museum has in a glass case.
The author signs one book from the printed run, and the publisher says that only 500 of this kind exist.
Buying a house is not a quick decision. You think about the next twenty years and make a plan that lasts a long time.
The company says it wants steady growth over many years and not just a quick profit this month.
A doctor says that the changes in your diet will only show results after a very long time. Which word means 'for a long period'?
The film is made from a true story. What it shows is built on facts that happened in real life.
Her success is not only luck. It has its foundation in many years of hard work.
The teacher asks on what the whole theory is founded, and a student answers with the main idea.
You get dressed in the morning and first put on a piece of clothing under your trousers.
On a washing line you see socks, shirts and small cotton garments that are worn closest to the skin.
At the shop you buy a pack of three small cotton garments for under your jeans. What are they?
In the chemistry lab, the teacher shows a white powder and says it is a material with fixed properties.
A critic says the new film looks nice but has no real depth or meaning, so there is little of real value in it.
The label on the bottle says it contains a harmful matter, a chemical material. What is the word for it?
After a long day you lie in bed, close your eyes, and soon you are sleeping.
During the boring film, your father's head falls down and he begins to snore on the sofa.
The baby is calm now. A mother says: 'Shh, she is just about to drift off into sleep.'
At the end of the semester you sit in a big hall for two hours and write answers on paper while the teacher watches you. Which word names this written university test?
Your sister cannot go out on Friday because she has a big written test at university on Monday morning.
Monks live behind high walls in a quiet part of the monastery where visitors may not enter. This closed area has the same name.
You look for a belt that goes well with your brown shoes, one in the same colour and style.
The teacher says your answer is just right for the question, because it says exactly what was asked.
You have a wedding to go to. Which word describes clothes that are right for such an event?
Your family doctor sends you to a colleague who knows everything about skin problems, because that is the one area he knows best.
A professor knows a little about all of history, but there is one small area in which he is the top expert.
At the job interview, the boss asks: 'What is the field you are best in?' Which word names that area?
The child is angry and pulls the paper apart with both hands, and now there are two pieces on the floor.
Your jeans caught on a nail and now there is a long opening in the leg.
You do not want anyone to read the old letter, so you pull it into little pieces before you throw it away.
The table has a sharp line where the top meets the side, and your little son bumps his head on it.
You stand at the very end of the cliff, near where the ground ends and falls away. The place is dangerous.
A carpenter runs his hand along the place where two surfaces of the wood meet, to check if it is smooth.
After the accident, your grandfather cannot walk and needs other people to help him with shopping and cooking.
A student without savings must rely on the money his parents send each month, or he cannot pay his rent.
A small village has no shop, so the people can only live if they have a car. Which word describes the need to rely on something?
Some actors walk into a room and everybody looks at them. They have a special power that draws people in.
After a happy holiday, your friend has a positive glow that others notice at once.
The news says a famous radio programme goes out on the air tonight at eight. What is the word for sending a programme out?
You want to ask the shop about your order, so you write them an email or call them to get in touch.
A police officer says: 'If you saw anything, please get in touch with us at this number.'
Your boss asks you to reach out to the customer who has not answered for two weeks.
On the weekend you go to a hotel with a sauna, a pool and a massage, to relax and feel good.
A magazine has a page about healthy food, gentle sport and quiet time that make you feel well in body and mind.
The flyer shows a spa with warm baths and herbal tea. Which English-sounding word describes this type of relaxing holiday?
On the map you see the large island with England, Scotland and Wales. Which island or country is it?
A friend flies to London for work and then to Edinburgh by train. Both cities lie on the same large island in the north-west of Europe.
At the Olympics, the team in blue and red, with players from England, Scotland and Wales, wins a medal.
Our company sells many types of shoes, but the larger part of the sales is sport shoes. Which word means 'for the greatest part'?
In the south of the country it rains a lot, but it is mostly sunny in the east, and there are only a few exceptions.
The audience at the concert was largely young people, with a few older ones.
In maths class, the teacher asks you to take 7 and make it 8 times bigger: 7 times 8 equals 56.
A baker has a recipe for four people and needs it for twelve, so he takes every amount three times as large.
You are calculating the area of a room by taking its length and its width together, using the times sign.
Your new colleague arrives early every day, has many ideas and really wants to do a good job.
The football coach says that his players are full of energy and eager to win the next game.
After watching an inspiring speech, you feel ready and want to start your project right now.
You have a bad back, and the doctor gives you medicine and ten sessions with a physiotherapist.
The hospital says the care of the patient will take three weeks, with daily checks.
A customer complains that the way the staff dealt with him in the shop was rude. What is this way of dealing called?
Your body has its own defence against germs. In winter it works hard to keep you from getting a cold.
A doctor says that sleep, vegetables and sport make your body better able to fight illness by itself.
When people get a vaccination, it helps the body's natural protection learn to fight a disease.

en: to correspond to, to meet, to comply with, to conform to
situations: The new building looks exactly like the plans the architect drew. It matches them.
The hotel room did not live up to the pictures on the website, so you complain.
The goods you receive must meet the quality rules in the contract. Which word means 'to be in line with'?
The manager gives the new worker a short note: 'First turn on the machine, then press the green button.'
A policeman at the crossing says loudly: 'Stop here!' and people must do what he says.
The package comes with a leaflet that shows how to put the shelf together step by step.
Your friend calls in the morning and asks if you can come to dinner tonight. This is without much time to plan.
The company needs a quick fix to solve the problem this week, and not a plan for many years.
The concert is cancelled just one hour before, with hardly any warning. Which word describes such a notice?
You started learning a language last month, so you are at a low stage, and your teacher puts you in the beginners' class.
The restaurant was very expensive and the food was of a high standard, so everybody was happy.
The sea has risen by a few centimetres, so the height of the water is higher than before.

en: to have on you, to have with you
situations: A friend asks: 'Hey, do you have a pen on you right now?' and you check your bag.
You go to the airport and you must be sure that you have your passport in your pocket.
It starts to rain, and you are glad that you brought an umbrella along.
You read the newspaper and find a short text from a company that is looking for a new worker and lists the tasks and pay.
On a website, you search for a text by a shop that wants to hire a salesperson, and you apply.
Your father writes a text for the local paper because his bakery needs a new baker. What is this text called?
The weather report warns about a big storm, which makes your mother nervous about her trip.
A strange noise from the engine makes the driver feel uneasy and unsure.
The doctor's face looks serious, and the test results make you feel anxious. What does the news do to you?
Your flight was cancelled, and the airline gives you money back for the trouble it caused you.
After a car crash, the insurance pays you for the damage to your car.
The shop sent a broken product and offers you a payment to make up for it. Which word names this?

en: honorary, voluntary, voluntarily, on a voluntary basis
situations: On Saturdays, my aunt works at the food bank without getting any pay, because she wants to help others.
The sports club coach is not paid. He does it as a free service in his spare time.
Many people in the town help at the fire brigade without a salary. Which word describes such work?
In 1990, the two parts of Germany became one country again, after the fall of the wall. What is this event called?
A history teacher tells how East and West came together as a single state after many years apart.
A TV report about two parts of a country that were split and are now being joined again.
You open a bottle of fizzy water, and tiny round air pieces rise up through the liquid.
Water comes up out of the ground in the mountains, and it moves up and makes a happy noise.
In a pot, the soup starts to make small bubbles just before it boils.
A magician makes a coin vanish in front of the children. They ask him to show how it was done.
Your friend has a clever little way to open a jar that is stuck: he hits the lid with a spoon.
In a game of cards, your friend plays a clever move to fool you.
The forecast says there is only a two percent chance of snow in July. Snow is very unlikely, you think.
It is hard to believe that she did not get your message, so you doubt her story.
Winning the lottery has a tiny chance of happening. Which word describes something that will probably not happen?
In a western film, the cowboy pulls a small weapon from a holster at his belt.
A police officer in a TV show carries a small weapon on his belt that shoots bullets.
At the athletics track, a starter fires a loud blank shot with a small gun to begin the race.

en: to believe sb capable of, to think sb capable of
situations: Your boss thinks that you can lead the new project even though you have never done it. He says: 'I know you can do it.'
Your friend says: 'I would never think that he is able to cook a three-course meal, he can barely make toast.'
A trainer believes his young player can win a gold medal, so he gives him a place in the final.
When your grandmother died, she left her house and some money to the family. This is what you receive.
The old castle and the traditions of a country are a part of its history that is passed on to future generations.
Your uncle writes in his will who will get his things after his death. What is this called?

en: in this respect, as far as that goes
situations: You say: 'Yes, you are right to that extent, but there is one more thing to consider.'
A teacher says: 'To this degree it is a good essay, but the end is weak.'
A friend says that the plan works only if everyone helps. Which word means 'in that respect' or 'as far as that is concerned'?
The bridge can carry a weight of 30 tons, and above this number it may break.
After working double shifts for months, the nurse says she feels too much pressure and she is tired.
A doctor says that the heavy weight on your knees from running on hard ground may cause pain.
You find old photos from your childhood, and you feel a sweet sadness and miss those days.
The old man listens to a song from his youth and smiles with a little sadness in his eyes.
At the end of summer, you look at the empty beach and feel a soft longing for the past. What word describes this mood?
The witness in the TV court says: 'No, I did not do it. It is not true.'
Your friend is asked if he took the last cake, but he says: 'It was not me, I did not touch it.'
A politician in the news says he never met the man, though the paper claims he did. What does he do to the claim?
The queen wears a gold circle with jewels on her head at the royal ceremony.
In Sweden, Denmark and Norway you pay with a currency whose name is the same as the king's headwear.
A dentist puts an artificial cover over a broken tooth. Also, the highest part of a tree has leaves and branches.

en: water body, body of water, stretch of water
situations: On the map, a lake, a river and a pond are all drawn in blue. What is the word for all of them together?
The environment office tests the quality of rivers and lakes in the area to see if they are clean.
The sign says that swimming is forbidden in the area, because it is a protected part of nature with water.

en: to send, to ship, to dispatch
situations: Before Christmas, you put cards in envelopes and put them all in the post box for friends in many countries.
A company sells books on the internet and every day packs them in boxes and ships them to the customers.
The school sends a letter about the party trip to all the parents at the same time.
A big city is divided into twenty-three parts, each with its own local office and a name, like Kreuzberg or Mitte.
The police chief of one area of the city says that the crime numbers are low there.
In Vienna, you say you live in the 7th part of the city. What is that part called?
At a party, a man arrives who nobody invited, and the host does not want him there.
A sign on the door says that salespeople who come to your door are not welcome.
Bad side effects from a drug are results that nobody wants. Which word describes them?
Your grandmother opens a big book with old photos stuck on its pages.
A band spends two years in the studio and then publishes twelve songs together on one disc.
A boy collects football stickers and puts each one in a special book with empty spaces.

en: to accuse, to charge, to indict
situations: In a courtroom film, the prosecutor stands up and officially says that the man in front of the judge has committed a crime.
The newspaper writes that the state has formally charged the manager with cheating on his taxes.
The lawyer says his client should not be blamed, as the court begins the trial. What does the prosecutor do first?
The special lighting in the film created a strong result on the audience, and many were afraid.
A medicine was tested, and the doctors say that it has a clear positive result on blood pressure.
In a photo app you click on a button, and your picture suddenly looks like an old painting.

en: pushchair, pram, baby carriage, stroller, buggy
situations: A young mother walks in the park and pushes a small bed on wheels with her baby inside.
At the train station, a father lifts a baby's wheeled carriage up the stairs because the lift is broken.
The shop sells prams and cots. Which item on wheels do you use to take a baby for a walk?
The boss is on holiday, so the second manager answers the phone and signs papers for her.
A teacher is ill, and another teacher is taking the class. He is the one who is acting in her place.
A prize is given to one person, but it is accepted on behalf of the whole team. Which word describes such a role?
The bus is crowded and the driver says: 'Please shift a little to the back so more people can get on.'
You push the sofa a little to the left so there is space for the new table.
On the bench your friend slides a bit to the side to make room for you.
At university you study how the whole money system of a country works, with prices, jobs and trade, and not just one company.
The minister speaks about the situation of the economy of the whole country on the evening news.
A professor teaches how a state produces goods, pays workers and manages money as a whole.
A company spends five million euros on a new factory because it hopes to earn more in the future.
You put your savings into shares because you expect them to grow in value over the years.
A town spends money on a new bridge and says it will pay off for decades. What is such spending called?
You put your old photos and letters in a box in the cupboard so you can look at them again in ten years.
A bank offers you a locker where you can leave your jewellery safe.
A doctor says to put the medicine in a cool and dry place where children cannot reach it.
You waited a long time for the test results, and when the doctor says it is all good, you take a deep breath and smile.
The mother had feared that her child was lost, but he was found. She no longer feels worry and is glad.
After handing in your last exam, a heavy weight falls from you. How do you feel?
In the stadium there are thousands of people pushing together, all in one big group.
A scientist weighs a stone and says how heavy the stone is, measured in kilograms.
The baker mixes flour and water into a soft, thick dough, a shapeless lump.

en: by no means, not at all, in no case, in no way
situations: A friend says you must be angry, but you answer that you are not angry at all, in no way.
Someone asks if the exam was easy. You say that it was in no way simple.
The waiter asks if it bothers you to wait, and you say: 'Not at all, take your time.'
You type the password so that you can open the files on the shared computer, because you have the right to reach them.
The company allows only the managers to enter the database. Others are blocked.
The police got hold of the suspect at the airport. What is this sudden grasp called in the news?

en: to go on, to move on, to keep moving, to continue, to proceed
situations: A police officer at an accident says to the crowd: 'Please keep moving, there is nothing to see.'
After a short break on the walk, you say to your friends: 'Let's continue, we still have a long way.'
The meeting is not over yet. The boss says that it will go on after lunch.
The news says that the economy is shrinking for two quarters in a row, many factories close, and people lose jobs.
Economists worry because prices for goods rise, but sales go down for companies. The country is in a period of weak business.
A teacher explains the word for a phase when a country's production falls and unemployment rises.
After sleeping in a bad position, your neck is very stiff and you cannot turn your head.
The metal bar does not bend at all, because it is hard and unyielding.
A rabbit sees the headlights of a car and cannot move for fear. It stands completely still, as if frozen.
The driver goes faster than the allowed 50 km/h and gets a ticket.
The bill is higher than your budget, so you spend more than the limit you set.
The hiker walks past the border of the country by a few steps. What does he do to the line?
In a war film, the highest officer in a green uniform with many medals gives orders to the soldiers.

Two neighbours agree on a fair deal about who pays for the fence. They are happy with this agreement.
The school has an arrangement for the way pupils go home in the winter.

en: to glide, to slide, to slip
situations: A bird spreads its wings and floats through the air without moving them, high over the valley.
You step on wet ice, and your feet move smoothly along the surface.
A skier moves down the soft slope with no effort, and the skis slip over the snow.
In a science fiction film, a green being from another planet lands in a flying saucer and says hello to the people of Earth.
Your little brother draws a picture of a creature with big eyes from outer space who visits Earth.
Some people believe that beings from other worlds visit our planet. What do they call these beings?
Nobody knows if the football match will take place tomorrow, because of the heavy rain. It is uncertain.
The boss says that it is open to doubt whether the new machine will arrive in time.
A lawyer says that the witness is not very trustworthy, so it is hard to believe his story. Which word describes this?
For a camping trip, you take a metal tin with beans inside, because it stays fresh for years without a fridge.
The shop has shelves full of tins with soup, fish and tomatoes that can be kept for a long time.
In an emergency, people store food in jars and cans so they last for months. What is this food called?

en: to come towards, to come to
situations: A big dog is running right at you across the field, and it is coming nearer and nearer.

The postman said: 'This letter is meant for you, it belongs to you.'
The teacher gives the class homework: write two pages about 'My best holiday'.
A short text that students write at school on a given topic, with a beginning, middle and end.

en: to adjust, to adapt, to customize
situations: You buy a new jacket, and the shop assistant changes the sleeves a bit so that they fit your arms.
When moving to a new country, you must get used to the weather, food and customs to feel at home.

He says that he was ill yesterday, but you doubt it and say that he was 'ill' with a smile.
The newspaper says that the star will have a baby, but nobody has proven it.
A police officer says: 'We have no evidence at the moment, there is nothing here to show that he did it.'
The doctor looks at the paper in front of him and says that the test results have arrived and are now there.
A bank clerk says that your request is on his desk, so it exists, and it is now being checked.

A hospital needs a person with a licence from the doctor's profession to give this kind of care.

The thieves kept their loot in a secret place under the floor, which the police found after weeks.
A squirrel stores nuts in a small hole under the tree for winter. What is such a place called?

en: to shape, to form, to emboss, to coin, to mint
situations: A teacher who was very strict has influenced your life, and you still think of his words today.
The coins are made in a factory where a machine presses a picture into the metal.
The long war left its mark on the whole country. What does an event do to the way a person or country develops?
A friend wants to spend his whole salary on one game, and you say: 'Be wise and think about it.'

A person who does not eat for religious reasons, for example before Easter, does what?

In the lab, the scientist looks through a microscope at a bacterium that makes people sick.

Miners go down into a deep mine to dig for the black, hard material used to make heat and power.
For a barbecue in the garden, you light black pieces under the grill, which glow and make the meat hot.

en: to bring in, to introduce, to contribute
situations: At the team meeting, each person adds his own ideas and skills so the project becomes better.
The farmer collects the grain and takes it into the barn before the rain comes.

The team is behind by one goal, but the coach says: 'I am sure that we will win in the end.'

A friend asks: 'What have you got planned for the summer?' and you tell him about your idea to travel.

In football, the players at the back try to stop the other team from scoring.
The body's own fight against germs is strong when you are healthy and sleep well.
The country builds up its army and weapons to protect itself from enemies.
In the cold winter evenings, your grandmother sits in her chair with two needles and wool, and makes a scarf, one loop after another.
You make a warm hat by working long strings of wool into loops with two needles.
A friend learns a hobby to produce a sweater by hand with wool and needles.
Wind, sun and water are forms of energy that never run out, in contrast to oil and coal.

At school, there is a quiet room with shelves full of books where students can read and borrow.
The town opens a new building with thousands of books to lend, plus a children's corner.

en: to rise, to increase, to go up, to grow
situations: The temperature goes up in the morning from five to twenty degrees by noon.
The prices of food keep going higher each month, and people complain about it.
The road runs up to the top of the hill, and gets steeper and steeper.
After the scandal, the minister decides to leave his job and announces it on TV.
The coach of the football team says that he is giving up his position after the loss.
You cancel the contract with the gym within the time allowed. What is this step back from a contract or office called?
A child asks: 'Why do you eat so much?' and you answer: 'Because I am hungry, that is the reason.'
You missed the bus, and so you were late, and you tell this to your boss. Which small word means 'for that reason'?
You ask for a book and your friend says: 'That's why I came, to talk about it.'
In the story, the hero is about to lose, but then a sudden change happens, and everything goes in a different direction.
The year 1989 brought a big change in the politics of East Germany. People talk about the moment when things changed.
The runners go around the end of the pool, make a quick turn and swim back.
Your neighbour's husband died five years ago, and she now lives alone in the house.
On the form, there are boxes for single, married, divorced and one for people whose partner has died.
The old man whose wife passed away lives with his daughter now. What is his family status?

en: to assess, to judge, to evaluate
situations: The teacher reads the essays and gives each one a mark, after thinking carefully about its quality.
A doctor looks at the x-ray to say how serious the injury is.
A jury at a talent show watches each singer and then gives a view on how good the performance was.
The sky turns dark, there is lightning and loud thunder, and heavy rain makes the streets flood.
The weather service sends a warning to your phone about strong wind and hail tonight.
The campers run into the car because of the strong rain and wind. What was the weather like?
The newspaper page is divided into vertical strips of text, and you read the first strip from top to bottom.
After the earthquake, a long narrow opening appears in the ground near the road.
In a spreadsheet, there are rows and vertical lines of cells, labelled A, B, C. What is one of those vertical lines called?
The football team wins the last match and gets a place in the World Cup. It has earned the right to play.
After the training, a worker gets the skills and papers that make him fit for a better job.
The runner is fast enough in the first race to go through to the final.
The boy's toy is broken by his brother, and his face turns red, he shouts and stamps his feet.
The customer waits for an hour, and he is so angry that he shouts at the staff.
A driver is cut off in traffic and feels a hot, strong emotion. What is this feeling called?
In the country, all citizens can vote and choose their own government in free elections.
The club decides things by letting each member raise a hand, and the majority wins.
A teacher says that in this kind of state people are free to say what they think. Which word describes it?
Your car uses about six litres of petrol for every hundred kilometres. What is the word for how much fuel a car uses?
The electricity bill is high this month because your family used a lot of power with the heating and the dryer.
A shop owner tells you that the amount of milk that people drink every week has gone down.

en: to stick together, to keep together, to hold together, to bind
situations: In a hard time, the whole family stays together and helps each other, and nobody leaves.
You glue two pieces of wood so that they stay joined and do not come apart.
A strong rope keeps the bundle of sticks tied together so they do not fall apart.
The runner crosses the line first, and at the ceremony someone puts a round gold disc on a ribbon around his neck.
At the Olympics, the winners get gold, silver or bronze, and they hold up the round prize on a ribbon.
Your grandfather shows you a small round piece of metal on a ribbon that he won for bravery in his youth.
The recipe says that flour is one of the main things that goes into the bread.
A mechanic says that the engine is made of many small pieces, and each one is a necessary piece of the car.
The label says what the juice contains: water, apples and sugar. Each thing in the list is one what?

en: easy-care, easy to maintain, low-maintenance, easy to get along with
situations: Your friend buys a plant that needs almost no water and no special care, so it stays alive even if you forget it.
The shirt does not need ironing and you can wash it at home in the machine without any problem.
A cat is easier to keep than a dog, because it needs less attention. Which word describes such a pet or plant?
The bank officially lets you have a loan of ten thousand euros after checking your papers.
The king allows the prisoner his freedom and gives him a wish.
The school gives a student extra time in the exam because he has a problem with his eyes.
At the restaurant, you order a steak, and it comes with potatoes or rice on the same plate as an addition.
The waiter asks which extra you want with your fish: salad, vegetables or chips.
In the magazine, there is a small separate booklet with TV programmes, which you get at no extra cost.
After cooking, there are crumbs on the kitchen floor, so you take a tool with a long handle and stiff bristles to sweep.
In a fairy tale, the witch flies through the night on a long stick with straw at the end.
You clean the leaves from the yard with a long-handled tool that has bristles. What is this tool?
After the old director retires, a young woman takes over his position as the new head of the company.
The little ducks walk behind their mother in a line and go where she goes.
A prince takes the throne after his father. What does he do in relation to the king?
Your grandfather does not like new ideas and wants to keep the old ways for dress, music and family life.
A newspaper says that the party wants to keep traditions and change things only slowly.
The bank manager always wears the same dark suit and dislikes modern changes. What kind of person is he?
In your history lesson, you learn about the Romans who ruled over many lands in a huge state from one city.
In fairy tales, the king rules his land, which is called his ...? A big area under one ruler.
An old map shows a vast territory ruled by one emperor with many conquered countries.
You like all fruit, but you love strawberries most of all. You say: 'I like fruit, and strawberries above all.'
The teacher says that all students should read the book, and above all those who missed the last class.
A doctor says to avoid sugar, and in particular sweet drinks.
Your grandfather can still recall the names of all his school friends, because he has a very good ability to keep things in his head.
After the accident, the man lost his ability to remember things from before, and the doctors say it will take time.
At school, you train your mind with learning lists. A good one is helpful for exams. What is it?
You order a book online and the shop promises to post it to your home address.
The office says it will mail you the form within two days if you give your address.
After your request, the company will deliver a catalogue to your mailbox.
A man says first that he was at home all evening, and later that he went to the cinema. The two statements cannot both be true.
The boss says: 'I want the work done today.' The employee replies: 'No, I disagree, that is not possible.'
A lawyer points out that two parts of the contract say the opposite of each other.
The instructions are written so badly that you cannot understand what to do.
The photo is blurry and you cannot see the faces, so it is hard to say who is in it.
It is not certain who will win the election because the numbers are so close. Which word describes the situation?
The recipe says: 'Add three of the large spoons of sugar to the dough.' Which spoon is it, bigger than the one for tea?
At the dinner table, you use a big spoon to eat your soup.

en: to put on, to gain, to grow, to get oneself sth
situations: After a winter of eating too many sweets, you notice that your trousers are tight, and you have gained some weight.

Your friend plans to buy himself a new phone, as the old one is broken.
At the weekend, a group of cyclists compete over fifty kilometres to see who finishes first.
In the schoolyard, you and a friend start to see who can get to the tree first.

en: to appoint, to invoke, to refer to
situations: The president officially picks a famous scientist to become the new head of the national health office.

en: to ask, to question, to consult
situations: A reporter stands on the street and puts questions to passers-by about the new law.

situations: The dinosaurs lived millions of years ago, but today none of them are left on Earth.
