The news says that a storm warning has been given for the whole of the continent. Which word describes something that covers all of Europe?
On the lake in the park, a big white bird with a long curved neck glides slowly over the water.
In the fairy tale, the ugly duckling becomes a beautiful white bird with a long neck.
The children feed bread to a large white water bird, which hisses when it is annoyed.
At breakfast, you drink tea, but this morning you had coffee. You say what you drink in most cases.
The bus comes at eight o'clock in the morning on most days, but today it is late.
The shop opens at nine, as a rule. Which word means 'in the normal case'?
You are a member of the town football club and have been for ten years.
The island is part of the country that lies next to it, and its people have the same passport.
Your friend is in a band with four other people. He is one of the group. What is the word for being a part of a group?
You travel south to a big German state where people wear leather trousers at a big beer festival, and Munich is the capital.
The football club in Munich plays in red and is known all over Germany. Which state is it located in?
A friend tells you that the Alps, castles and beer gardens are all part of this German state. Which state?
The police say that three men were part of the robbery, and they are looking for all of them.
All the people in the project, from designers to workers, were part of its success.
A student takes part in the group discussion and gives his opinion. How would you describe him?
The president speaks to all the citizens of the country on TV and says: 'I speak to all of you.'
In the old story, the king asks the ordinary citizens what they think, not the nobles.
A teacher talks about a group of people who share one language, culture and land.

en: to show, to point out, to demonstrate
situations: The report makes clear the problems in the old system, with numbers and examples.
The guide shows the tourists the weak parts in the wall with his finger.
A researcher presents clear proof of how fast the ice is melting. What does he do with the facts?
You click on a link, and a game from the internet is copied onto your computer.
The teacher sends you a file, and you save it to your laptop from the web.
The app shows a bar that fills up while a film is moved from the server to your phone.
The architect shows the client a first drawing of the new house, which can still be changed.
A student writes a first rough version of the letter and shows it to his teacher before writing the final one.
A fashion designer makes a rough picture of a new dress. What do we call this early plan?
At the restaurant, the waiter brings the soup to your table and puts it in front of you.
At a dinner party, the host brings the dishes to the guests on big plates.
A tennis player starts the point by hitting the ball over the net from behind the line.
The old man woke up in a strange place and could not understand where he was or what was going on.
The tourist looks around at the busy station with many signs and has no idea which way to go.
After so many different instructions, the child does not understand any of them. How does he feel?
In the news, police officers take a man to the police car after the robbery, and put handcuffs on him.
A reporter says that the bank robber was caught at the airport last night.
On a crime show, the detective says: 'You are under ...' at the end. What is the word for the act of catching a suspect?
The teacher gives the students a one-page paper that shows the main parts of the whole course.
From the top of the tower, you see the entire city in one look and understand how it is laid out.
The manager asks for a short list of all the projects, so that he can see how they stand.

en: to load, to burden, to charge
situations: The heavy bag on your back puts a lot of weight on your shoulders.
The long court case is weighing on the family, and the stress makes them tired.
The new rules put a large strain on small firms. What do they do to them?
Because of the virus, people stand two metres from each other in the queue at the shop.
On the motorway, the driver keeps a safe gap behind the car in front of him.
The teacher puts the chairs a little apart so that the students cannot copy.
A friend shows you a knife with many tools, chocolate with cows on the wrapper and a watch from a country in the Alps.
The skier on the podium comes from Zurich, and he holds a red flag with a white cross.
Your colleague from Geneva speaks French and German and has a passport from the country with a white cross on its flag.
An old woman gets a call from a man who pretends to be from the bank and takes her money. This is a crime of deceiving people.
The police warn about a false website that sells goods but never sends anything.
A man cheats an insurance company by saying that his car was stolen when it was not. What is this crime called?
The lawyer shows with a video that the witness's story is wrong, and so he proves it is false.
A scientist shows with new tests that the old theory cannot be true.
You say that your friend is wrong about the date, and you prove it with the calendar. What do you do with his claim?
After the war, many families had no food, no home and no money, and they suffered terribly.
A neighbour is in great trouble, because he has lost his job and has no way to pay for his flat.
In an old saying, a friend in trouble is a friend indeed. What is the word for this kind of hard time and hardship?
A man comes to your house for tea in the afternoon and stays for an hour. You are the host, and he is your ...?
The museum counted 5,000 people who came in during the weekend.
At the hospital, a woman arrives with flowers to see her friend. What is she called?
The teacher gives you a problem with numbers, signs and formulas that you must solve using logic.
A scientist uses a model with equations to describe how the planets move.
Your friend has a gift for numbers and is good at the subject with algebra and geometry. Which word describes this gift?

en: to suggest, to indicate, to imply, to hint
situations: Your boss does not say it openly, but he gives small signs that a new job is coming, and you understand.
The weather report says that clouds in the west are giving a first sign of rain.
Your friend says: 'I might be a bit late,' which is a quiet way of telling you without saying it fully.
You ask your sister: 'What are you looking for in that drawer?' which asks about the thing she is searching for.
The law says: 'According to which rule must we act?' A teacher asks about the source of the rule.
A friend says that he is not sure what you are asking about, and you repeat: 'What did you ask for?' Which question word starts it?
To remember the order of the planets, you learn a silly sentence where each word starts with the same letter as one planet.
The teacher gives you a little rhyme to help you remember a hard rule, a trick for your memory.
A student invents a funny phrase to recall a long list of words. What is such a helper for memory called?
The evening before the opening night, the actors play the whole show in costumes, as if the audience were there.
The orchestra plays the whole concert once more on the day before, to check that everything works.
At the school, the children perform the entire play on the final practice day. What is that practice called?
The cat sees the dog and looks away to the other side, so it does not have to face him.
The government spends money to stop a big crisis from happening.
Angry at his friend, he moved his face away from him and said nothing.
The river flows all the time, without stopping, day and night.
The company has grown steadily for ten years without a break.
The teacher says to practise a little every day, without gaps. Which word describes this?
Everyone calls the tall boy 'Giant' at school, though his real name is Max.
Your friend has a funny short name that his teammates gave him, which is different from the one on his passport.
A famous footballer is known by a short, friendly name rather than his real name. What is such a name called?

en: to run away, to take off, to cut off, to chop off, to leave
situations: When the teacher comes in, the boys quickly run off and leave the room.
The thief heard the alarm and took off through the window before anyone could stop him.
The woodcutter swings the axe and cuts the branch from the tree with one hard blow.
The seasons go round and round: spring, summer, autumn, winter, and then spring again. This is a repeating ...?
A washing machine runs through a set of steps, from washing to drying, and then it stops.
The moon changes shape in a regular order over a month. What do we call such a repeating process?
The police say that the thief has a special sign, a scar on the left cheek, that makes him easy to identify.
A biology teacher shows what makes a bird different from other animals: it has feathers and a beak.
A good phone has several properties, such as a bright screen and long battery life. What is each one?
The new bridge is made of steel and does not shake at all, even when heavy trucks pass over it.
The doctor says that the patient is in a steady condition and no longer in danger.
A table with thick legs does not wobble. How would you describe it?
A student who goes to extra classes gets a lot of use from them and gains good marks.
When the shop lowers its prices, customers gain by paying less.
The company earns a lot from the growth of the online market. What does it do?
You want to open a bottle of wine, but the top is a piece of tree bark, so you need a tool with a screw shape.
At the picnic, nobody can open the wine because the tool is missing at home.
The waiter pulls the cork from the bottle with a small tool with a metal spiral. What is the tool?

en: disturbance, breach of the peace, disorderly conduct
situations: At two in the morning, the neighbour plays loud music, and so you call the police, who tell him to stop.
The landlord warns the tenants about making a lot of noise after ten in the evening, as it breaks the peace of the house.
The police write a report about a party where the guests shouted until dawn.

en: to concern, to go on, to tackle
situations: Your boss says: 'This is none of your business,' meaning it does not concern you.
The team decides to start work on the difficult task and deal with it step by step.
The street lights come on at dusk, and the show starts at eight.
In your history class, you learn about the two big wars of the twentieth century that involved most countries on Earth.
Your grandfather's father fought in the war that lasted from 1914 to 1918.
A museum shows photographs of the war that ended in 1945. What kind of war was it?
You hold a pen in your hand, but you write with the other side, the one next to your heart.
The driver says: 'Please turn at the next corner towards the side opposite to right.'
In the picture, the boy on the side opposite to the right wears a red cap. Which side is he on?
A young painter goes to a special school for the arts and learns to draw and paint.
Famous scientists meet at a society that is old and respected and gives out prizes.
The police train their officers at a special school for many months. What is such a school called?
Before Christmas, the family puts lights, balls and stars on the tree to make it look beautiful.
For the wedding, they put flowers and ribbons around the hall.
Children make the classroom prettier with paper chains and drawings. What do they do to it?
On a trip to the north of Europe, you visit countries like Sweden, Norway and Denmark, with cold winters and fjords.
The furniture shop is famous for simple design from this region in the far north.
A friend says: 'In this part of Europe, they have long winter nights and the northern lights.' Which region?
You point at the chair and say to the child: 'Come to this place.'
The waiter asks where you want to sit, and you point to the table by the window: 'Put the bag to this spot.'
Your friend is standing far away, and you wave your hand and ask him to move to where you are. Which word means 'to this place'?
The elephant was so big that it filled the whole truck. It was extremely large.
The singer earns a huge amount of money for each concert. This is more than normal.
The pressure on the students before the final exam is extremely high. Which word means 'very, very big'?
A married man secretly meets a woman he loves, but she is not his wife. What do we call her?
In the old novel, the king has a secret woman he loves, apart from the queen.
In the song, a man sings about the woman he loves and misses. How is she called in this sense?
You give your neighbour the key to your flat, because you trust him to water the plants while you are away.
A girl tells her best friend a secret that she has told nobody else.
The parents leave their baby in the care of the grandmother for the evening, trusting her fully.
The train goes across a large flat land with no hills for hours, and you see only fields.
In a tall building, the garage is on a lower floor than the shops.
In a discussion, the speaker talks about a different level, the political one, rather than the personal one.
In Germany, the most important set of rules for the whole state, written in 1949, protects the dignity of every person.
A lawyer says that a new law must agree with the country's founding document, or it is invalid.
At school, the class reads the first article, which says that human dignity cannot be touched. Which document is it?
After your uncle died, you get his old car because he wrote your name in his will.
The daughter receives her mother's jewellery after she passes away.
A child has his father's blue eyes. In the family, many things come from the older generation.
After the storm, the street was a real river, you could say. It was truly flooded.
His answer was a real insult, nothing less.
The party turned into a total mess, a real chaos, and you say it with one word.
In some parts of the world, families live without enough food, clean water or a place to sleep. Which word describes this situation?
A charity says that it wants to fight a problem in which millions of people have very little money.
A man grew up with very little money and never had new clothes. What was his situation in life?
A student goes to live with a family in France for a year, while a French student comes to Germany.
The shop lets you bring back a shirt that is too small and take a bigger one in its place.
Two friends share ideas about the book and talk about it for hours. What is the word for giving and receiving?

en: to invest, to create, to apply, to dock
situations: The ship comes to the harbour in the evening and ties up at the wall.
A woman puts her savings into a fund, hoping that her money will grow.
The gardener makes a new flowerbed in the garden, with paths and a small pond.
At night, you look up at the sky and think about all the stars, galaxies and planets, everything that exists in space.
A scientist tries to learn how everything in space started, from the big bang until now.
A child asks what is bigger than the Earth, the sun and all the stars. What is the biggest thing of all?
The paint on the outside wall of the house is old and needs to be done again.
The doctor looks at the skin on the outside of your arm to see if there is a wound.
On the box, the label is on the surface, not on the inside. Which word describes the side you can see?
A person who uses the new app on his phone every day is one of these.
A computer asks for a name and a password, which belong to the person who uses it.
The company tests how easy the website is for people who use it every day. Whom do they ask?
In the shop, you go into a small room with a mirror and put on a pair of trousers to see if they fit.
Before buying shoes, you walk a few steps in them to see if they are comfortable.
The tailor asks you to put on the jacket so he can check its size on you.
In the maths lesson, the teacher writes 2x + 3 = 11 on the board and asks you to find x.
A student solves a problem that has an equals sign with a different value on each side.
The physics teacher shows a formula with letters and numbers on both sides of an equals sign. What is it?
The teacher says: 'Thank you for all the work you put in, even though the result was not perfect.'
After many hours of hard work, the team tried everything to finish on time.
The boss says that she saw how much you tried to solve the problem. Which word describes this?

en: to slip so's mind, to be dropped, to be omitted
situations: You wanted to say something at the meeting, but suddenly the name went out of your head.
Because of the new rule, the extra fee is cancelled and no longer applies.
On the list, the item about the garage was left out, so it is no longer there.
The baby has very soft skin that gets red easily from a new cream.
Your friend gets upset very quickly when somebody says something about his work.
The glass is thin and can break at the smallest touch. Which word describes something that must be handled with care?

en: rescue service, ambulance service, emergency service
situations: After a car accident, a vehicle with a blue light and a siren arrives and takes the injured person to hospital.
When you call 112, a team of medical helpers comes to your home within minutes.
A paramedic works for the organisation that gives first help and drives people to hospital in an emergency.

en: mostly, usually, for the most part
situations: On Sundays, you sleep late, but now and then you get up early. You say what you do in most cases.
The visitors to the museum are mostly students, and only a few are older.
The weather in the town is for the most part sunny in the summer. Which word means 'most of the time'?
After coming home from the trip, you tell your mother in detail how the town looked, what you ate and who you met.
The witness gives the police a clear account of the man's face and his clothes.
The writer paints a picture with words so that the reader can almost see the village. What does he do?
You wait at the bus stop for a short time, and then the bus arrives.
Your mother says: 'Sit down and rest for a little time, then we can eat.'
The old man thinks about the question for a period and then answers slowly.
The girl walks onto the stage with her head up and speaks clearly, with no fear of the audience.
The new manager believes in his own skills and says what he thinks without any doubt.
A student answers every question with a firm voice and a smile. Which word describes her?
The bus leaves every fifteen minutes, so there are fifteen minutes between two buses.
The doctor says to take the medicine at regular times, every six hours.
In music, the distance between two notes is described by a number, for example a third.

en: to be responsible, to be liable, to adhere, to stick
situations: The parents have to pay for the damage that their child caused to the neighbour's window, because by law they are responsible.
Company directors can be held legally responsible if the firm breaks the law.
The sticker is on the wall and does not come off. What does the glue do?
The pedestrian crossing is on the road near the school, where children walk to the other side.
The change from childhood to adult life can be difficult for young people.
At the border, you drive through a place where you can go from one country into another. What is that place?
The teacher says that the topic has many sides, and the economic side is only one of them.
When buying a car, safety is an important point for a family, besides the price.
The discussion looked at the problem from different angles. What is each of these points of view?
A dancer moves so softly and easily that every step flows like water. How would you describe her movements?
You rub cream into dry hands and now your skin feels soft and smooth to the touch.
A cat slips along the wall with quiet, flowing, easy movements. Nothing about its body looks stiff.

en: to put down, to lay down, to lie down
situations: You feel very tired after lunch, so you go to the sofa and stretch out flat to rest.
Your bag is heavy, so you place it gently on the floor and leave it there.
A mother tells her sleepy child to go to bed and rest flat for a while. Which verb means 'to lie down'?
A manager says a colleague is perfect for the job because she has all the skills and knowledge needed.
You ask who decides about the budget. Your boss says only the finance team has the official power to decide, not you.
In a job test, the company checks whether you can really do the tasks well and properly. Which noun means 'competence'?
A website lists train times and adds: 'We cannot give any firm assurance that this information is correct.' Which noun means such an assurance?
A shop owner says: 'I stand behind this phone. If it breaks, I will fix it.' He is giving you a promise about the product.
The newspaper prints lottery numbers with a note that the paper does not promise they are right. What is the missing promise called?

en: to pass, to go by, to elapse
situations: You are having so much fun with friends that you look at the clock and three hours have already gone by.
You wait in a boring queue and it feels like the minutes never move on and time seems to stand still.
A grandmother says the years go by so fast that soon another summer will be gone. Which verb fits?
You hear a strange noise in the dark house at night and your heart beats fast because you are afraid.
A small child will not walk past big dogs because of a deep dread. What is this strong feeling called?
In a story, the sailors felt great terror when a huge storm hit the ship. Which noun means this feeling?
A salesman promises that this cheap cream will make you look ten years younger. You doubt it and raise an eyebrow.
Your friend says he will become rich by next month. You do not believe him easily and ask for proof.
A scientist reads a surprising result and says she is not convinced yet. Which adjective means 'doubtful, not easily believing'?
At a job interview you say you are happy to work on weekends if needed. This shows how willing you are to help.
The firefighters at the station stay on standby all night, ready to leave at any moment.
A charity asks how willing you are to give money. Which noun means 'willingness'?

en: to acquire, to purchase, to buy
situations: A big company pays money to take ownership of a small chain of shops.
Through years of practice you slowly gain a new skill, like speaking another language.
A sign at a museum says tickets can be obtained at the desk, in formal wording. Which verb means 'to buy'?
After carrying boxes up four floors, you are out of breath and sweating. That took a lot of physical work.
Your teacher says good grades come only when you really try hard every day.
A marathon runner says the last kilometre took every bit of strength he had. Which noun means such hard effort?

en: Interior Minister, Minister of the Interior
situations: On the TV news, the government member in charge of police and domestic security speaks about new rules for the police.
In a quiz you must name the cabinet member, a man, who leads the ministry for police, borders and internal security.
A headline says the man responsible for the country's police and internal affairs will visit a new police station today.
A football player falls on the pitch, holds his ankle and cannot continue playing.
You fell off your bike and your knee is bleeding. How is your knee?
The news reports a bus accident: five passengers needed a doctor, but nobody died. Which adjective describes these passengers?

en: to announce, to declare, to proclaim
situations: At the end of the talent show, the host opens the envelope and tells everyone loudly who won.
The school director stands before all students and officially tells them the school will close early on Friday.
A king in a fairy tale reads out his decision from the balcony so that all the people can hear. Which verb means 'to proclaim'?

en: on it, at it, in it
situations: You point to a cup with a crack and say: 'Careful, a small piece of glass is stuck on it.' Which small word means 'on it'?
Your colleague asks if you are still working on the report. You say yes, you are busy at it right now. Which small word means 'at it'?
You open a drawer and say there is an old key in it. Which small word can mean 'in it'?
A report studies how the new road toll changes daily life for the people living nearby.
A doctor explains that eating too much sugar has long-term results for your health.
A company asks what the storm did to its deliveries. Which noun means 'impact'?
At university your cousin studies how to write programs and build algorithms.
At school, your favourite lesson is the one where you learn to write programs for computers.
A degree in this subject covers data, programming and computer systems. Which word means 'computer science'?
You pull a piece of paper hard with both hands and it splits in two.
You catch your trousers on a nail and the cloth opens with a loud sound.
A very old rope is pulled hard and suddenly it breaks apart. Which verb means 'to tear'?
It is November. You talk about the same month one year earlier and call it the one before this.
You talk about the week that just ended, not this one, and say you were ill during it.
A teacher says: 'Open your books at the page we used in the lesson before this one.' Which adjective means 'previous'?
Football fans think of a huge South American country with Rio de Janeiro, the Amazon rainforest and Portuguese as its language.
A geography quiz asks for the largest country in South America, whose capital is Brasília.
A coffee package says the beans come from the biggest country in South America, famous for carnival and samba.
You get on the bus and the driver asks you to show proof that you paid for your ride.
A controller walks through the tram and asks everyone to show the small paper they bought at the machine.
At the station machine you press a button to buy a paper for one journey on the metro. What do you get?
Your doctor writes a note so that the pharmacy gives you antibiotic tablets.
You have a bad cough. The doctor says you need strong medicine and writes it down officially for the chemist.
Which verb means that a doctor officially writes out a medicine for a patient?
A glass falls on the kitchen floor and breaks. You carefully pick up one sharp piece.
Archaeologists dig up a small broken piece of an old clay pot.
A mother warns her child: 'Careful, there is a sharp piece of broken glass on the pavement.' Which noun means that piece?
An engineer checks the building and finds problems in the way the walls and beams hold it up.
A news report says the company's money problems are not temporary but come from the basic way the firm is organised.
A report talks about changes that affect the whole basic frame of a system. Which adjective means 'structural'?
The weather app shows 80 percent for rain tomorrow. What does that number tell you?
In maths class you roll a die and work out how likely it is to get a six.
Your friend asks how likely it is that you will come to the party. You say it is high. Which noun means 'likelihood'?
A fisherman cleans a freshly caught fish by taking out its insides before cooking.
A new law applies to all companies, but small family shops are left out of the rule.
At the market the seller prepares a chicken for you by removing everything from inside. Which verb fits?
You look at a Chinese text and cannot read the single written symbols.
Your computer shows a strange sign instead of the letter you typed. Which noun means one written sign like a letter or symbol?
A teacher in Japanese class says each one of these small written signs has its own meaning.

en: to take off, to remove, to detach, to come off, to peel off
situations: You put a plaster on your arm. Now it is time to peel it carefully off your skin.
A sticker on the old fridge comes loose after years and slowly separates from the surface.
You soak a stamp in water so that it comes off the envelope. Which verb fits?
You say there is a nice bakery, a park and a school all close by, in the area around your home.
A newcomer asks if the people right next to where you live are friendly. You say yes, they are very nice.
A flat advert says: 'quiet area with shops in the vicinity'. Which noun means 'neighbourhood'?
A friend's flat has warm lights, soft cushions and plants. You feel at home immediately.
An empty office with grey walls gets rugs, lamps and a sofa to make it feel nice to live in.
Which adjective means 'cosy' for a room?
Your grandmother's mother is 96 years old and tells you stories about the old days.
At a family photo, four generations stand together. The oldest woman is your mother's grandmother.
At a birthday party someone says: 'She is the mother of my grandmother.' Which word names her?

en: to proceed somewhere, to come to pass
situations: An announcer at the airport politely asks passengers to make their way to gate 12 in a formal way.
An old storybook begins: 'It happened that one evening...' Which formal verb means 'to come to pass'?
A doctor asks a patient in formal words to go over to room 5 for the X-ray. Which verb fits?
Your friend has no partner and says she enjoys living alone and dating around.
On a dating app you see a profile of a man who is not in a relationship.
At a party the host asks who is here without a partner. Which word names a man without a partner?
You walked in a circle on all sides of the lake. Which small word means 'around'?
A child runs here and there and says he was just playing around the house. Which small word means 'around'?
You ask if there is a bank somewhere around here, meaning in this area. Which small word means 'around'?
A pharmacist says the tablets can make you sleepy, a small unwanted result besides helping your headache.
On the paper inside a medicine box there is a long list of unwanted reactions your body might have.
After a vaccine your arm hurts a little. The doctor says this is a normal one. Which noun means 'side effect'?
A fox walks up to a girl and eats from her hand without fear. It is used to people.
In the zoo the children may pet the sheep because they are not wild at all.
Which adjective describes an animal that was once wild but is now used to people and not dangerous?

en: to go through, to pass through
situations: A road is blocked ahead, but people on foot may walk through the gate.
You go through the narrow passage between two buildings to get to the other street.
The night train from Berlin to Vienna goes all the way through without a change. Which verb means 'to go through'?
Early in the morning, a thin line of light from the sun comes through the curtain.
A water pipe breaks and a thin, strong line of water shoots out.
A doctor shines a thin beam from a small torch into your eye. Which noun fits?
A tropical yellow fruit with a spiky green crown on top, often cut into rings.
Some people argue about whether this sweet fruit belongs on a pizza with ham.
At the market you buy a big fruit with rough skin and sweet, sour yellow flesh. It comes from the tropics. Which fruit is it?
At the airport you give your suitcase and passport to the person at the desk and get your boarding pass.
You arrive at a hotel, show your booking at reception and receive a room key.
Which verb means to register your arrival at a hotel or airport?
In a restaurant you order kebab and strong tea. The waiter speaks the language of Istanbul and Ankara.
A friend's grandmother comes from Istanbul and speaks the language of her country.
Which adjective means 'from Turkey', like in 'coffee from Turkey'?
A ruler has many tiny lines. The distance between two of them is the smallest unit you can read.
A weather report says it rained 3 of these small units. It is one thousandth of a metre.
A carpenter says the board must be cut exact to the nearest thousandth of a metre. Which unit is that?
At a carnival party, children wear a cover over their face with holes for the eyes.
In the hospital, the nurse puts a cloth over her nose and mouth before the operation.
A face-care shop sells a green cream you put on your face for twenty minutes. Which word means 'mask'?
You want to hang a shelf, so you make a hole in the wall with an electric tool.
The dentist uses a small, loud tool to clean out a bad tooth.
Oil workers make a deep hole into the ground. Which verb fits?
A baby falls on the floor and lands on the soft part of the body you sit on.
A mum puts a clean nappy on the part of the baby's body between legs and back.
After hours on a hard chair, the part of the body you sit on hurts. Which informal word names it?
A ticket costs 10 euros, or less with a student card. What is the usual price without a discount called?
A shop says: 'Our usual opening hours are 9 to 6, except on holidays.' Which adjective fits?
A doctor says your blood pressure is in the usual, expected range. Which adjective means 'regular'?
Your teacher says she cannot read your notes because the way you write with a pen is so messy.
You know a letter is from your grandfather by the shape of the letters he wrote with his own hand.
A museum shows the old pages, written by hand, of a famous poet's book before it was printed.
After a long working week, you lie in a warm bath with music and let your muscles go soft.
A yoga teacher tells you to breathe slowly and let your shoulders drop.
On holiday you say: 'I just want to do nothing by the pool.' Which verb means 'to relax'?

The news says the situation is calm at present, but may change.
Your friend asks where you work, and you say, 'At the moment, I work in a shop.' Which word means 'currently'?
The old man lives alone and has no visitors; no one comes by for weeks.
In a big city, a student is surrounded by people but feels that nobody knows him.
A woman lives on a distant island and sees no one for months. Which word means 'loneliness'?
In biology class, you learn that your eye colour comes from small parts of your DNA given by your parents.
A scientist tells you the tiny unit of heredity in the cell decides if you are tall.
A disease runs in your family because of a change in one piece of DNA. Which word means 'gene'?
The manager organises the work of several teams so everything fits together at the same time.
Before the party, you plan with your friends who brings what, so nothing is missing.
During the rescue, one person leads the work between the police, the doctors and the firefighters. Which word means 'to coordinate'?
In the city square, a grey bird walks among the people and picks up bread crumbs.
In the story, a white bird with an olive branch is the symbol of peace.
Some people keep these birds in a box and send them home with letters. Which word means 'dove' or 'pigeon'?
The teacher answers calmly, with facts only and no anger, even when the student is rude.
In the meeting, the manager gives a calm report with only the facts, without any feelings.
Your colleague keeps discussions on the topic and never gets personal. Which word means 'objective' or 'factual'?
In horoscopes, one sign is shown as a woman holding a plant and is for people born in late August.
In an old story, a young woman lives in a tower and has never been with a man.
In the zodiac, the sign after Leo is shown as a woman. Which word means 'virgin' or 'Virgo'?

en: to line up, to queue, to be pending, to be due
situations: At the post office on Monday, you stand in a long row of people and wait for your turn.
In the office, a list of tasks is waiting; many decisions are still due.
At the cinema, people stand one behind the other to buy tickets. Which word means 'to queue' or 'to line up'?
Your neighbours start a group on their own to plant trees on the street.
Your boss says she likes you because you do things by yourself without being asked.
A citizens' group collects signatures for a new bike lane. Which word means 'initiative'?
After many weeks without rain, the farmer's fields turn brown and cracked.
In winter, the heating makes the air so lacking in moisture that your skin feels tight.
The news reports that rivers are low because it has not rained all summer. Which word means 'dryness' or 'drought'?
The old man gives good advice, because he has seen a lot and understands life deeply.
In the fairy tale, the king asks a very clever old woman for advice about what to do.
Your grandmother always knows the right thing to say because she has great wisdom. Which word means 'wise'?
Your mother says, 'Come here and watch this photo,' so you turn your eyes to it.
At the museum, you stop for a minute to view each painting.
Your friend asks you to examine his new shoes. Which everyday word means 'to look at'?
In your grandmother's garden, there are plants like parsley and basil, used in cooking.
In a southern German restaurant, the sausages are served with fermented, sour cut leaves.
You put some green plants into the soup for flavour. Which word means 'herb' or 'cabbage'?
An artist paints your face on a canvas, and you sit still for hours.
In the museum, a big picture shows the head and shoulders of a king.
A photographer takes a close-up photo of your face for a magazine. Which word means 'portrait'?

en: to publish, to put on, to hang up
situations: At the end of the phone call, you say goodbye and press the button so the line is ended.
A DJ puts a new record on the turntable at the party.
The publishing company decides to print a new edition of the book. Which word means 'to put on' or 'to hang up'?
A man you have never met rings your door bell, and you do not know who he is.
The police find a phone number that no one recognises.
An artist whose work nobody has heard of exhibits in a small gallery. Which word means 'unknown'?
In the history book, a government that rules without freedom for the people falls after thirty years.
The news reports on the leaders who control the country by force.
A strict government with one leader and no free elections is called what? Which word means 'regime'?
In spring, small purple flowers grow in the garden under the trees.
After a fight at school, the boy has a dark mark around his eye.
A sweet violet scent comes from a tiny flower on your table. Which word means 'violet' (flower) or 'black eye'?

en: to generate, to earn, to make
situations: At the end of the year, the company has earned a profit of two million euros through its business.
The farm produces enough income from selling milk and eggs to pay all its workers.
A club wants to make more money from its shop than last year. Which word means 'to generate' or 'to earn' (by business)?
The waiter says, 'It costs only five euros, nothing more.'
You tell your boss you were absent for just one day, not more.
A report says that the difference was merely small and not important. Which word means 'merely' or 'only'?
Your cat is ill and does not eat, so you take her to the doctor for animals.
A man in a white coat gives your dog an injection and checks his ears.
A cow on the farm is sick, and the farmer calls this male professional. Which word means 'vet'?
The small radio runs on batteries, and you can carry it around easily.
A big increase in rent is not something that most families can accept or afford.
The new laptop is light and can be taken anywhere. Which word means 'portable' or 'wearable'?
A detective asks why the man did it, searching for the reason behind the crime.
A painter chooses a picture of a mountain as the subject of his work.
A pattern with flowers is repeated on the wallpaper. Which word means 'motive' or 'motif'?
At the museum, a sign says you must not put your hands on the art.
A mother tells her child to keep his fingers off the hot stove and not to touch it.
In the shop, you pick up a shirt to feel the fabric with your hand. Which word means 'to touch'?
An astronaut looks out of the spaceship window and sees only stars, the Moon and darkness far above the Earth.
In a science film, a rocket leaves the sky and enters the empty area beyond the Earth's air.
Telescopes help us look at planets and galaxies far beyond our planet. Which word means 'outer space'?
In the zoo, the lion eats meat and the guide says it hunts other animals in the wild.
In a nature film, a wolf follows a deer and catches it for food.
Tigers, lions and bears hunt other animals to survive. Which word means 'predator'?

en: to roll, to roll out, to coast
situations: Before baking the cake, you flatten the dough with a long wooden tool until it is thin.
The red carpet is unfolded and spread along the floor before the guests arrive.
The bus turns off its engine and slowly moves forward until it stops. Which word means 'to roll out' or 'to coast'?
Tomorrow you will fly for the first time, and you cannot sleep because your heart beats fast.
Before the exam, your hands shake and you cannot sit still.
The children jump around the room the night before the holiday trip. Which word means 'excited' or 'nervous'?
The teacher says the text is well organised: an introduction, a middle and an ending.
Workers put the stage together for the concert in the afternoon.
After the war, people started to build up the city again from nothing. Which word means 'structure' or 'construction'?
Your landlord says dogs are not nice, but he lets you keep yours and does not complain.
The teacher does not accept rude jokes in class and will not put up with them.
The country allows some visitors to stay without papers, but without approving it. Which word means 'to tolerate'?
A man gets up at five in the morning to milk his cows and drive the tractor to the field.
At the village market, a man sells potatoes and eggs from his own land.
A person who grows crops and keeps animals on a farm is called what? Which male word means 'farmer'?
After the player was caught cheating, the whole team felt very embarrassed in front of everybody.
Your grandmother says it would bring dishonour on the family if you stole something.
A criminal's name is dragged through the mud, and he loses his good reputation. Which word means 'shame' or 'disgrace'?
The old king rules over a large land, and everyone fears his strength and influence.
A huge, strong storm rolls over the mountain and shakes the houses.
The company is so rich and influential that it controls half the market. Which word means 'powerful' or 'mighty'?

en: to emphasize, to highlight, to stress, to point out, to accentuate
situations: With a yellow pen, you colour the most important lines in your text so they stand out.
In his speech, the speaker says again and again that teamwork is the key to success.
The manager wants to put special focus on one good result in the report. Which word means 'to emphasize' or 'to highlight'?
A small child falls down and cries, calling for the woman who always comforts him.
At school, your friend says, 'I must go home, my female parent is waiting.'
A baby's first words are often 'dada' and this word for the female parent. Which word means 'mum' or 'mummy'?
After winning three gold medals, the athlete is known all over the world.
The old singer enjoys public admiration and many people recognise him on the street.
A soldier from the old stories gets great honour and a place in history. Which word means 'fame' or 'glory'?

en: to enact, to issue, to remit
situations: The government announces a new law and puts it into effect.
The school director issues a new rule that phones are not allowed in class.
The mayor releases an order that forbids parking on the square. Which word means 'to issue' or 'to enact' (a law)?
You open the fridge and smell milk that has gone bad for weeks; it makes you want to be sick.
The soup has a horrible taste and looks like mud.
A dirty, smelly public toilet makes you turn away. Which word means 'disgusting'?
In history class, you learn that Britain once ruled India and many far-away lands as its territories.
A group of ants lives together in a big nest under the ground.
A country far away is ruled by another country as a territory in the 19th century. Which word means 'colony'?
The football coach draws arrows on a board to plan how his team will play against the opponent.
In chess, you plan your moves carefully to trap the other player.
A company has a clever plan on how to win customers from its rivals. Which word means 'tactic'?
You move the chair away to the side so that people can walk through the room.
The teacher takes a student to one side to speak to him privately.
She puts her phone down to one side and starts to work. Which word means 'aside'?

en: to raise, to bring up, to rear
situations: Your aunt takes care of her two little children and teaches them how to behave until they are adults.
The farmer raises a small baby bird by feeding it every day until it can fly.
A grandmother looks after her grandchildren from babies until they are grown up. Which word means 'to bring up' or 'to raise'?
You buy a new phone, and you have to open the cardboard box and plastic around it.
The shop wraps the gift in coloured paper and puts a ribbon on it.
After the delivery, your kitchen is full of cartons and foam. Which word means 'packaging'?
You tell your friend, 'Sorry, I cannot come on Friday. I already have a meeting set with someone.'
The two colleagues meet at the cafe at the time they planned earlier.
The date and place are fixed and both people have agreed. Which word means 'arranged' or 'fixed'?
The teacher asks you to calculate how much bigger 12 is than 7.
The two business partners have a serious disagreement about money.
In the report, the gap between the two numbers is five percent. Which word means 'difference'?

en: to support, to endorse, to favour, to favor, to approve
situations: A city councillor says he is for the new bike path and will vote yes.
Your boss says she backs your plan and wants it to go ahead.
Most teachers are in favour of a longer lunch break. Which word means 'to support' or 'to favour' an idea?

en: individual case, single case, specific case, particular case, isolated case
situations: The teacher says that the student's bad behaviour was only one time and not a general problem.
The lawyer says each case must be judged separately, according to its own facts.
The company says the mistake was a unique case and will not happen again. Which word means 'individual case' or 'isolated case'?
You point at the map with the finger next to your thumb.
The teacher raises the finger next to the thumb and says, 'Be quiet.'
A child points to the moon in the sky with one finger. Which word means 'index finger'?
You must wear a suit and tie to the meeting, because it is an official event.
The letter starts with 'Dear Sir or Madam', not with 'Hi'.
Your boss asks you to use polite and official language, not casual talk. Which word means 'formal'?

en: to enable, to allow, to make possible
situations: The scholarship lets you study abroad, which you could not afford before.
The new bridge makes it possible for people to cross the river in minutes.
The app lets users pay with their phones, which was not possible before. Which word means 'to enable' or 'to make possible'?
After a few days in the wet cloth, a tiny green shoot comes out of the bean.
The doctor says you must wash your hands because tiny bacteria can make you ill.
In the kitchen, the potatoes in the dark start to put out small white shoots. Which word means 'germ' or 'sprout'?
The teacher says, 'It is true that water boils at 100 degrees. This is not an opinion, but what we know is real.'
In the debate, one man says, 'Check the facts! The numbers are there.'
You say what really happened, without guessing or an opinion. Which word means 'fact'?
Your friend talks on and on about nothing important for an hour on the phone.
The two women at the next table chat loudly about silly things.
A man keeps on speaking nonsense and you cannot stop him. Which informal word means 'to babble' or 'to prattle'?
In the small town, the man who leads the city government opens the new library with a speech.
In the local newspaper, the elected head of the town says the roads will be repaired.
A man runs the town hall and is chosen by the citizens. Which male word means 'mayor'?
The lawyer gives such strong arguments that everyone in the room believes him.
Her speech is so good that even people who disagreed change their minds.
The salesman's reasons are so strong that you buy the product. Which word means 'convincing' or 'persuasive'?
Both witnesses tell the same story, and their statements are in full agreement.
The police find that the fingerprints on the glass fit exactly those of the suspect.
The numbers in the two reports are exactly the same. Which word means 'match' or 'agreement'?

en: to see again, to meet again
situations: You have not met your old school friend for ten years, and tomorrow you will meet him again.
At the airport, the family is happy to see their daughter again after a long time abroad.
You say goodbye and say you hope to meet again soon. Which word means 'to see again'?
Before the football match, most people think the home team will win; they are the one expected to win.
Among all the dishes in the restaurant, pizza is the one you like best.
At the horse race, the horse with the best chance to win is called what? Which male word means 'favourite'?
The nurse touches the baby very lightly and with great care.
A quiet breeze blows over the field on a summer evening.
The pillow is so smooth and light that you fall asleep fast. Which word means 'gentle' or 'soft'?
Your neighbour's father died, so you go to her door and say you are sorry for her loss.
At a funeral, people shake hands with the family and say words of sympathy.
A friend loses a pet, and you send a card saying you feel sad with him. Which word means 'condolence'?

en: to set up, to put up, to nominate
situations: Before the party, you place tables and chairs in the garden.
The party chooses a woman as its candidate for the next election.
The camper puts up the tent in the field. Which word means 'to set up' or 'to put up'?

en: in between, in the meantime, occasionally
situations: While working all day, you eat a small snack from time to time between meetings.
You study for four hours and now and then take a short break.
The shop is busy, but once in a while a quiet moment comes. Which word means 'in between' or 'occasionally'?
Your uncle has lost all the hair on top of his head and it shines in the sun.
The barber says that there is no more hair to cut because the man's head is completely smooth.
A man shaves his head completely and has no hair. Which word means 'bald head'?

en: to carry out, to perform, to pass
situations: The scientist does an experiment in the lab following the plan step by step.
The school plans a survey and carries it out among all students.
The doctor performs an operation on the patient. Which word means 'to carry out' or 'to perform'?
In the village, the church tower makes a loud ringing sound at noon.
At the school door, the metal object makes a sound when it is time for class.
A cow around its neck has a metal object that rings when it moves. Which word means 'bell'?
Your friend comes from Tel Aviv, so we say his nationality is this.
At the market, you buy oranges that are grown in Israel.
The Prime Minister of Israel visits the city for a conference and is described with this nationality word. Which word means 'Israeli'?
At midnight on New Year's Eve, people pop a bottle and drink a sparkling wine from France.
At the wedding, the guests lift their glasses of bubbly wine.
A very expensive sparkling drink is named after a region in France. Which word means 'champagne'?

en: to evoke, to arouse, to cause
situations: The sad song brings back memories of your childhood and makes you cry.
The medicine can cause an allergic reaction on your skin.
His joke makes the whole room laugh. Which word means 'to cause' or 'to evoke'?

en: cardinal direction, direction, point of the compass
situations: On a hiking trail, the guide says the village lies north of the lake; you learn the compass points.
The compass needle always shows one of four points: north, south, east or west.
In the map, the sun rises in the east. Which word means 'cardinal direction' or 'point of the compass'?
You go online and reserve a hotel room for two nights in Berlin.
The travel agent sends you a confirmation of your trip with the flight and the hotel.
The accountant puts a payment into the books of the company. Which word means 'booking' or 'posting'?

en: complex, lavish(ly), costly, expensive, elaborate(ly), time-consuming
situations: The cake takes six hours to make and requires many special ingredients; it is a lot of effort.
The wedding has a lavish party with a huge hall and an orchestra, which costs a lot.
Repairing the old building needs a great deal of time and money. Which word means 'elaborate' or 'costly'?
The police take away a driver's licence because he drove too fast.
The court takes the lawyer's right to work away from him.
A teacher takes away the right to use the library from the student who broke the rules. Which word means 'to withdraw' or 'to remove'?
A clever child solves a hard puzzle by thinking about it carefully.
Your mother says, 'Use your head before you decide something so silly.'
When someone is wise and thinks clearly, we say he has a sharp one of these. Which word means 'intellect' or 'mind'?
On election day, a man goes to a polling station to put a paper in the box.
The politician says that she wants to speak to the people who will choose their leader.
In the news, the number of people who choose the party has gone up. Which male word means 'voter'?

en: to plan to do, to intend to do, to get to work on
situations: On New Year's Eve, you promise yourself that you will do more sport in the next year.
Before the weekend, you decide that you will clean the whole flat on Saturday.
You make up your mind to finally learn to swim this summer. Which word means 'to plan to do' or 'to intend to do'?
The two friends start their own small company with the help of a bank loan.
In history class, you learn about the year when the university was started by a king.
The club celebrates its 100th anniversary since it was set up. Which word means 'foundation' of a company or club?

en: again, once more, another, renewed, repeated
situations: The bus is late again, for the third time this week, and you sigh.
The teacher tells the student to try once more, since the first attempt failed.
The news reports that the same problem has happened another time. Which word means 'again' or 'once more'?
The same story looks different when you see it from your friend's point of view.
The young engineer says the company offers good chances for his future.
A painter draws the road so it looks smaller in the distance. Which word means 'perspective'?

en: to notice, to realize, to catch, to get
situations: You were on your phone, so you did not catch what the teacher said about the test.
Your neighbour was shouting, and everyone in the street heard it and realised something was wrong.
You ask, 'Did you notice that he left early?' Which word means 'to notice' or 'to catch'?
The engineer does a lot of maths to find out how much weight the bridge can hold.
The bill shows how the final price was worked out step by step.
The teacher asks you to show your work for the maths problem. Which word means 'calculation'?
The project has gone well up to now, and no problem has appeared yet.
You say, 'I have never been to Italy so far.'
Until this moment, the weather this week has been dry. Which word means 'so far' or 'up to now'?
The new phone is easy to use, with no difficult steps.
Your guest is relaxed and friendly and needs nothing special; she is no trouble at all.
The recipe is very simple, with only three steps. Which word means 'uncomplicated' or 'straightforward'?
In the old temple, tall round stone supports hold up the roof.
The building has big round stone posts at the front entrance.
A strong round stone post in a hall carries the weight of the floor above. Which word means 'column' or 'pillar'?
At night, the stars give light in the dark sky.
The little lamp on the desk gives out a soft light in the room.
The face of the child is bright with joy; his eyes seem to give off light. Which word means 'to shine' or 'to glow'?
The teacher draws a circle and measures the line from one side through the center to the other side.
The pizza is 30 centimetres wide from edge to edge through the middle.
To find out the size of the pipe, you measure its widest distance across. Which word means 'diameter'?
In history class, you learn that France ended its king's rule and became a country led by a president.
A country with an elected president and no king is called what?
In the news, a country says it will be led by elected leaders and not by a royal family. Which word means 'republic'?
The big dog growls at the child and he is frightened that it will bite.
A letter says that if you do not pay, you will be punished; it frightens you.
Pollution is a danger to many animals and might make them disappear. Which word means 'to threaten'?
The craftsman repairs the tiny watch with great skill and clever hands.
The goalkeeper catches the ball in a very clever and practical way.
A good negotiator knows how to talk cleverly to get what he wants. Which word means 'skilful'?
Your grandmother gives you a shiny white-grey metal ring for your birthday.
At the Olympics, the athlete comes second and gets a medal of this colour and metal.
Cutlery for special occasions is made of this precious white metal. Which word means 'silver'?
You fly north to see volcanoes, hot springs and the northern lights on a cold land in the Atlantic Ocean.
A friend says her trip to Reykjavik was wonderful, with glaciers and waterfalls.
On the map, a country in the north Atlantic is made of ice and fire. Which word means 'Iceland'?

en: to refer, to relate, to obtain, to source
situations: You get the electricity from a company, so you receive it from there regularly.
In the text, the pronoun 'he' relates to the manager mentioned earlier.
The shop obtains its fruit from farmers nearby and has a regular supply. Which word means 'to obtain', 'to source' or 'to refer'?
A good teacher has qualities like patience and kindness.
The scientist describes the features of the metal: it is hard and does not rust.
Water has the characteristic of boiling at 100 degrees. Which word means 'characteristic' or 'property'?
Before learning to cook fancy meals, you need to learn the most basic skills first.
The new law brings a deep and big change to the whole system.
Reading and writing are the foundation of all education. Which word means 'fundamental' or 'basic'?
In the kitchen, you put the leftover soup into a plastic box with a lid.
At the garage, a big metal tank holds the oil for the heating.
You keep your screws and nails in a small closed box in the cellar. Which word means 'container'?
The company shows a funny video on TV to make people buy its new drink.
A shop hangs big posters on the street to attract customers.
A football club uses famous players to promote its products. Which word means 'to advertise'?
After talking with his father, the boy understands that he was wrong and says sorry.
The police officer asks to look at the documents and read them.
After the long discussion, the manager shows a deeper understanding of the problem. Which word means 'insight'?
You put a red scarf together with a blue coat to make a nice outfit.
The chef joins sweet and sour tastes in one dish.
In the quiz, you join two clues to find the answer. Which word means 'to combine'?
The climbers hold on to a huge, hard stone wall high in the mountains.
Waves hit the large grey stone at the edge of the sea and splash up.
A goat stands on a steep wall of stone on the mountainside. Which male word means 'rock' or 'cliff'?
The professor publishes his research in a serious journal with data and proof.
At university, you must write a text with sources and a careful method.
A study is done by experts using tests and measurements, not guesses. Which word means 'scientific' or 'scholarly'?
After winning the final, the football team lifts a shiny metal prize over their heads.
In the shop window, there is a gold prize for the best player of the year.
The captain kisses the big silver prize in front of the cheering crowd. Which word means 'cup' or 'trophy'?
It was raining hard, but we went for a walk anyway, in spite of it.
The test was difficult, but you passed nevertheless.
He was tired, and he still went to work all the same. Which more formal word means 'nevertheless'?

en: to have one's turn, to be asked, to be picked, to reach, to get at
situations: At the doctor's, you wait and finally the nurse says it is your turn.
In class, the teacher says, 'Who will be asked next to read aloud?'
At the bakery, you stand in line and wait until you will be served. Which word means 'to have one's turn'?
On the news, a man who left his home country because of war arrives in a new city and looks for shelter.
A volunteer helps a person who had to run away from danger to find a flat.
A man who had to leave his country to find safety is called what? Which male word means 'refugee'?
The farmer says the corn was changed in a lab by working with its DNA.
The label on the food says that its plants were altered by modern methods using genes.
A scientist works on a new method that changes the DNA of plants. Which word means 'genetic' or 'relating to genetic engineering'?
After a long day at work, you lie down and a person presses and rubs your sore back.
The spa offers a treatment with warm oil and strong hands for sore muscles.
The sports player has a tight muscle and goes to get it relaxed by hand. Which word means 'massage'?

en: to hide, to conceal, to cover
situations: The child puts the toy behind his back so that nobody sees it.
The spy tries to keep his real name secret and not let anyone know it.
She smiles to cover her sadness so that nobody can see how she feels. Which word means 'to hide' or 'to conceal'?
Tourists stand on the hill and are amazed by the lovely view of the lake.
In the museum, a famous painting of a woman is admired for her looks.
The poet writes a song about the way the sunrise looks so lovely. Which word means 'beauty'?
The manager has a high job in the company and many people work under her.
In yoga class, you hold your body in a particular way for a minute.
The general moves his soldiers to a new place on the hill. Which word means 'position'?
You ride a bike through a flat country with tulips and windmills, and you taste cheese from Gouda.
Your friend from Amsterdam speaks the language of the Netherlands and she is described with this word.
A team in orange shirts plays football for the Netherlands. Which word means 'Dutch'?
After a long, tiring day, you let out a deep breath with a sound and say you are tired.
The student looks at the pile of homework and breathes out loudly.
She looks out of the window sadly and lets out a long breath. Which word means 'to sigh'?
At university, the student writes a long paper that argues one main idea to prove it.
The teacher says, 'Your main claim is interesting, but you must support it with evidence.'
A scientist states a first idea that must still be tested. Which word means 'thesis'?
The tailor takes your size in centimetres before making the suit.
The doctor says to take the medicine in small amounts, to a limited degree.
The government sets one step to fight rising prices. Which word means 'measure' or 'degree'?

en: to reach, to get, to arrive, to enter, to access
situations: After a long walk through the forest, you arrive at a small village.
The secret information reaches the newspaper and becomes public.
A hiker comes to the top after a hard climb. Which word means 'to reach' or 'to get to'?
A man fills out a form to ask for a visa and waits for the office to decide.
At the bank, a woman asks for a loan and the clerk checks her papers.
The office sends a letter to the person who asked for money from the state. Which male word means 'applicant'?
The student listens to his teacher quietly and speaks to her politely.
Younger people stand up to give their seat to an older man on the bus, showing great regard.
The employee talks to his boss in a polite and honouring manner. Which word means 'respectful'?
In the town hall, citizens raise their hands to say yes or no to a plan.
Before the meeting, the teams talk to each other so that their plans fit together.
The members of parliament cast their votes on the new law. Which word means 'vote' or 'coordination'?

en: to be correct, to apply, to be true, to prove right
situations: The teacher reads a sentence and asks, 'Is this true?' and you say it is correct.
The rule says it applies to everyone under 18, and it covers you as well.
The form says to tick the answer that fits you. Which word means 'to apply' or 'to be correct'?
In the army film, a man with stars on his uniform gives orders to the soldiers.
At the airport, a man in uniform with a rank above sergeant checks the plane.
A person who leads soldiers in the military is called what? Which male word means 'officer'?
The shop sells bags that are made from recycled material and are good for nature.
You ride your bike to work instead of driving, and it does less harm to nature.
The new bus runs on electricity and makes no smoke. Which word means 'environmentally friendly'?

en: manager, managing director, general manager, director, CEO
situations: In a small company, one man runs the business every day and answers to the owners.
The email is signed by the person at the top of the company who leads it.
The newspaper interviews the person who leads a big firm. Which male word means 'managing director'?
At the beach in the evening, you watch the sun go below the horizon.
The old ship hits the rocks and slowly goes below the water.
The boat is too full and begins to go under the waves. Which word means 'to sink' or 'to go down'?
Your grandfather says that in his day people wrote letters, but today everybody uses phones.
Children use tablets at an early age these days.
Compared with the past, we now often shop online. Which word means 'nowadays'?
The teacher says that students must give attention to the safety rules.
The traffic sign must be followed by every driver; ignoring it can cause trouble.
The new artist did not get much notice from the newspapers. Which word means 'attention' or 'observance'?
After running a marathon, the athlete lies on the ground and cannot move any more.
The nurse works night shifts for weeks and falls asleep on the sofa from being very tired.
The doctor says your body is worn out from too little rest and too much work. Which word means 'exhaustion'?

en: to take place, to occur, to happen
situations: The bank says the payment will be made within three working days, so you wait for it to happen.
The announcement says the opening of the new hospital will take place in May.
A news report says that the accident happened at night. Which formal word means 'to take place' or 'to occur'?
A judge must decide only by the facts and not by personal feelings.
The reporter writes about the match without taking sides for either team.
A good scientist looks at the data fairly, without personal opinions. Which word means 'objective'?
You want to buy a house, so you and the bank work out how the money will be raised.
The charity needs to find out where the money for the new school will come from.
The company asks investors to pay for its new factory. Which word means 'financing'?
A poster in school says that every person has the right to live in freedom and safety.
An organisation fights for the basic freedoms that every person should have, such as speaking freely.
The right not to be treated cruelly belongs to every person in the world. Which word means 'human right'?
Your hands are cold, so you move them quickly against each other to warm them up.
Before making potato pancakes, you push the potatoes against a metal tool to make small pieces.
You press a cloth on the stain on the table and move it back and forth. Which word means 'to rub' or 'to grate'?
The man who plans and runs the concert says that tickets are sold out.
A company arranges the big city marathon each year and sets the route.
The festival has a problem, and the person in charge of the event speaks to the press. Which male word means 'organizer'?
The offer is only available once and will never be repeated.
You see a rare, wonderful view from the mountain and say there is nothing else like it.
The trip was amazing, one of the best days of your life. Which word means 'unique' or 'fantastic'?

en: to plan, to design, to conceive
situations: The architect draws the first idea of a new library with large windows.
A teacher works out a new course for the next semester, step by step.
The team thinks up a plan for a new app and decides what it will do. Which word means 'to design' or 'to conceive'?
Every morning, your friend sits quietly on a mat with closed eyes and focuses on her breathing.
In the yoga studio, the teacher asks everyone to be silent and clear their mind.
To reduce stress, you spend ten minutes in calm silence, thinking about nothing. Which word means 'meditation'?
The doctor taps your knee and your leg jumps; this was a trigger for a reaction.
The old town has a special charm that makes many tourists visit.
A bright light makes the eye react. Which word means 'stimulus' or 'appeal'?
At the baptism, the priest makes a sign over the baby and asks God for good things for him.
Before the journey, your grandmother touches your head and wishes God's protection for you.
In church, the priest says holy words over the bread. Which word means 'to bless'?
The news warns that the fire is moving quickly across the forest and growing bigger.
Doctors try to stop the illness from moving from person to person across the country.
Over the years, the city grows into the countryside around it. Which word means 'spread' or 'spreading'?
The room is white, clean and without any decoration, like a hospital.
The company tests the new medicine in a trial on patients under a doctor's supervision.
The doctor says that, in medical terms, there are no signs of the illness. Which word means 'clinical'?
Your little brother cannot go out yet because the long string on his shoe is not tied.
You trip because the cord on your trainer has come undone.
In the shop, you need a new pair of strings for your black boots. Which word means 'shoelace'?

en: to be based on, to base
situations: The film is not invented, because it rests on a true story from the 1960s.
The company says its new product is built on years of research.
The theory takes its ground from many experiments. Which word means 'to be based on'?
The lamp in your hallway stops working, so you go to the shop for a new round glass part that gives light.
A child draws an idea as a small glass bulb above a person's head.
You screw a new round glass part into the ceiling lamp. Which word means 'light bulb'?
Your friend says she will not go to the party, and you say you did not want to go anyway.
You offer to help carry the bag, and he says, 'No need, I am going that way in any case.'
There is no point in running, because the train has left already anyway. Which word means 'anyway' or 'in any case'?

en: any, as you like, arbitrary, random
situations: The waiter says you can choose any table you like in the restaurant.
The computer picks a number without any pattern, completely by chance.
The teacher says, 'Take a card, any card at all.' Which word means 'any' or 'random'?

en: college of higher education, university of applied sciences
situations: After school, you study engineering at a practical university with lots of work placements in companies.
Your cousin goes to a school that is not a classic university but teaches practical professions.
In Germany, there are two kinds of higher schools, and one focuses on applied subjects. Which word means 'university of applied sciences'?

en: to extend, to expand, to improve, to enlarge, to remove
situations: The city builds more roads and trains to improve public transport.
The company wants to make its online shop bigger and better next year.
The mechanic takes the old engine out of the car. Which word means 'to expand' or 'to remove'?
Every morning at ten, a man in a yellow jacket brings letters to your front door.
A dog barks at the man who delivers parcels and letters on the street.
You wait for a package and ask the person who delivers letters if it has arrived. Which male word means 'mailman'?
The sign on the shop says the person who owns it is away on holiday.
At the lost property office, a man proves that he is the person that the umbrella belongs to.
The dog's name tag has the number of the person who owns the dog. Which male word means 'owner'?
You are not sure how a word is spelled, so you open a dictionary to find out.
Your mother asks you to go and see whether the door is locked.
You check the timetable to see when the next bus leaves. Which word means 'to look up' or 'to check'?
If you never study for the exam, failing is something that will certainly happen.
The ice melts in the sun, and the water will unavoidably drip down.
A big storm is coming and some damage cannot be avoided. Which word means 'inevitable'?
Scientists are not sure if life on other planets is real, and they ask whether it is there at all.
A small shop owner worries about his livelihood, because the new supermarket may close his business.
A child asks whether ghosts are real. Which word means 'existence'?
The nurse takes a little blood from your arm to be examined in the lab.
The band meets in the evening to practise the songs before the concert.
In the shop, you get a small free portion of the cheese to try. Which word means 'sample', 'test' or 'rehearsal'?

en: to enclose, to differentiate, to distinguish, to delimit
situations: A fence marks the border between your garden and your neighbour's garden.
In the essay, you explain how your topic is different from similar ones.
The teacher shows how to tell two similar birds apart from each other. Which word means 'to distinguish' or 'to delimit'?
The town has a special place and plan for getting rid of old batteries and paint safely.
A company takes away your old fridge and handles its waste correctly.
The cost of getting rid of nuclear waste is very high. Which word means 'disposal'?
Your uncle reads philosophy books all day and enjoys talking about ideas.
The writer is known for her deep thoughts and her smart discussions of art.
The job is not physical but needs a lot of thinking work. Which word means 'intellectual'?
After many years in the capital, she moves to a quiet small town far from the big cities.
In Canada, the country is divided into regions with their own governments, such as Ontario.
The young man says life in the countryside is slow and boring compared with the city. Which word means 'province' or 'the provinces'?
At the gallery, a man with a small hammer sells the old painting to the person who offers the most money.
The police sell the confiscated cars to the highest bidder.
The family sells the antique table by taking offers that keep going higher. Which word means 'to auction'?
In the library, the encyclopaedia has twenty books, and you need the fifth one.
The teacher says, 'Open the second one of the series of novels.'
A big set of books is made of many numbered parts. Which male word means 'volume'?
After the accident, you visit a person who helps you do exercises to move your arm again.
A man sits across from you and listens as you talk about your worries every week.
The patient says that the professional who treats his mind has helped him sleep better. Which male word means 'therapist'?
The young company is full of energy and grows very quickly.
The coach describes the football player as quick and always moving, full of life.
The new manager brings lots of drive and changes things fast. Which word means 'dynamic'?

en: to flee, to escape, to run away
situations: Seeing the big dog, the small cat runs away and hides.
People leave their village in a hurry because of a flood.
The prisoner in the film tries to escape from the building at night. Which word means 'to flee'?
When the old director retires, a younger man comes in to take over his post.
The new phone model replaces the old one and has a better camera.
The king chooses his son as the person who will rule after him. Which male word means 'successor'?
The teacher asks you to explain how far your idea can solve the problem.
You wonder to what degree the new law will change your daily life.
Your boss asks, 'To what extent has the project been finished?' Which word means 'to what extent'?
When you were small, you fell off your bike, and now there is a white line on your knee.
After the operation, the surgeon says a thin mark will stay on your skin.
A man has a long mark on his cheek from an old cut. Which word means 'scar'?
The company promises that the product will work for two years or it will be repaired for free.
The security team makes sure that nobody can enter without a pass.
The government wants to make certain that every child can go to school. Which word means 'to guarantee' or 'to ensure'?
At the market, you buy vegetables grown in your own region, not imported.
The bird is one that naturally lives in this country's forests.
The shop sells products from the local area. Which word means 'native' or 'local'?
In a debate, you give a good reason why the city should build a new park.
Your brother wants a dog, and he lists five reasons that support his wish.
The teacher says your essay is not convincing because the reasons behind your opinion are weak. Which word means 'argument'?

en: to suffer, to endure, to sustain
situations: In the football match, the team loses badly, and everyone has to live with the defeat.
The driver is hurt in the crash and has to bear a serious injury.
The company loses a lot of money this year. Which word means 'to suffer' or 'to sustain' a loss?
The cat's soft covering is warm and thick, and you stroke it.
In winter, the dog's thick hair keeps him warm in the snow.
The hunter takes the skin and hair of the animal to make a rug. Which word means 'fur' or 'coat' of an animal?
In a board game, you shake a small cube with dots and throw it on the table.
The teacher shows a solid shape with six equal square sides.
In the game, you roll a small cube and get a six. Which word means 'cube' or 'dice'?
The gymnast can bend her body in ways that most people cannot.
Your grandfather is old, but he can still touch his toes easily.
The cat can twist and jump into very small spaces. Which word means 'supple' or 'flexible'?
You stand outside in a thin shirt, and your body shakes a little from the cold.
The child comes out of the water and starts to shake because he is cold.
You have a fever and feel a cold shake going through your body. Which word means 'to shiver'?
A person stands by the road and carefully watches the bird without disturbing it.
The UN sends people to watch an election to see that it is fair.
A man sits on a bench in the park and silently watches the people. Which male word means 'observer'?
The train goes into a mountain, and for a few minutes it is completely dark outside.
On the road to Italy, you drive through a long dark passage under the Alps.
Workers dig a long passage under the river for the metro. Which word means 'tunnel'?
When metal gets hot, it becomes a little bigger.
