The company wants to make its business reach into other countries.
The lake spreads over a larger area after heavy rain. Which word means 'to expand' or 'to extend'?
In maths class, the teacher says a line has one, a flat shape has two, and a cube has three.
In a film, the hero travels to another world with different rules of space and time.
The problem has a size that nobody expected, and many sides. Which word means 'dimension'?
On her eighteenth birthday, she can vote and sign contracts without her parents' permission.
The sign says that only people who have reached the legal age as adults may enter.
The bar checks your ID to see if you are old enough to be called an adult. Which word means 'of legal age'?
The army goes back from the border because the battle is lost.
After the scandal, the politician steps away from public life and does not come back.
In a game, your team goes back to its half and stops attacking. Which word means 'retreat' or 'withdrawal'?
At the vote, you do not say yes or no, you simply do not choose a side.
The councillor does not vote in the meeting because he has a conflict of interest.
Your friend asks what you voted, and you say that you chose neither. Which word means 'to abstain'?
In a white coat and gloves, the scientist mixes chemicals in tubes at her workplace.
A blood test is sent to a special room, where machines examine it.
At university, the chemistry students do experiments in a room with microscopes and safety glasses. Which word means 'laboratory'?
Someone says a sentence, and you cannot understand it without knowing the situation around it.
The reporter says the quote was taken out of the surrounding text and so means something different.
The teacher says to look at the sentences before and after to understand the word. Which word means 'context'?
The student sits quietly at the desk and puts all her attention on the exam.
The surgeon works with great care and does not look at anything else.
The pupils listen to the teacher without being distracted by their phones. Which word means 'focused'?
Before bed, you clean your teeth with a toothbrush and paste.
You smooth your long hair with a comb-like tool until it is tidy.
You clean your dirty coat with a stiff tool to remove the dust. Which word means 'to brush'?
The boss shouted at the workers, and they thereupon left the room.
The shop received many complaints, and as a result it changed the recipe.
You told him a joke, and right after that he started to laugh. Which word means 'as a result' or 'thereupon'?
In the letter, the writer says, 'With regard to your last email, here is my answer.'
You buy a new cloth to put over the cushion on your sofa.
The text makes a link to a famous book. Which word means 'reference' or 'cover'?
The pianist plays the song without a single mistake, and the audience says it was flawless.
The designer works for weeks to make every detail exactly right.
The cook wants the dish to be absolutely without fault. Which word means 'perfection'?
You stand quietly behind the door and secretly hear what the neighbours are saying.
In the forest, you stay still and carefully listen to the birds.
The child sits near the fire, listening to his grandfather's story with big eyes. Which word means 'to listen' or 'to eavesdrop'?
The little boy solves a very hard maths problem, and the teacher is amazed.
The dog finds its way home from 50 kilometres away, which is surprising.
The concert sold out in one minute, which is hard to believe. Which word means 'astonishing' or 'amazing'?
In the football match, the player who put the ball in the net is named on the screen.
At the shooting range, a man hits the target every time with his rifle.
In horoscopes, the sign of November and December is shown as a man with a bow. Which male word means 'marksman', 'scorer' or 'Sagittarius'?
Before building the house, the workers lay a solid base to support the walls.
The teacher says that good basic knowledge is the foundation for learning more.
The two countries sign a contract and use it as the ground for further talks. Which word means 'basis'?

en: to free, to liberate, to release, to rid
situations: After years in prison, the man is let go and is no longer held.
You clean the old paint from the table so that it is free of it.
The firefighters help the animal that was stuck in the fence to get out. Which word means 'to free' or 'to liberate'?
At a party, someone asks when your birthday is and says you are a Leo or a Virgo.
In the magazine, the horoscope page lists twelve signs, one for each part of the year.
Your friend believes that the sign you were born under says something about your character. Which word means 'zodiac sign'?
Switzerland, Austria and Germany are countries where people speak a certain language, and tourists are told this.
The newspaper is aimed at readers in countries where this language is spoken.
The hotel has a guide for visitors who speak the language of Berlin and Vienna. Which word means 'German-speaking'?
Once a year, you go to the doctor for a check-up before you become ill.
You save money each month so that you will be safe when you are old.
The company has put up safety measures to avoid accidents before they happen. Which word means 'prevention' or 'precaution'?

en: to form, to shape, to mold
situations: A child makes small animals out of soft clay with his fingers.
The potter gives the wet clay the shape of a bowl.
The baker makes the dough into small round rolls. Which word means 'to form' or 'to shape'?
A mother says to her small son, 'Come here, my little dear!'
Among all the toys, the teddy bear is the one the child loves best.
The teacher has a student she likes best and treats a little better than the others. Which male word means 'favourite' or 'darling'?
In a race, the runner who crosses the line before everyone else wins the gold medal.
You enter the room and are the one in line before all others.
In a list of ranks, number one comes before number two. Which word means first (1st)?

en: to decide, to determine, to define
situations: The teacher is in charge and says who will read next.
A scientist uses tests to find out the type of the plant.
The law says that, from now on, every driver must wear a seatbelt. Which word means 'to decide', 'to determine' or 'to define'?
The news says the country has money problems, with high prices and few jobs.
The government plans a package to help firms and workers to get through the crisis.
A shop makes a profit, so it is worth running. Which word means 'economic' or 'cost-effective'?
In the film, men with masks suddenly enter the bank and demand money.
A man is stopped on a dark street at night and his bag is taken.
The news reports a sudden attack on a petrol station. Which word means 'robbery' or 'raid'?

en: to misplace, to mislay, to postpone, to reschedule, to publish
situations: You cannot find your glasses because you put them somewhere and forgot where.
The meeting is moved from Monday to Wednesday, so the date is changed.
A company prints and sells new books, which means it brings them out. Which word means 'to misplace', 'to postpone' or 'to publish'?
On your burger, there is a long green vegetable cut in slices with a sour taste.
A salad has long, green, watery slices that are cool in summer.
Your grandmother puts small vegetables in a jar with vinegar for winter. Which word means 'cucumber' or 'gherkin'?
The notice in the office says that the office is, from this day on, open on Saturdays.
In a formal letter, the company says that, after the long delay, the work is now complete.
The report states that the building is, as of this moment, finished. Which formal word means 'now'?
The court explains that its decisions about the law over many years show how the rule is read.
The lawyer says that the judgments of the highest court all agree on this matter.
The students learn about the system by which judges decide legal questions. Which word means 'jurisdiction' or 'judicial decisions'?
The supermarket sells many different kinds of cheese from all over the world.
The team is made of people from many backgrounds and ages.
The magazine has lots of varied articles on topics that are not connected. Which word means 'diverse' or 'various'?

en: to call, to name, to describe, to denote
situations: People give this small animal a name, such as cat, in their language.
The text uses a certain word to describe a typical worker.
The teacher asks you to say what the symbol on the sign denotes. Which word means 'to call', 'to name' or 'to denote'?
Oil, coal and iron ore are natural materials that factories use to make goods.
The country is rich because it has lots of wood and metal in the ground.
Before a table is made, wood is the natural material needed. Which word means 'raw material'?
In the film, the thieves hold a woman in the bank and will not let her go until they get their money.
The news reports that a person was kept by criminals who made demands for her release.
A man is held by others so that they can force something from the police. Which word means 'hostage'?
Your friend remembers every detail of the page as if he had taken a picture of it with his mind.
The museum shows a collection of pictures taken with a camera in the 1950s.
The artist uses a method with film and light to create images. Which word means 'photographic'?
The teacher takes a long time to make the hard text clearer with examples.
At the meeting, the manager gives more details about the plan to the staff.
The guide describes the history of the old castle to the tourists. Which word means 'to explain' in a detailed way?
After the news about the bombing, the whole city is full of fear.
The government says it will fight against people who spread violence to make citizens afraid.
A film shows a time of cruelty and fear under a violent leader. Which word means 'terror'?
Looking from the hill, you see a village far away at the edge of the horizon.
He dreams of going to far places and living abroad.
A ship sails away and becomes smaller until it is gone in the far space. Which word means 'distance'?

en: to put in charge, to imply, to insinuate, to store, to take shelter
situations: Your boss says he will make the new worker answer to you, so you are in charge of him.
You park your bike under a roof to keep it out of the rain.
The man says to you, 'You are only helping me because you want something,' which you never said. Which word means 'to insinuate' or 'to take shelter'?
At the Olympics, athletes from every country march into the stadium with their flags.
The president speaks to all the people of the country on television.
People who share a land, a history and a culture are called what? Which word means 'nation'?
The man has a job that is not for a limited time, and he can keep it for many years.
The sign says the road is closed forever, not just for a week.
The noise from the building site is always there, day and night. Which word means 'permanent'?
On the beach in the evening, the sky turns red and orange as the sun goes down.
Couples sit on a bench to watch the sky change colour at the end of the day.
The photographer waits on the hill for the moment when the sun touches the horizon. Which word means 'sunset'?

en: to arouse, to excite, to attract, to annoy
situations: The loud noise makes the horse very nervous and excited.
The strange new building makes all the people curious and gets their attention.
His rude behaviour makes the teacher angry. Which word means 'to arouse', 'to excite' or 'to annoy'?
In the classroom, a round model of the Earth stands on a stand and you can turn it with your hand.
You point at a country on a ball-shaped map on the teacher's desk.
As a gift, you buy a small ball that shows the seas and the continents. Which word means 'globe'?
On the news, the leader of a republic talks to other leaders at a summit.
The head of the club opens the yearly meeting and welcomes the members.
The man who is chosen as leader of the country lives in a big house and signs laws. Which male word means 'president'?
The doctor says there is no cure for the patient's illness, and she has only a short time left.
The old man is in the hospital and knows that his disease will end his life soon.
A character in the film has an illness that cannot be healed. Which word means 'terminally ill'?

en: to forbid, to prohibit, to ban
situations: A sign at the pool says that running is not allowed, and the lifeguard says it is banned.
The doctor does not allow you to eat sweet things for a month.
The city has made smoking on the bus stop against the rules. Which word means 'to forbid' or 'to ban'?
On the news, the group of ministers led by the chancellor announces a new plan for the whole country.
The government in Berlin decides on rules for all the states.
The ministers meet to decide a new law that applies in all regions of the country. Which word means 'federal government'?
The children run from the bottom to the top of the hill.
You look to the roof and say, 'Let's go up the stairs.'
The cable car takes the tourists towards the mountain peak. Which word means 'up' or 'upwards'?
You travel by train to Munich and Stuttgart, near the Alps and the Black Forest.
People in this region say 'Servus' and eat pretzels and white sausage.
The map shows the part of the country with Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg. Which word means 'southern Germany'?
During the test, a student looks at his neighbour's paper to copy the answers.
In a card game, your friend hides a card in his sleeve so he can win.
A runner takes a shortcut during the race so he finishes earlier. Which word means 'to cheat'?
The coach says the young player may become a champion one day, as he has the possibility.
The police say the unknown package is a possible danger.
The company talks to people who may buy the product in the future. Which word means 'potential'?
On the kitchen shelf, your grandmother keeps a thick book full of recipes with pictures of dishes.
You want to make a new dinner but forget the steps, so you open the book with recipes and amounts.
As a birthday gift, your friend gets a book with a hundred pasta recipes. Which word means 'cookbook'?
In a history class, you learn about knights, castles and kings living a thousand years ago.
At a fair, people dress up as peasants and soldiers from the time between ancient Rome and modern times.
The museum shows swords, armour and old manuscripts from a period roughly between the 5th and 15th centuries. Which word means 'Middle Ages'?

en: to appear, to seem, to be published, to be released, to come out
situations: A ghost suddenly shows up in the doorway in the old film, and everyone gasps.
The author's new novel will be on sale in the shops next month.
The magazine comes out every Thursday. Which word means 'to appear' or 'to be published'?
On her nose and cheeks, the girl has many tiny brown spots that get darker in the sun.
Your little sister does not like the small spots on her face, but you think they look cute.
In the summer, small brown dots show up on fair skin after a day in the sun. Which word means 'freckle'?
The child asks whether the dragon in the book exists, and you say it is only a story, not what exists in the world.
The scientist says the problem is not imaginary but a fact in the world.
Your friend says the film seems so true to life that it looks like it could actually happen. Which word means 'real'?
You order shoes online, and the shop says the sending of the goods takes two days.
On the website, there is a line for the cost of sending the parcel to your home.
The warehouse is busy packing boxes and sending them to customers. Which word means 'shipping' or 'dispatch'?
You tell your friend, 'Please post the photos to me by email after the trip.'
The company says it will send you the catalogue by mail if you give your address.
Your aunt in another city promises to send you a parcel for your birthday. Which word means 'to send' or 'to mail' to someone?
In a language lesson, the teacher writes 'run', 'eat' and 'sleep' on the board and says they are words that show actions.
To make a sentence, you need a word for who does something and a word for what they do.
Words like 'swim' and 'jump' belong to a group of words that describe actions. Which word means this type of word?
After he got ill from the fish, he stays away from seafood.
You take another road to stay clear of the heavy traffic.
Your friend tries to stay away from her ex at parties. Which word means 'to avoid'?
The nurse puts a long strip of cloth around your hurt arm after the fall.
Football clubs from all over the country are members of one big official organisation.
Farmers join a group to speak together with the government about prices. Which word means 'association' or 'bandage'?
The doctor says your headache is not from the body but comes from stress and worry in your mind.
The film is exciting because of its mind games, not its action.
The test shows how a person's thinking and feelings work. Which word means 'psychological'?
You eat ice cream and feel a sharp pain in your mouth, so you go to the dentist.
At night, you cannot sleep because one of your teeth hurts badly.
Your friend holds his cheek and says there is a sharp pain in his mouth. Which word means 'toothache'?
You arrive late and explain to your boss why it was not your fault, giving good reasons.
The government explains why it spent so much money, to show its decision was right.
A child tries to show that taking the cookie was correct. Which word means 'to justify'?
In the forest, a small natural stream of clear water flows between the stones.
The children take off their shoes and play in a small flowing water near the village.
A little body of running water is smaller than a river. Which word means 'stream' or 'brook'?
In history class, you learn about a system where property is shared and the state controls the economy, used in the Soviet Union.
Your grandfather tells you about living in the East under a system with one party and no private companies.
The system imagined by Karl Marx is one where there are no classes and everything is owned together. Which word means 'communism'?
The school is not private but is run and paid for by the government.
A certificate is given and approved by the authorities of the country.
The bank is owned by the state and not by private people. Which word means 'state' or 'government-run'?
The magician pulls a rabbit from a tiny hat, and the audience is surprised and cannot believe it.
The child's talent for the piano surprises all of his teachers.
The size of the new stadium greatly amazes the visitors. Which word means 'to astonish' or 'to amaze'?
When you dive in the warm sea, you see colourful, hard, branching structures made by tiny animals.
In the aquarium, there are bright pink and orange growths on the rocks under the water.
A big reef in Australia is made from tiny sea animals that build hard shapes. Which word means 'coral'?
You see a broken window and ask, 'By what means did this happen?'
The teacher asks, 'Explain through which steps the water becomes ice.'
The report says that the machine stopped, and through this, the factory lost time. Which word means 'whereby' or 'by what'?
Two shops on the same street sell the same shoes and try to win the same customers.
The runner sees that the man in the next lane is quickly catching up.
A big phone company watches what the other firm in the market is doing. Which male word means 'competitor' or 'rival'?

en: to look, to glance, to peep, to peek
situations: You turn your head and quickly glance at the clock on the wall.
Through the crack in the door, the child peeks into the room to see the presents.
She looks up from her book and over to the window. Which word means 'to glance' or 'to look'?
You ask the shop, 'Is this jacket in stock, so I can buy it today?'
The doctor says she is free to see you on Friday at ten.
The app shows that the meeting room is empty and can be used. Which word means 'available'?
At the end of the war, the people cheer in the streets because they are no longer ruled by the enemy.
A student gets a note that says he does not have to pay the school fees.
After the long exam, you feel a great sense of relief. Which word means 'liberation', 'exemption' or 'release'?
On the news, the police say a man who planned bombings to spread fear has been caught.
In the film, a masked person plans violent acts against innocent people.
A person who uses violence to frighten society for political goals is called what? Which male word means 'terrorist'?

en: to bear, to endure, to stand
situations: You cannot stand the loud music from next door any longer, but you have to put up with it.
The soldier has to carry the pain of his injury without complaining.
She is unable to bear the heat of the sun at noon. Which word means 'to bear', 'to endure' or 'to stand'?
A news report says that a man has been sentenced in court for a serious sexual crime against a person who did not agree.
In a law class, the teacher names the crime of forcing someone into sex against their will.
The police say they take this serious crime very seriously. Which word means 'rape'?
The school says wearing a helmet on the trip is a rule that you cannot skip.
Attending the first lecture is not a choice for the students; everyone has to be there.
The contract says you must pay the fee every month. Which word means 'mandatory' or 'compulsory'?
In the old castle tower, a man is kept behind a locked door and cannot leave.
The soldier is captured in the war and held by the enemy.
A man who is locked in jail is called what? Which male word means 'prisoner'?

en: to tend, to tilt, to bend, to lean
situations: The tall tree bends a little toward the road in the wind.
Your cousin often gets angry quickly; he has a habit of doing that.
You lean your head to one side while listening. Which word means 'to tend', 'to tilt' or 'to lean'?
In the discussion, each person says what he thinks about the new rules.
From the hotel, you have a nice view of the sea, and the postcard shows a picture of the town.
Your friend says, 'In my opinion, the film was boring.' Which word means 'opinion' or 'view'?
On the computer screen, a small arrow moves when you push your hand mouse.
You cannot find the little arrow on the screen, so you move your mouse until it appears.
The screen shows a blinking arrow where you will click next. Which word means 'cursor'?
You leave the milk out in the sun, and it goes bad and becomes undrinkable.
The rain makes the picnic bad and ruins the day for everybody.
A single mistake destroys the whole painting. Which word means 'to spoil' or 'to ruin'?
The doctor wants to know the exact kind of pain, not just a general feeling.
The teacher asks for one particular example, not a general one.
This tool is made for one special use only. Which word means 'specific'?
In the Sahara, there is sand as far as you can see, very little rain and hot days.
A camel walks slowly over big dunes with almost no plants around.
The traveller runs out of water in the dry, empty land with sand everywhere. Which word means 'desert'?
Two friends sit at the table and play a round of chess for an hour.
In the newspaper, the football team lost its last match.
Your grandfather says he plays one round of cards with his friends every Sunday. Which word means 'game' or 'round'?

en: to commission, to engage, to hire, to instruct, to task
situations: The city asks an engineering firm to plan the new bridge, giving it the job.
The manager gives a colleague the task of preparing the report.
You hire a company to paint your house. Which word means 'to commission' or 'to instruct'?
The doctor advises you to keep the air in your bedroom fresh, with the right temperature and moisture.
The office has a new system that controls how warm and humid the air feels inside.
In the winter, the heating makes the air in the flat very dry. Which word means 'room climate'?
Two sisters look exactly the same because they came from a single fertilised egg that split.
The doctor says the boys are the same in their genes, because they come from one egg.
Twins who share the same DNA and look identical are called what? Which word means 'identical' (twins)?
After a long day at work, you want to be in the place where you live, on the sofa.
The phone rings, and your mother asks, 'Are you in the flat now?'
You say, 'I am staying in tonight, I will not go out.' Which word means 'at home'?
A teenager goes through a period when he only listens to loud music, and it will pass.
The moon changes from a thin line to a full circle in different stages.
The project is divided into three stages, and the first has just ended. Which word means 'phase'?
The boy says to his mother, 'It was me who broke the window.'
In the police film, the man finally tells the truth about what he did.
You say sorry and tell your friend that you lied to him. Which word means 'to confess' or 'to admit'?
On the form, there is a line for your first name and a line for the name you share with your family.
The teacher calls the class by the name that comes after the first name, like Mr Meyer.
On the passport, the family name of the person is written in the first line. Which word means 'surname'?
The new law makes people argue, and half the country is for and half is against.
The player's decision to leave is something that fans cannot agree on.
The film's ending is something that critics keep discussing and many dislike. Which word means 'controversial'?
On a hot summer day, you eat a big green fruit with red flesh and black seeds.
At the picnic, your uncle cuts a huge round fruit into slices and everybody eats it.
The market sells large round fruits with green skin, that are very juicy and sweet. Which word means 'watermelon'?
You hear a concert is free tonight, and you decide you will walk to the place.
Your teacher says, 'If you want to see the show, you must go there on time.'
A friend says there is a nice cafe nearby, and you say you want to go there. Which word means 'to go (there)'?
A little boy runs to the door and shouts when he sees his father coming home.
At the playground, a girl asks her father to push the swing and says his name for him.
A baby's first words are often 'mama' and a word for the male parent. Which word means 'dad' or 'daddy'?

en: to widen, to extend, to expand, to broaden
situations: The company adds a new building to make the factory bigger.
You read many books to make your knowledge wider.
The city makes the road wider so that more cars can pass. Which word means 'to widen', 'to extend' or 'to broaden'?
The teacher explains the steps by which a seed grows into a plant.
The police write a report about what happened at the crossroads.
The manager says the whole way things are done in the office, from the request to the answer, is slow. Which word means 'process' or 'occurrence'?
The man has a lot of hair on his arms and chest.
The spider has a thick, furry body and long legs.
The dog's legs are covered with long fur and look like they have thick hair. Which word means 'hairy'?
Many people in the village go to church because of their deep trust in God.
He has trust that he will get better, though the doctor is not sure.
She says that her religion gives her strength and hope. Which word means 'faith' or 'belief'?
The climber manages to get over his fear of heights and reaches the top.
The team fights hard and finally gets past all the problems of the year.
She gets over her shyness and gives a speech in front of everyone. Which word means 'to overcome'?
In the shop, the person at the counter gives you the goods and takes your money.
The company says that this month the number of items sold was higher than last month.
You put your old bike on the internet because you want to get rid of it for money. Which word means 'sale'?
You want to visit the Great Wall and eat noodles, so you fly to this big country in Asia.
Beijing is the capital of this country with over a billion people.
The map shows a very big country east of India that makes many of the world's phones. Which word means 'China'?
After the flu, you have no energy and feel weak on the sofa.
The salad lies in the sun and the leaves are floppy and soft.
The man's handshake is limp and has no force. Which word means 'limp' or 'listless'?

en: to prefer, to favour, to favor
situations: You can have tea or coffee, and you say you like tea better.
The teacher gives one student more help than the others, which is unfair.
Many people choose the train over the plane for short trips. Which word means 'to prefer' or 'to favour'?
After years of research, the scientists make a big discovery that changes medicine.
The singer's first song becomes a huge hit, and suddenly she is famous.
The water breaks through the wall of the dam. Which word means 'breakthrough' or 'breach'?
In the garden, a small black insect carries a leaf many times its own size to its nest.
A long line of tiny insects walks across your picnic blanket looking for sugar.
A small animal that lives in colonies under the ground is hard-working and strong. Which word means 'ant'?
You say to your friend, 'Do not worry about the dishes, I have to wash my plate in any case.'
Your brother says, 'I do not care if I get blamed, I always get blamed anyway.'
You say 'It is raining anyway, so we may as well stay inside' in a casual way. Which short casual word means 'anyway'?

en: to put up, to erect, to straighten up
situations: After bending over for a long time, you slowly move your back up straight.
The workers put up a tall flagpole in front of the town hall.
After the storm, the farmer raises the fallen fence. Which word means 'to put up', 'to erect' or 'to straighten up'?
The police are looking everywhere for a missing child, and many volunteers join in.
You type words into the website to find a flat in the city.
Where are my keys? You spend half an hour going through all the rooms. Which word means 'search'?
The sign says that you may park here for two hours.
The teacher says you are allowed to use a dictionary in the test.
In the park, dogs are permitted if they are on a leash. Which word means 'allowed' or 'permitted'?
You buy a can to cover your old wooden door with a shiny, hard colour.
The car has a scratch, and the garage needs to repair the shiny coating on top.
The painter uses a clear, glossy liquid to protect the wooden table. Which word means 'varnish' or 'paint'?

en: to fix, to fix one’s eyes, to fixate
situations: The doctor holds your broken arm in place with a cast so that it cannot move.
You stare at one point on the wall and do not look away.
The workers attach the board with screws so it does not move. Which word means 'to fix' or 'to fixate'?
On your phone, you download a small program to check the weather.
The company has made software that you can use on your tablet for banking.
On the screen, there are many little icons for programs. Which word means 'application' (an app)?
The girl plays the violin perfectly at the age of seven, and the teacher says she has a special natural ability.
Your classmate draws amazing pictures without ever having taken a lesson.
A boy learns languages so fast that people say he has great natural talent. Which word means 'gifted' or 'talented'?
After the flood, many people send letters to the families who lost their homes, to show that they care.
At the funeral, the neighbours express their warm feeling for the sad family.
A friend's mother passes away and you say you feel for him in this hard time. Which word means 'sympathy' or 'compassion'?
Before the trip to Africa, the doctor gives you a shot to protect you from a disease.
Children at school get an injection that prevents measles.
Every autumn, many older people go to the doctor to get a shot against the flu. Which word means 'to vaccinate'?
After you cut your finger, the skin around it turns red, hot and swollen.
The doctor says that your throat is red and sore because it is infected.
A wound is painful and swollen, and you need medicine. Which word means 'inflammation'?
The doctor asks what signs of the illness you have: a cough, fever or a headache.
A runny nose and a sore throat are the first signs that you are catching a cold.
A rash can be a sign of an allergy. Which word means 'symptom'?

en: to ignore, to skip, to pass
situations: The manager does not mention your good work and simply leaves you out of the talk.
You see an item that you do not know and you decide to skip the question.
The boss chooses another person for the job and does not take you into account. Which word means 'to ignore' or 'to skip'?
The room is cold, bare and has no soft chairs, so you do not want to stay.
Outside, it is wet, dark and windy, and you do not want to go out.
The waiting room has hard chairs and bright lights, so you feel uneasy. Which word means 'uncomfortable' or 'unpleasant'?
The glasses have a curved piece of glass in front of each eye so you can see clearly.
A camera has a glass part at the front that focuses the light.
A tiny, round, flat bean is cooked in a soup with sausage. Which word means 'lens' or 'lentil'?
The new girl speaks in front of the class without fear because she believes in herself.
After many failures, the boy has little trust in his own abilities.
A good coach helps young players to believe in themselves more. Which word means 'self-confidence'?
In a quiet classroom, a boy lets out gas from his bottom with a funny sound, and the kids laugh.
The little child giggles after he makes a smelly noise while sitting on the sofa.
A silly children's book is about a dog who does this everywhere. Which informal word means 'to fart'?
In an economy class, the teacher explains the system where private people own companies and compete for profit.
In the news, a writer says that markets and private ownership make some people very rich.
The opposite of communism is an economic system with free markets. Which word means 'capitalism'?
The company says that the costs have gone up by a large amount this year.
There is a big difference between the two prices, and it matters a lot.
The accident caused serious and noticeable damage to the building. Which word means 'considerable' or 'significant'?
In the supermarket, the people buying and using products are protected by the law.
A report says that the people who buy goods are paying higher prices for food.
A group tests products and tells the people who buy them which ones are best. Which male word means 'consumer'?
The committee spends the afternoon working on the question of the new school rules.
A student says that she will look into the topic of climate change for her essay.
The lawyer says he is busy with your case at the moment. Which word means 'to deal with'?

en: on the other hand, on the contrary, in contrast, whereas
situations: You say, 'My brother loves football; my sister, on the other hand, hates it.'
In summer, the days are long; in winter, in contrast, the days are short.
The first test was easy, whereas the second was very hard. Which word means 'on the other hand'?
The contract for your phone lasts two years, and then you can end it.
The bank explains that the loan has a time of five years before it must be paid back.
The film has a length of ninety minutes. Which word means 'term' or 'duration'?

en: to arrive, to come true, to happen, to occur
situations: The guests will be here at six o'clock, the host says.
The train from Munich gets to the station at eleven.
What the fortune teller said about you comes true the next week. Which word means 'to arrive' or 'to come true'?
With your fries, you squeeze a red, sweet sauce made from tomatoes out of a bottle.
A child puts a lot of red sauce on a hot dog.
At the burger place, there are two bottles on the table: one with yellow mustard and one with this red sauce. Which word means 'ketchup'?
The teacher says that only the most important points are needed for the test.
There is a big, basic difference between the two plans.
Water is a basic need of all living things. Which word means 'essential' or 'fundamental'?
You take a ferry to Copenhagen, the capital of a small country north of Germany.
Your friend says that he is moving to a country known for its bikes and the little mermaid statue.
The map shows a country with many islands between the North Sea and the Baltic Sea. Which word means 'Denmark'?

en: to go past, to pass by, to pass, to miss
situations: You walk along the street and move by your friend's house without stopping.
The bus does not stop, it simply goes past the bus stop.
The opportunity passes you by and you miss it. Which word means 'to go past' or 'to pass by'?
After failing every exam, the boy feels that he is a complete loser.
The film was a big flop and nobody went to see it.
He says, 'I never get anything right; I am a failure.' Which male word means 'failure' or 'loser'?
From the letter, it is clear that she was angry.
The mistake is easy to see in the numbers, as anyone can notice it.
It is plain that he did not prepare for the meeting. Which word means 'apparent' or 'evident'?
After years of work, she finally achieves her dream of becoming a doctor.
The company makes sure that every rule in the contract is followed and done.
A wish that has come true brings a feeling of deep satisfaction. Which word means 'fulfilment'?
The teacher tells you to look at page ten of the book for more information.
The website sends you to another page to read the rules.
The doctor directs you to a specialist. Which word means 'to refer'?
A bird opens the two parts of its body that it uses to fly, and goes up in the air.
The plane has two long metal parts at the sides that hold it in the air.
A butterfly has colourful parts that move when it flies. Which word means 'wing'?
You thought the meeting was at three, but your boss said four, and now there is confusion.
She thought he was angry, but he was only tired; it was a mistake in understanding.
After the email, the two friends find out that they had both understood something different. Which word means 'misunderstanding'?
At the parade, soldiers in uniform march with tanks and flags.
The country spends a lot of money on its army and weapons.
The man had a strict and ordered manner, as if he were a soldier. Which word means 'military'?
The new law brings about a big change in how people work.
Your kind words cause him to smile again.
The medicine causes the fever to go down. Which word means 'to cause' or 'to effect'?
During the exam, you need to keep your attention on the paper for two hours.
The chemist says the amount of salt in the water is very high.
The teacher says your mind wanders and you need to focus more. Which word means 'concentration'?
After winning every race in the season, the athlete is named the best in the world.
The boxer holds the belt as the title holder in his class.
A team wins the final and everyone calls them the winners of the league. Which male word means 'champion'?

en: to aim at, to seek, to strive for
situations: The young woman plans to become a judge and works toward that goal.
The company wants to reach a higher profit next year and sets clear aims.
The politician hopes to win a majority in the election. Which word means 'to strive for' or 'to aim at'?
To rent the flat, you must show a paper that proves that you have a job.
The scientist needs evidence that the medicine really works.
At the border, you need a certificate to show you had a vaccination. Which word means 'proof' or 'certificate'?
He spends money on expensive gifts and parties without thinking and loses it quickly.
The rich family throws out half of the food each day.
The hotel has an over-the-top, lavish lobby with gold on every wall. Which word means 'wasteful' or 'extravagant'?
You lost your glasses and say, 'They must be in some place in the house.'
She wants to live in any place where it is warm.
I have seen this man at some point in some place before, but I do not remember where. Which word means 'somewhere' or 'anywhere'?
You open the back of the car and put your suitcases into the space behind the seats.
At the supermarket, you load the shopping into the car's rear storage space.
The driver says there is not enough space at the back of the car for all the bags. Which word means 'boot' or 'trunk' of a car?

en: to follow, to pursue, to track, to persecute, to prosecute
situations: In a film, a detective runs through the streets right behind a thief, never letting him out of sight.
A nature film shows a cheetah running after a deer across the dry grass.
A state lawyer takes a company to court for cheating its customers. Which word means 'to prosecute'?
Your teacher says that reading many books will make the number of words you know grow bigger.
Before a language exam you try to count how many words you know in that language. What is the whole collection of words a person knows called?
A learning app shows: 'You now know 1,200 words!' That total of known words has a special name.
Your friend does not just say 'we went to the museum'. She tells you every small thing she saw, room by room.
The engineer gives the manager a long report with every number, every step and every small fact included.
A map of your city shows every little street and even single houses. What kind of map is it? Which word means 'in detail'?
A small child puts coins into a pink pig made of clay. When it is full, the child will break it open and buy a toy.
For your birthday, your aunt gives you a pig-shaped box with a slot on top, so you can save your coins.
In a toy shop you see a ceramic animal with a slot in its back for saving money. What is it called?

en: to fix, to fasten, to attach
situations: You want to put a shelf on the wall. You use four screws to make it stay in place.
At the beach, you push long pegs into the sand so the tent will not blow away.
At the bike shop the worker puts a new lamp on your handlebar and tightens it so it does not fall off. Which word means 'to attach'?
In a small town, a group of elected people meets every month to decide where to build the new playground.
A local newspaper writes: 'The town's elected representatives voted yesterday to repair the old bridge.' Who voted?
You live in a village and want to complain about the broken street light. Which group of elected people in your village decides such things?
On Halloween, a child wears a white sheet with two holes for eyes and goes 'Boo!'
An old castle is said to have a floating white figure that walks through the halls at night.
In a scary story, a see-through spirit of a dead person appears in the dark bedroom. What is it?

en: to climb, to rise, to ascent, to move up, to go up
situations: Smoke from a campfire goes slowly up into the sky.
A hot air balloon leaves the ground and goes higher and higher.
Your football team won every match this year, so next season it will play in a higher league. Which word means 'to move up'?
The doctor says your knee cannot be healed with pills. It needs treatment with an operation by a surgeon.
A company says that the daily work of running the business, not the long-term planning, is handled by one manager.
The army talks about a base that is ready and working for use. Which word means 'operational'?
Three friends start a small company together. Each one puts in money and owns a part of the company.
At a firm's yearly meeting, the people who own parts of the firm vote on how to use the profit.
You read that a business has two owners with shares, who are not the boss but own part of the company. What are they called?
After the winter holidays you step on the scale and see that you now weigh three kilos more.
A news report says the number of cars on the city's roads has become bigger every year.
The shop owner is happy: sales this month are higher than last month. Which word means 'an increase'?
You forgot a piece of bread in the kitchen for two weeks. Now it is covered with green and white fuzz.
The cheese at the back of the fridge is old and has fuzzy spots on it. It has begun to do this.
A damp wall in the bathroom starts to get black spots. What is happening to the wall? Which word means 'to go mouldy'?
A writer finishes her novel, and the book appears in all shops on the same day.
A scientist sends her research paper to a journal so that everyone can read it.
A band tells fans: 'The new album comes out on Friday.' Which word means the 'release' of something to the public?
If you never study for a test, you will fail it. It cannot happen differently.
The factory closes, so the workers must look for new jobs. There is no other way.
When you have a lot of rain and a river that is already full, floods will follow. It cannot be avoided. Which word means 'inevitable'?

en: to stress, to emphasize, to emphasise, to accentuate, to hightlight
situations: In your speech you say one sentence louder and slower, so that everyone notices it is very important.
The teacher draws a line under the key word in the sentence to show it matters most.
The manager says, again and again, that safety comes first. Which word means 'to emphasize'?
A man says, 'I saw a flying plate in the sky last night,' but he has no photo or proof.
A friend tells you that cats can always land on their feet. You wonder if you should check if that is true.
In a news story, a politician says something, but nobody has shown it is true. What is such a statement called? Which word means 'claim'?
The teacher says: 'Please look at me and listen carefully. I need your full focus now.'
A baby cries loudly in the supermarket and everybody turns to look at it.
A street artist in bright clothes wants people to notice him. He wants to catch people's what? Which word means 'attention'?
Your football team lost 2:1, but you say to your friend: 'We scored one goal, that is something.'
The train is late, but you say: 'The sun is out, and we have seats.' It is a small good side.
Your holiday was rainy. You say: 'The hotel was nice, though.' Which word means 'at least' or 'after all'?
In the story of a famous book, a scientist makes a living being with his own hands.
A game designer builds a whole new world with mountains, seas and animals on her computer.
A sculptor makes a new statue from nothing but a block of stone. Which word means 'to create'?
Before a holiday you decide: 'We can spend at most 1,000 euros.' That is your limit for money.
The school plans a party and the director says there is only a small amount of money available for food and music.
A company plans how much money each department may spend this year. What is this planned amount of money called?
A very strong storm brings rain and wind that almost break the windows.
Two neighbours have a loud and angry argument in the garden.
After a hard fall, you feel a very strong pain in your arm. Which word means 'intense' or 'severe'?
Before a chess match, the player thinks about a long plan to win the game, not just the next move.
A football coach explains to the team how it will play to win the final.
A company writes a plan on how it will grow its business in the next five years. What is this big plan called?

en: to bear, to endure, to stand, to hold out
situations: It is 40 degrees in the bus, and there is no air conditioning. You can hardly stand it, but you have no choice.
Your neighbour plays loud music every night, and you must put up with it.
The firefighters did not leave the burning building until the last person was safe. They kept going. Which word means 'to endure'?
At a church, two people in a long white dress and a black suit walk out as everyone throws rice.
At a wedding party, the guests clap as the two people who just got married start the first dance.
The photographer asks for a picture of the woman in the white dress and the man next to her on their wedding day. What are the two called together?
You choose a white shirt with no pattern and no logo. It is very simple.
The room has only a bed and a table. There is no decoration at all.
A wedding with no big party, just two people and a quiet dinner. Which word means 'plain' or 'simple'?
Your phone shows no signal because you are too far from the next mobile tower. You are out of what?
A baby's toy is just out of the child's arm length, so the child cannot grab it.
The ad says: 'This electric car can drive 400 km on one charge.' How far a car can go is its what? Which word means 'range'?

en: to come out, to get out, to emerge, to be released, to be published
situations: The door opens, and a little dog runs out of the house into the garden.
Your favourite band's new album will be on sale in shops next month.
The mouse was hiding under the sofa for two hours. Now it is slowly leaving its hiding place. Which word means 'to come out'?
Before you sing on a big stage, your hands shake and your stomach feels strange, though you know the song well.
An actor says he feels very nervous every time just before the curtain goes up.
Before your first speech in front of 200 people, you feel scared and sweaty. What is this nervous feeling called?
After five hours of walking, you stand at the very highest point of the mountain and look at the clouds below.
A climber puts a flag on the highest point of the Alps.
On the picture postcard you see a snow-covered mountain with a pointed top. What is the highest point of a mountain called? Which word means 'summit'?

en: to confiscate, to guarantee, to ensure, to make sure, to secure
situations: The police find stolen goods in a car and take them away as evidence.
Before a trip, you check twice that all windows are shut and the gas is off. You want to be completely sure.
A manager says: 'We must make certain that every customer gets the parcel on time.' Which word means 'to ensure'?
After a long day of exams, you are tired not in your body but in your head and your thinking.
A puzzle is not a sport for the body. It is an activity for the mind.
A teacher says that a good diet helps your mind work better. Which word means 'mental' or 'intellectual'?
It is a cold winter day. You wrap a long piece of wool around your neck before you go outside.
At the shop you choose a soft woolly piece of clothing for your neck, to wear with your hat and gloves.
Your grandmother knits a long, warm, striped item for you so your neck stays warm. What is it?
At the post office you want to send a normal letter in a regular envelope, not a big one and not a parcel.
You ask the clerk how much a stamp costs for an ordinary letter of the usual size.
A company sends the same letter text to all customers. What kind of letter is this? Which word means 'standard letter'?

en: to grant, to put away, to admit, to concede, to acknowledge
situations: In an argument, your friend finally says, 'Okay, you are right, I made a mistake.'
The landlord lets his tenants use the garden for free. He gives them that right.
After the match the coach says, 'Yes, we played badly.' He accepts the truth. Which word means 'to admit' or 'to concede'?

en: association, alliance, federal government, covenant, waistband
situations: Your trousers are too big at the waist, so you pull a belt through the strip of cloth around your middle.
The news says that the country's central government and the regions are meeting to talk about school money.
Several countries form a close group to work together. What is such a union or alliance called?
The market is full of red, yellow, green and blue fruits, cloths and flowers.
A child paints a picture with every colour in the box: bright, happy, and many.
A summer dress has orange, pink, and turquoise patterns. Which word means 'colourful'?
The box says: 'Only for use outside the house.' It tells you how the product may be used.
You do not know what to do with these old jars. You search for a good purpose for them.
In a shop, the sign explains that this cream has many ways of being used. Which word means 'use' or 'usage'?
The alarm rings, and you slowly open your eyes in your warm bed.
The sleeping baby suddenly opens its eyes when the door shuts loudly.
After a long operation, the patient slowly returns from sleep. Which word means 'to wake up'?
The weather forecast says rain, so you pack an umbrella to fit the situation.
The boss said the job is very difficult, and the salary is high to match it.
You say: 'It is very cold outside, so I dress in a way that fits.' Which word means 'accordingly'?
On the coast, a boat finds a quiet place where the sea cuts into the land, with a small beach.
On your holiday you swim in a small, round, protected part of the sea with cliffs on both sides.
A map shows the sea going into the land like a curve, perfect for ships to stop. What is it called? Which word means 'bay'?
The farmer looks at the field where wheat and rye are growing.
You take one tiny seed from a bag of rice or wheat and hold it between your fingers.
The baker says his bread is made from whole cereal seeds. What is a single small seed of wheat or rye called? Which word means 'grain'?
A teacher's help was very important for your success. Without her, you would not have passed the exam.
A new engineer played a key part in building the bridge. Her ideas changed everything.
A judge's opinion is the one that counts most in the case. Which word means 'decisive' or 'significant'?

en: to block, to lock, to ban
situations: The city closes the bridge for cars because of repairs, and a sign says 'Road closed'.
You lose your bank card, so you call the bank to stop it from working.
A game moderator stops a player from the chat for bad behaviour for one week. Which word means 'to ban' or 'to block'?
After the birthday party, there are cups, plates, balloons and toys all over the flat. Nothing is in its place.
At the airport, all flights are cancelled, and thousands of people are running around confused.
Your desk is covered in papers, cables and cups. You say it is a total mess. What is this wild disorder called?
At the supermarket you take a small cardboard box of tea from the shelf.
You buy a bag of ten biscuits. The whole thing is wrapped in plastic.
The label says: 'Contains 500 grams of pasta in a closed paper container.' What is this sold container called? Which word means 'pack'?
The prisoner in an old film climbs over the wall and gets away from the guards.
The mouse runs quickly through a small hole and the cat cannot catch it.
A fox gets out of the trap just in time. Which word means 'to escape'?
A boy is afraid to jump into the pool from the one-metre board. He climbs down and says he has a stomach ache.
In a story, the knight runs away from the dragon before it even moves.
Your friend does not say what he thinks because he is scared of what others will say. What do we call such a person? Which word means 'cowardly'?
You go to a person who gives you professional help on which insurance to buy.
A company hires an outside expert to give tips on how to save money.
At a bank, a man sits with you and explains your choices for a loan. What is his job? Which word means 'advisor'?

en: to delight, to please, to enjoy, to take pleasure
situations: Seeing flowers in the garden every morning makes you feel happy and cheers you up.
A letter from an old friend makes your grandmother happy all day.
You say: 'It makes me very glad that you came.' Which word means 'to delight' or 'to please'?
For breakfast you eat a white, creamy milk product from a cup with a spoon, often with fruit.
At the supermarket you take a small plastic cup of strawberry-flavoured milk product from the fridge.
A dessert is made from milk with special bacteria so that it becomes thick and a bit sour. What is it?
The fire brigade gets a call, and all the firefighters drive out to the scene of a big fire. This is called their what?
Your teacher thanks you for your great effort and hard work in organizing the school party.
A company says it plans the use of robots in its factories next year. Which word means 'use' or 'commitment'?
At the party someone asks, 'What do you do?' You say, 'I work as a nurse in a hospital.'
A man is always on the move and busy; he does many things during the day.
A volcano that still erupts from time to time is not asleep. It is what? Which word means 'active'?
In the library you talk very quietly so that nobody else can hear you.
A child tells a secret into her friend's ear, with a very soft voice.
The teacher says: 'Please don't speak loudly during the exam.' You speak in a very soft voice instead. Which word means 'to whisper'?
On a hill, you see an old stone building where monks live, pray and work together.
A tourist visits a quiet place with a garden, where nuns live a simple life.
In history class you learn that in the Middle Ages, people with a religious life lived together in a closed community building. What is it called? Which word means 'monastery'?
At the bookshop you buy a book with tips on how to stop smoking.
A website gives you practical advice on how to save money every month.
Your mother gives you a book with tips on how to look after a baby. What is such a book called? Which word means 'guide' or 'adviser'?
You are holding a rope tightly. Your friend says, 'You can open your hand now.'
A boy opens his fingers, and the balloon flies up into the sky.
After a breakup, a friend tells you to stop holding on to the past. Which word means 'to let go'?
On a pizza you see small round black or green fruits with a stone inside.
In Greece you eat a salad with tomatoes, cheese and little salty green fruits from a tree.
The oil for cooking comes from this small fruit of a tree. What is the fruit called?
The movie warns: 'This film has scenes that show everything very clearly, with nothing hidden.'
The teacher gives clear rules: 'Say it directly, do not just hint.'
A contract says in plain words exactly what each side must do. It leaves nothing unclear. Which word means 'explicit'?
Your friend asks, 'Is it possible that she will pass the test?' You say, 'Yes, quite possible, I think.'
Someone asks if the cheap restaurant is good. You say: 'Yes, it is definitely good.'
You are asked, 'Could you live in a small flat?' and you answer, 'Absolutely, why not.' Which word means 'quite' or 'absolutely'?
At the end of the year, the accountant makes a paper showing everything the firm owns and everything it owes.
After one month of exercise, you look at all the results and say: 'Overall, I have lost three kilos.' You sum up what happened.
A team coach says: 'At the end of the season we count our wins and losses.' Which word means 'balance sheet' or 'balance'?
A father shows his son the bad school report and asks him directly why the marks are so bad.
A woman goes to her colleague and tells him to his face that she knows he took her lunch.
A reporter puts the proof in front of the minister and demands an answer. Which word means 'to confront'?
It is a very bright day at the beach. You put on dark glasses so your eyes do not hurt.
Driving into the low sun, the driver takes a pair of dark lenses from the dashboard.
In summer, you buy something to wear on your face to protect your eyes from the sun. It is a pair of what?
You take a tape measure and go once around a big tree to know how thick it is.
The teacher says: 'The exam covers a lot, so please learn the whole book.' The size or amount of the material is big.
A manager says the project is growing and nobody knows how big it will get. Which word means 'extent' or 'size'?
A mother cannot find her child in the huge shopping centre. She calls his name with a crying voice and has lost all hope.
The man has lost his job, his flat and his money. He feels there is no way out.
A student cannot solve the problem and starts crying. He thinks it is all useless. Which word means 'desperate'?
Before the trip, you put all the bags neatly into the boot of the car.
On the plane, you place your small suitcase in the box above your seat.
The sailor puts all the ropes and tools into a small space on the boat. Which word means 'to stow'?
In a museum, you see a large picture in a golden frame, made with oil colours on canvas.
An artist spends two months making a picture of a lake with a brush and paint.
In a gallery, you look at a famous picture of a smiling woman painted by hand. What do you call such a picture? Which word means 'painting'?
On the bus, a young man gives his seat to a woman with a big belly who will have a baby in two months.
At the doctor's, a woman waits for her check-up because she will have a baby soon.
A sign at the cinema says that this special seat is for a woman who is going to give birth soon. Who is she? Which word means 'pregnant woman'?

en: to present, to recite, to perform
situations: At the end-of-year party, a child stands on a stage and says a poem from memory.
In a meeting, you stand and show your results to your colleagues with slides.
A pianist plays a piece of music in front of an audience. Which word means 'to present' or 'to recite'?
On a graph, the line goes straight up from bottom to top, like a tall wall.
A tall building has a long straight line of windows from the ground up to the roof.
The teacher says: 'Draw a line that goes straight up, not sideways.' Which word means 'vertical'?
At the zoo, you see a horse-like animal with black and white stripes eating grass.
On a safari, a herd of striped animals runs across the African grassland.
A child asks: 'Which animal has black and white stripes like a pedestrian crossing?' Which animal is it?
After the gym, the trainer says you need to eat more eggs, fish and meat to build your muscles. These food parts are what?
The label on the milk package shows 'fat', 'sugar' and a building block for muscles. Which one?
A fitness shake contains a powder that helps your body grow muscle. The powder is mostly made of what? Which word means 'protein'?

en: to hammer in, to smash, to take, to follow, to choose
situations: The carpenter uses a hammer to drive a nail into the wall.
At a crossroads, you decide to turn into a small side road.
A burglar breaks the window with a stone. Which word means 'to smash' or 'to hammer in'?
A baby sits on the floor and falls gently on the soft part of the body that we sit on.
After sitting for a long time on a hard chair, the part of your body you sit on starts to hurt.
A mother says to her toddler in a friendly way, 'Let me wipe your little what?' Which word means 'bottom' or 'bum'?
A small child runs around the garden with no clothes on after the bath.
The tree in winter has no leaves at all and stands with bare branches.
In the art museum there is an old statue of a person without any clothes. Which word means 'naked'?
Your computer suddenly stops, the screen goes black and you lose your work. This is a sudden failure of the system.
The news reports that a small plane fell from the sky into a field.
A game app on your phone closes by itself every time you open it. What does this sudden stop and failure of a program or plane mean? Which word means 'crash'?

en: to convert, to transform, to change, to turn
situations: A company turns an old factory into flats where people can live.
Ice in the sun becomes water. It changes from one form to another.
At the exchange office, you change euros into dollars. Which word means 'to convert' or 'to transform'?
On a long train ride, you play cards with your friend just to have something to do.
Your grandfather loves doing crossword puzzles in his free time to keep himself busy.
What do we call something you do for fun while you wait, when you are bored? Which word means 'pastime'?

en: again, in turn, on the other hand
situations: The first shop sold the bag for 20 euros. The second shop, on the other hand, sold the same bag for 30 euros.
My brother loves coffee. His wife, in turn, never drinks it.
You tell a story and then say, 'And this person, in turn, told another friend.' Which word means 'in turn' or 'again'?
At the beach, a child sees a small sea animal with two big claws walking sideways on the sand.
In a fish restaurant, you can order a sea animal with claws. It has a hard shell that turns red after cooking.
A doctor explains that some cells in the body grow wildly and cause a serious illness. Which word means 'cancer'?
A heavy rain falls for three days, and floods in the town are the consequence.
In the study, the data shows that bad sleep leads to poor school marks. The marks come as a result.
A manager says that the drop in sales is a result of the high prices. Which word means 'to result'?
In the old house, the corridor has no light, and you can hardly see anything. It feels a little scary.
The sky is full of heavy clouds, and it feels like evening at noon.
A film begins in a dark, sad and unfriendly town. Which word means 'gloomy'?
A manager uses the company credit card to buy private holidays. He uses his power in a wrong way.
A news report says that a person was using a trusted position in a bad and wrong way.
A doctor warns that taking too many pills for pain is wrong use of medicine. Which word means 'abuse' or 'misuse'?

en: to tolerate, to bear, to take, to get on, to make up
situations: After eating spicy food, your friend says, 'I cannot handle it; my stomach hurts.'
Two brothers had a fight but made peace and now they get along again.
You say that you can't tolerate milk. Which word means 'to tolerate' or 'to get on with'?
On the form, you see a space where you must write the name of the product.
The teacher says the correct word for a young cat is 'kitten'. That is the proper term.
At work, your job name on your contract is 'Sales Assistant'. This name or title for something is called what? Which word means 'designation'?
On a farm, a horse sleeps in a building with straw on the floor.
In the countryside, a farmer feeds his cows in a barn at night.
A child keeps a pet rabbit in a small wooden house in the garden. What is this house for animals called? Which word means 'stable' or 'shed'?
After the new heater was installed, the room became clearly warmer. You could notice it.
Prices in the shop have gone up so much that everyone clearly sees it.
The doctor says: 'You will feel a clear difference after a week of treatment.' Which word means 'noticeable'?

en: to pull in, to ask for, to catch up, to obtain
situations: You are a slow runner. Your friend started later but runs faster and now stands next to you.
Before you build a house, you must ask an office for official papers or a permission.
A company asks for three offers from different firms before buying. Which word means 'to obtain' or 'to catch up'?
At the family dinner, you introduce the woman who is married to your brother.
Your husband's sister comes to visit you for the weekend, and you call her by a special family word.
Your brother's wife is a member of your family by marriage. Which word means 'sister-in-law'?
In a chemistry lesson, the teacher explains that water is made of oxygen and the lightest gas in the world.
A new bus does not use petrol but a very light gas, and its only waste is water.
In the periodic table, the first and lightest element has the letter 'H'. Which word means 'hydrogen'?
You put thick material in the walls of your house so heat does not escape in winter.
During an illness, the doctor says the sick child must stay alone in a room so others do not get it.
An electrician covers a bare wire with plastic so that there is no electric shock. Which word means 'to insulate' or 'to isolate'?
A family goes to church each Sunday, and their priest follows the Pope in Rome.
In Bavaria, many villages have a church of a Christian faith that is led from Rome.
On a form, you must write your religion. The person writes the Christian group whose leader is the Pope. Which word means 'Catholic'?
The hikers start the long walk up the mountain at six in the morning.
A young worker gets promoted to manager after only three years in the firm.
A small local team wins its league and moves up to the first division. What is this move up called? Which word means 'ascent' or 'promotion'?
After the accident, the man lies on the ground and does not answer. He has lost the state of being awake and aware.
You understand that smoking is bad for your health. You have a clear understanding of the problem.
The doctor says the patient has come back to a state in which he knows who and where he is. Which word means 'consciousness' or 'awareness'?

en: to colour, to color, to dye, to stain, to turn
situations: At the hairdresser's, your friend changes her hair from brown to red.
In autumn, the leaves of the trees slowly get yellow and red.
A child puts red ink into a glass of water and the water becomes pink. Which word means 'to colour' or 'to dye'?
On Saturday, your friends plan a trip together to a lake with a picnic.
A small business starts a risky new project in another country. It is something one takes on.
The tourist office suggests a fun trip, a day out for the family. Which word means 'venture' or 'undertaking'?
In a museum, you touch a screen and the exhibit answers you and changes with your choices.
A learning game reacts to every answer you give, and you are not just watching.
The teacher says that this new website lets users talk with the program, not only read. Which word means 'interactive'?
A plan is on paper, and now builders begin to carry it out, step by step.
At the shop the seller says: 'This model comes in two different versions: leather and cloth.'
The manager praises the way the project was done: 'The carrying out of the plan was perfect.' Which word means 'execution' or 'implementation'?

en: to cream, to put cream on, to moisturize
situations: After a day in the sun, you spread lotion on your arms and legs so they do not dry out.
In winter, you rub a little cream on your hands because the skin feels dry.
A mother puts sun lotion on her child before going into the pool. Which word means 'to put cream on'?
The detective says: 'There must be a deeper reason behind this crime. What is the basic cause?'
A lawyer explains that an old rule is the foundation of the new law.
In a science class, the teacher says that one simple idea is behind all these results. It forms the base. Which phrase means 'to form the basis'?
For breakfast, an egg is cooked in a pan with the yolk on top, not mixed, not boiled.
On a burger in a restaurant, there is an egg cooked flat, with a round yellow centre looking up at you.
You ask a cook for an egg that is fried on one side with the yolk still soft. What is it called? Which dish is it?
Your period is late. You buy a small plastic stick at the pharmacy and wait two minutes to see one line or two.
A woman sits in the bathroom, holding a little stick with a window. The result will tell her if a baby is on the way.
At the pharmacy, a customer asks for something to check at home if she is expecting a baby. What is the small product called?
Yesterday you had a cold. Today you have a high fever, a cough and you cannot get out of bed. Your cold got more serious.
The traffic was bad on Monday, but on Tuesday there was a big accident and it was much more terrible.
Your friend says her day was bad, but yours was even more awful. Which word means 'worse'?

en: to put back, to put aside, to cover (distance)
situations: You walk 10 kilometres to get to the village. The guide says you have already done half of the way.
At the clothes shop, you ask the seller to keep the jacket for you until tomorrow, because you have no money now.
After reading, you take the book and place it on the shelf where it was before. Which word means 'to put back'?
The manager says he likes your positive way of thinking and your willingness to help others.
The company will begin to give a job to three new workers next month. This is the act of hiring someone.
On your camera, you change the brightness and focus. These options are called what? Which word means 'setting'?
You plan a holiday to a warm country in Europe where people eat paella and dance flamenco. Its capital is Madrid.
A football fan supports Barcelona and Real Madrid. In which country do these clubs play?
On a map of Europe, you see a big country next to Portugal in the south-west. What is its name?
The shop keeps its extra goods in a big building outside the town until they are sold.
The scouts put up their tents in the forest and spend the night there.
You keep old wine bottles in a cool dark cellar. Which word means 'to store'?
There is only one painting like this in the whole world. No copy exists.
Your fingerprint is not the same as anyone else's. Nobody has the same.
A teacher says that every snowflake is different and has no twin. Which word means 'unique'?
After washing your hair, you use a small machine that blows hot air to make it dry fast.
In the bathroom of a hotel, you find a small electric device on the wall for drying hair.
A woman packs a brush, a bag of make-up and a small device for blowing warm air on her wet hair. What is the device?
The city plans to build more bike paths and make the train network bigger over the next ten years.
A company makes its internet network faster and builds new towers for more customers. It is the growth of the network.
Your family builds a new room under the roof to have more space. This is the making bigger of the house. Which word means 'extension' or 'expansion'?

en: to investigate, to inquire, to find out
situations: The journalist spends weeks looking for facts about where the company's money went.
A woman wants to find out where her grandfather came from, so she looks at old papers.
After the strange noise at night, the neighbour tries to discover its source. Which word means 'to investigate'?
In summer, you eat small red round fruit with a stone inside from a tree, and spit out the pit.
On top of an ice cream sundae, there is one small red fruit with a stem.
A cake, called the Black Forest cake, has small dark red fruits between cream and chocolate. What fruit is it?
A man sleeps on a bench in the park because he has no flat and no money to rent one.
In winter, a charity gives hot soup and blankets to people who have no place to live.
The town opens a shelter for people with no home. Which word means 'homeless'?
After the race, a girl stands on the highest step of the stage and gets a gold medal.
In a lottery, one man's number was drawn and he gets a million euros.
At the end of the game show, the person with the most points gets the prize. What do we call this person? Which word means 'winner'?

en: to warn, to urge, to remind
situations: The library sends you a letter saying that you must bring back the book you borrowed three weeks ago.
The teacher raises her hand and tells the noisy class to be more quiet, in a serious voice.
The doctor tells you that you must stop smoking, or your health will get worse. Which word means 'to warn' or 'to urge'?
Your friend always has new, unusual ideas for gifts and paints beautiful pictures. She has a lot of this quality.
At a design company, workers are encouraged to think of fresh ideas and not copy old ones.
A teacher says that art lessons help children to develop their power to make something new. What is this power called? Which word means 'creativity'?

en: to hand over, to pass, to transfer
situations: At the end of the shift, the nurse gives the keys to the next nurse.
The old king gives the crown to his son in a ceremony.
You give the parcel directly into the neighbour's hands because the postman could not leave it. Which word means 'to hand over'?
At Christmas, your grandmother bakes small, sweet, flat treats in star and heart shapes.
You eat a small, round, sweet baked snack with chocolate pieces with your tea.
A child asks for something sweet and crunchy from the tin on the shelf. It is small, flat and baked. What is it? Which word means 'biscuit' or 'cookie'?
The sign says that you may park here for two hours. The rule allows it.
In the exam, you can use a calculator. It is within the rules.
A lawyer says the evidence can be used in the court. Which word means 'permissible'?

en: city centre, inner city, town centre, downtown
situations: On Saturday, you take the tram to the middle of the city where all the big shops, cafes and the old church are.
Cars are not allowed in the central area of the city. Only people on foot and bikes can go there.
Tourists ask where the middle part of the town is, with the main square and many restaurants. What do you call this area? Which word means 'city centre'?
Someone asks if the new phone is better than the old one. You answer: 'Yes, there is no doubt about it.'
Your friend asks, 'Will she win the competition?' You say: 'Of course, she is the best singer.'
A reporter writes that the player is the best of his time, and nobody doubts it. Which word means 'undoubtedly'?
On the football pitch, the referee puts a small metal tool to his lips and makes a sharp sound to stop the game.
A man walks along the street in a good mood, making a tune with his lips, without words.
A kettle on the stove makes a high sound when the water boils. Which word means 'to whistle'?

en: wholemeal bread, wholegrain bread, wholewheat bread
situations: At the bakery, you ask for a dark, heavy bread with many whole seeds, which is good for your health.
A nutrition expert tells you to eat dark bread made with the whole grain, not white bread.
For breakfast, you have a slice of dark, healthy bread with cheese on it. It has lots of fibre. What kind of bread is it?
Before going out, a woman looks in the mirror and puts red colour on her mouth.
At the make-up counter, you buy a small tube of colour for your lips.
After a kiss, a red mark is left on a cup. It came from a coloured stick for the mouth. What is it?
The teacher says clearly, in so many words: 'Do not use your phone during the test.'
The doctor said clearly that you must not eat anything before the operation. It was no hint but a direct order.
The contract says in plain words that no pets are allowed. Which word means 'express' or 'explicit'?

en: to bellow, to roar, to shout, to howl, to bawl
situations: A lion opens his mouth wide and lets out a very loud, deep sound at the zoo.
A father shouts so loudly at the football match that his voice almost disappears.
A baby in the next room cries loudly and will not stop. Which word means 'to roar' or 'to bawl'?
A doctor on a health programme talks about how people who feel very sad should get help, because ending one's own life is never the answer.
A news article reports on new support lines for people who think about taking their own life.
In a health class, the teacher explains the word for when someone ends their own life on purpose. Which word means 'suicide'?
After many years, two parts of a country became one country again.
A group of fishing fans founds a club with members and rules. It is a formal group of people with one interest.
Two football clubs join into one. This joining together is called what? Which word means 'union' or 'unification'?
A young doctor decides that she will only work with children's heart problems in the future.
A small bakery stops making everything and now only makes cakes for weddings.
A lawyer wants to focus on one area of law only. Which word means 'to specialize'?
A scientist tests a new idea in a lab to see what happens. It is not proven yet.
A band plays strange and new music that is not like any normal song.
A theatre shows a play that is different from every normal play and tries out new ways of acting. Which word means 'experimental'?
The film begins with a man who loses his bag. Then he travels through three countries to find it. What happens in the film is called what?
The police say: 'The man did something against the law and we must judge his deed.' It is a thing someone did.
