A teacher asks you to tell the story of the book in your own words. What is the sequence of events in the story called? Which word means 'plot'?
Your friend is kind, funny and always honest. Everyone likes the way he is.
At the job interview, the boss says: 'We need someone with a strong, friendly nature.'
A famous singer attends the party and everyone wants to take a photo. In the press, such a famous person is called what? Which word means 'celebrity' or 'personality'?

en: to squat, to sit, to perch, to crouch
situations: The child sits low on the ground with his knees bent and looks at an ant.
Your friend spends all day in front of the computer. He just sits there the whole day.
A cat sits on the wall, ready to jump. Which word means 'to crouch' or 'to squat'?
A family leaves their country because of war and arrives with only two bags at a new country's border.
A volunteer helps a young man who had to leave his home country for safety and is now in a camp.
A school helps children who had to leave their home due to danger. What do we call these people? Which word means 'refugee'?
The man is not the mayor anymore, but he was the mayor some years ago. He is the earlier one.
A grand old hotel stands in the town. It was the home of a rich family once, but not any more.
A newspaper writes about the previous champion, who lost his title two years ago. Which word means 'former'?
The man who bought the house and has the papers saying it is his own is called the what?
A tenant says: 'I must ask the person who owns the flat if I can paint the walls.'
Your neighbour owns the shop and has the right to sell it. What is he called? Which word means 'owner'?
On Sunday afternoon, you sit on the sofa and look at the football game on TV.
Children stand at the fence and look at the builders working on the road.
A child does not join the game. She just stays at the side and looks. Which word means 'to watch'?
Your trousers are too loose, so you put a leather strap through the loops and close it with a buckle.
Your jeans keep falling down while you walk. You look for a long strap to hold them up around your waist.
In the shop you buy a black leather strap with a metal buckle, to wear around your waist. What is it?
On your laptop, you install a new program for writing documents and sending e-mails.
A technician says: 'The computer parts are fine; the problem is in the programs that run on it.'
A company sells programs and apps, not machines. These programs for computers are called what?

en: among each other, among themselves, one below the other, between them
situations: The children are sharing the sweets, and they divide them between themselves.
In the office, the colleagues talk with each other about the new boss, and nobody tells him.
In the old house, the flats are placed so that one is on top of another. Which word means 'among themselves' or 'one below the other'?
Two small companies decide to join together to make one big company.
A good leader makes people with different opinions work together as a team.
In the recipe, you must mix flour, eggs and milk into one dough. Which word means 'to unite' or 'to combine'?
After failing three exams, a student feels no desire to study any more.
The workers see that the boss never says thank you, and now they do not want to try hard any more.
A runner lost the race many times and now has no wish to train. How does he feel? Which word means 'demotivated'?
At a Sunday car show, an old shiny car from the 1950s drives slowly past, and everyone takes photos.
Your grandfather keeps a very old car in his garage and washes it every weekend. It is a collector's pride.
A tourist company offers a ride through the city in an old, restored classic car. What kind of car is it? Which word means 'vintage car'?
You applied for a job and now receive a letter: 'We are sorry, we chose another person.'
The organizers send an e-mail that the concert will not take place this year.
A friend invited you to a party, but you cannot come and tell her so. What do you give her? Which word means 'refusal' or 'rejection'?
A street performer in the circus throws five balls into the air and catches them again and again.
A clown on a bike keeps three burning sticks in the air with his hands at the same time.
You throw three oranges up in turn and catch them before they fall. Which word means 'to juggle'?
The jury looks at your work and checks each point on a list: neatness, originality and speed. Each such test point is called a what?
A university says: 'To be accepted, you must meet the following conditions.' Each is a test for deciding.
When you buy a car, you think about price, size and safety. Each is a standard you use to decide. Which word means 'criterion'?
Instead of asking you straight, your friend says, 'It is a bit cold in here', hoping that you will close the window.
You do not go straight from A to B but take a road with many turns.
The manager did not say it directly, but gave a hint through a colleague. Which word means 'indirect'?
The police ask you to describe all the facts around the accident: the weather, the time, who was there.
The doctor says: 'Under these conditions I cannot allow you to travel.'
The lawyer says that the situation around the event is important for the case. A single detail or fact of a situation is called a what? Which word means 'circumstance'?

en: to indicate, to point, to interpret
situations: A guide stretches his arm and shows with his finger where the old tower is.
A fortune teller looks at the cards and says what they mean for your future.
The sky is dark and the wind is strong. These signs show that a storm is coming. Which word means 'to indicate' or 'to interpret'?
In an old book, a waiter politely calls a young, unmarried woman with a polite title.
In an old film, a man bows slightly and says hello to a young woman with an old-fashioned title.
A very old-fashioned word was used for a young woman who is not married. Which word means 'young lady' or 'miss'?
After the storm, the damage to the roof cost a large amount of money.
The company made much more profit this year than last year. The difference is big.
The doctor says there is a big risk if you do not take the medicine. Which word means 'considerable'?
You think the hill is easy and take no water. But it is much harder than you thought.
The chess player did not think his opponent was good, but then he lost the game.
The company thought the work would take two days, but needed two weeks. They thought it was less than it really is. Which word means 'to underestimate'?
In the theatre, tonight is the first time that this play is shown to the public, and the actors are nervous.
Film stars walk on a red carpet at the first showing of the new movie.
The opera house shows a new production for the very first time on Friday. What is this first show called? Which word means 'premiere' or 'opening night'?
The news says that the number of people without a job has become smaller this month.
The shop owner worries because sales have gone down every month since January.
A chart shows the line for the number of cars sold moving down steadily. What is this going down called? Which word means 'decline' or 'drop'?
For you, learning languages is no trouble at all. Words stay in your head quickly.
A boy runs 5 km and finishes with a smile. It costs him no effort.
The teacher says: 'Maths is very easy for her.' Which expression means 'to find something easy'?
In a restaurant, the waiter writes down what you want to eat and drink.
You buy a jacket on the internet, and the shop says: 'Your purchase will arrive in two days.'
The farmer prepares his field and plants seeds in it in spring. Which word means 'order' or 'cultivation'?
The teacher shows a map and says: 'Look at the position of the town, the rivers and the mountains.'
In a quiz you must say where the highest mountain is. The questions are about places, land and maps.
A researcher says that the town has a good location on the map, with the sea close. Which word means 'geographic'?
Many offices stop using paper files and put all information into computers and online systems.
Banks now let people do everything with an app, and fewer people go to the bank.
A minister says that schools should change to using tablets and online lessons. What is this big change from paper to computers called? Which word means 'digitalization'?
After the concert, the workers take down the stage and the lights piece by piece.
The company decides to cut 500 jobs over the next two years.
You want to lower your stress, so you start to do yoga. Which word means 'to dismantle' or 'to reduce'?
The city was once full of factories, and now it is full of cafes and offices. Everything has changed.
A scientist says that the climate is slowly turning into something different from before.
A speaker talks about how society moves from one stage to another over many years. What is this process of changing called? Which word means 'change' or 'transition'?
The film was so bad that you say it was almost a joke.
The weather was so hot that it felt like a real oven.
Your friend says the price is absolutely crazy. Which word means 'downright' or 'virtually'?
You talk with your mother for half an hour on the phone about her trip.
At work, the boss says: 'I must make a short call with a customer, then we meet.'
Your friend sends a message: 'Let's have a talk by phone tonight at eight.' What do you call such a talk on the phone? Which word means 'phone call'?
The paint on the wall is not shiny. It does not reflect the light.
After running a marathon, you feel weak and without energy.
A photo printed on paper without a gloss has a soft look. Which word means 'matt' or 'dull'?
You are in a hurry and do not see the stop sign at the corner.
The teacher did not notice one mistake in the exam when she checked it.
You look through your bag for your keys, but they are right in front of you and you do not see them. Which word means 'to overlook'?
You cut your hair and dye it blue. Everybody says you look different now.
The company moves its office to a new building, and every day for the workers is different now.
A teacher notices that a student has become more confident over the year. What is this becoming different called? Which word means 'change'?
After four years, a young driver finally gets the official paper that lets him drive a car.
A new medicine gets the official yes from the authority so that it can be sold in pharmacies.
A student gets a letter saying that she is accepted to the university. Which word means 'admission' or 'approval'?
The sky is dark and you are afraid that the picnic will be cancelled.
The doctor says: 'I am worried that the test results may not be good.'
Parents wait for their child, who is late, and think something bad may have happened. Which word means 'to fear'?
After a long working week, you lie on the sofa with soft music and feel your body calm down.
In a spa, you sit in a warm pool and let go of all stress.
A doctor advises doing yoga to reach a state in which the body and the mind are calm. Which word means 'relaxation'?
A company uses only materials that can grow back and does not harm nature for the next generation.
A teacher says her lessons stayed in the student's mind for many years. The effect is long and strong.
You buy clothes that last long and are made in an environment-friendly way. Which word means 'sustainable' or 'lasting'?

en: crime scene, scene of the crime
situations: The police put a yellow tape around a house where a robbery happened, and experts search for traces.
In a Sunday evening crime film, the detectives arrive at the place where the crime happened.
A reporter stands in front of the garden where the burglary took place. What is this place called? Which word means 'crime scene'?

en: to strengthen, to reinforce, to amplify
situations: The workers put extra steel into the old bridge so that it can carry more weight.
The singer uses a microphone and speakers so that his voice is louder.
The football coach brings two new players to make the team stronger. Which word means 'to strengthen' or 'to amplify'?
In an old house, there is a very small room under the roof used to keep old boxes.
A castle has a small room where the king kept his gold and valuable things.
In the heart, the blood flows from room to room. Each of the spaces is called a what? Which word means 'chamber' or 'small room'?
The picture frame has four sides, all of the same length, and four right angles.
A chess board has a shape with equal sides and equal angles.
In geometry class, the teacher draws a shape with four equal sides. Which word means 'square'?
At the end of the month, you check how much money comes in and how much goes out of your account.
The minister speaks about the country's income, taxes and debts.
A friend says that she is not good at managing her money matters. Which word means 'finances'?

en: to lean forward, to prevent, to obviate
situations: You wash your hands often to stop an illness before it comes.
In the car, you move your upper body forward to see the screen better.
The doctor says that a healthy diet can stop heart problems. Which word means 'to prevent' or 'to lean forward'?
Instead of only talking about the problem, the mayor decided that now it was the time to do something.
A teacher says: 'Thinking is good, but we need real doing now.'
The firefighters act fast when there is a fire. What is this doing or acting called? Which word means 'action'?
You press the button and ask what this button does on your phone.
A new camera has a special feature that lets you take photos in the dark.
In a team, everyone has a task. The goalkeeper's task is to stop the ball. What is this task called? Which word means 'function' or 'role'?

en: to take advantage of, to exploit, to utilize, to utilise
situations: A rich man pays his workers very little because they have no other job. He uses their bad situation for his own gain.
A friend uses your kindness to get free rides every day.
You make full use of a sunny day by doing all the washing and hanging it outside. Which word means 'to exploit' or 'to take advantage of'?
The sky is grey and water comes down in drops all day. You put on your boots and take an umbrella.
A tourist is sad because the weather in London was wet for the whole week.
The forecast says clouds and drops for the whole weekend. What is the weather like? Which word means 'rainy'?

en: member of parliament, member of congress
situations: On TV, a man who was voted by the people in his area sits in the big parliament building and speaks about a new law.
A woman was elected by citizens to represent them in the national parliament.
Citizens write a letter to the person they voted for to represent them in the parliament. Who is this person? Which word means 'member of parliament'?

en: to one another, to each other
situations: Two friends say that they are always kind towards each other.
A couple has not spoken for days and no longer feels any closeness. They cannot find their way to each other.
The pieces of the puzzle fit together perfectly. Which word means 'to each other'?
Your friend always pays for everyone's coffee and says it is no problem. He does not mind giving.
A rich woman gives a lot of money for a new school and wants nothing in return.
A host fills your plate again and again and lets you take everything you like. This kind of giving is called what? Which word means 'generosity'?

en: to put together, to compose, to assemble
situations: You open a box from the furniture shop and join the parts to make a table.
The children take all the small pieces of the toy and build a castle from them.
A committee consists of ten members from different groups. How are such groups formed? Which word means 'to assemble' or 'to compose'?
At 7 p.m., the whole family sits at the table and eats soup and bread together after work.
A friend says: 'Come to my house tonight, I will cook the last meal of the day for you.'
In a hotel, the restaurant opens at six for the last big meal of the day. What is it called? Which word means 'dinner' or 'supper'?
A baby learns to grab small things with her fingers and to crawl. These are movements of the body.
A therapist helps a patient to practise movements of the hands after an accident.
The doctor says that this child's control of his muscles is very good. Which word means 'motor' when we speak about muscle control?
In an old western film, a cowboy aims at a bandit, and the bandit is shot dead.
In a history book, a prisoner is shot by soldiers, and the story is described in the lesson.
A detective story says: 'The man was killed by a bullet from a gun.' Which word means 'to shoot dead'?
You visit a country in the south of Europe with white houses, blue sea, the Acropolis and Athens as its capital.
In history class, you learn about the first Olympic Games and old philosophers like Plato. In which country did all this happen?
On the menu, you find feta cheese, olives and moussaka. From which country does this food come?
The weather report says: 'Today it will be 25 degrees.' Which temperature scale do most countries in Europe use?
In the oven, you set the temperature to 180 degrees. Which scale does the oven show?
Water freezes at zero and boils at 100 on a scale named after a Swedish scientist. Which word is the name of this scale?
At the library, you take a book home for three weeks and promise to bring it back.
Your neighbour asks if she can have your ladder for one day. You let her take it.
You do not have a car for a weekend trip, so you take one from a friend. Which word means 'to borrow' or 'to lend'?
After the earthquake, whole streets were broken, and houses no longer stood.
A child kicks down a tower of blocks that took two hours to build. The tower is completely ruined.
A report shows how the forest was cleared and nothing is left. What is this ruin called? Which word means 'destruction'?
The teacher says your essay was better than all the others. It gets the top mark.
The chef cooks a meal so tasty that all guests ask for more.
A critic writes that the film is the best he has seen this year. Which word means 'excellent' or 'outstanding'?
A ball hits the window, and the flat piece of glass in the frame breaks into pieces.
The cleaner uses a cloth and cleaner to wipe the flat glass in the frame so you can see through clearly.
In winter, the sheet of glass in the window gets covered with ice. What do we call this piece of glass? Which word means 'window pane'?
Every worker has the right to four weeks of holiday per year. It belongs to them by law.
The boy says: 'It is my turn, I deserve to go first.'
The contract says that the customer has a right to get his money back. Which phrase means 'to be entitled to'?
Your grandfather worked all his life as a carpenter, making tables and chairs with his own hands.
At a school fair, you can see old jobs like pottery, weaving and shoemaking.
A young person does not want to go to university but wants to learn a skilled manual job like a baker or electrician. What kind of work is this? Which word means 'trade' or 'craft'?
The old man says that the president in those days was very popular.
In an old photo, the car is of a model that was common long ago, but not now.
A book speaks about the king who was in power at that time. Which word means 'at that time'?
In a crime film, the police officer puts a metal ring on the wrist of the thief.
A magician is tied with a metal ring around his wrist, and then he escapes.
In a toy shop, a child asks for a police set with a badge and a pair of metal rings for the wrists. What is a single one called? Which word means 'handcuff'?
When you walk barefoot on warm sand, you notice a pleasant warmth.
She reads the sad letter and feels deep sorrow.
He says that he finds the music beautiful and feels joy while hearing it. Which word means 'to feel'?
At the aquarium, you see a big fish with sharp teeth and a triangle fin swimming above the water.
In a film, swimmers at the beach see a fin in the water, and the music turns scary.
A big sea animal with many rows of teeth is the top hunter in the ocean. What is it?
A person feels very sad for many weeks, has no energy and no joy, and goes to a doctor for help.
A doctor explains that this illness is more than normal sadness and can be treated with talking and medicine.
A health magazine writes about a mental illness with long-lasting sadness and tiredness. Which word means 'depression'?
The heat in the bus is so strong that you cannot stand it any longer.
The pain in his tooth was so bad that he could hardly think of anything else.
The noise from the building site next door is too much to bear. Which word means 'unbearable'?
You warn a friend: 'Do not drive too fast, not even a little too much.'
You say: 'Do not expect too much from the exam, it is very hard.'
The soup is a bit too hot, much more than you can enjoy. Which word means 'all too' or 'far too'?

en: to shine, to glow, to beam, to radiate
situations: The sun is out and light comes from it brightly into every corner of the room.
The bride walks down the aisle with a very happy face. Her whole face seems to be full of light.
At night, the stars send out a clear light in the dark sky. Which word means 'to shine' or 'to beam'?
In July, the whole family goes to a big swimming place that has no roof, with lawns and a diving board.
On a hot summer day, children queue at the entrance of a place with lots of water and sun, not in a hall.
In winter, you swim in a hall. In summer, you swim in a pool under the open sky. What is such a place called? Which word means 'outdoor pool'?
Fans wave a colourful piece of cloth on a stick at the football stadium.
On the national holiday, a piece of cloth in the national colours hangs on a pole at the town hall.
At the Olympic Games, each team marches behind a cloth with its country's colours. What is it? Which word means 'flag'?
A child puts his hand into the cookie jar, and his mother suddenly stands behind him and sees him.
You run fast and just manage to get on the last bus before it leaves.
The goalkeeper jumps and gets the ball with his fingertips just in time. Which word means 'to catch'?
A woman says about her neighbour: 'He is a really nice person, an easy-going man, just a normal chap.'
Two men talk in the pub: 'That man over there is a funny chap.'
In a friendly, informal way, people call a man a what? Which word means 'fellow', 'bloke' or 'guy'?

en: sober, with an empty stomach, plain, down-to-earth
situations: The police stop a driver and want to make sure that he has not had any alcohol.
The doctor says: 'Do not eat or drink anything before the blood test tomorrow morning.' You must go with an empty stomach.
The manager gives a plain, simple, no-nonsense report with just the facts. Which word means 'sober' or 'down-to-earth'?
A big car company buys a small one and becomes its new owner.
After the old manager leaves, a woman agrees to take on his job and all duties.
A supermarket chain buys the shares of another chain. What is this purchase of a company called? Which word means 'takeover'?

en: to stroke, to caress, to pet
situations: You sit on the sofa and softly move your hand over the soft fur of your cat.
A mother moves her hand gently over her baby's head to calm him.
At the farm, children gently touch the nose of a horse. Which word means 'to stroke' or 'to pet'?
A football club meets once a year, and the club members choose the group of people who will lead it.
A large company has a small group of top managers who take the main decisions.
In an association, the chairperson and the treasurer lead the club. What is this leading group called? Which word means 'board'?
The new neighbour helps everyone: she paints the fence, carries bags and works in the garden with a lot of energy.
A young manager takes on tasks with a lot of drive and gets things done.
The village needs someone who is active and has energy to start the new project. Which word means 'energetic' or 'active'?
On a map, 1 cm means 1 km. A note at the bottom tells you this ratio.
A teacher says that the exam will be a standard to judge your level.
The company says that the biggest rival is the model against which they measure their products. Which word means 'scale' or 'benchmark'?

en: to open, to hit, to serve, to pitch, to whip
situations: In the library, you take a book and open it at page 50.
In tennis, the player throws the ball up and hits it to begin the point.
The baby falls and hits her head on the floor. Which word means 'to open' or 'to hit' or 'to serve'?
In a Sunday crime film, a detective finds a dead person in the garden.
The police report says that they have found a lifeless body in the river.
In a detective novel, the doctor examines the dead person lying on the floor. What is such a body called? Which word means 'corpse'?
The old school building has damp walls, so the town spends money to repair it and make it modern.
A company with a lot of debts makes a plan to bring it back into good health.
Workers spend six months making an old, run-down flat as good as new. What is this work called? Which word means 'renovation'?

en: to spread, to disseminate, to distribute
situations: A rumour about the teacher goes quickly from one pupil to another all over the school.
The news about the new shop spreads through the town in a day.
A virus goes from person to person in the city. Which word means 'to spread'?
You are new at the job and you are not sure if you are doing it right. You ask many questions.
At night, the street is dark and empty and you do not feel safe.
The weather is changing a lot, so nobody can say if the match will take place. Which word means 'uncertain' or 'insecure'?
In the cemetery, a family puts flowers on the place where their grandmother lies buried.
At the cemetery, you see a stone with a name and two dates on it, in the ground.
On All Saints' Day, people light candles at the place where their dead are buried. What is the place called? Which word means 'tomb' or 'resting place'?

en: to quarrel, to squabble, to bicker
situations: Two small brothers argue all day about who can sit near the window.
The neighbours often shout at each other over a small matter like a parking space.
The couple argue about the TV remote every evening. Which word means 'to quarrel' or 'to bicker'?
In the garden, you see a small body of water with fish and water plants, smaller than a lake.
In the park, ducks swim in a small pool of water and children feed them bread.
At the farm, there are frogs in a little round water body behind the barn. What is it? Which word means 'pond'?

en: comparatively, in comparison, by way of comparison
situations: The flat is expensive, but if you look at other flats in the same area, it is cheap compared to them.
This summer, the weather was rather cool when you compare it with last year.
Your friend says that the exam was not so hard when you compare it with the one before. Which word means 'comparatively'?

en: rate, interest rate, rate of interest
situations: The bank says that you must pay 5% extra each year on the money you borrowed. The percentage is what?
A news report says that the central bank is going to change the percentage that people get on savings.
You compare two banks for a loan. One offers a lower percentage cost per year than the other. What is the percentage called? Which word means 'interest rate'?
The shop has a sign: 'The entrance is closed for two weeks because of building work.' It is only for a short time.
A worker gets a contract that ends after six months. It is not a permanent job.
The company builds a small wooden bridge to be used only until the real bridge is finished. Which word means 'temporary'?

en: to complain, to bemoan, to lament
situations: Your neighbour tells everyone how bad the weather is and that nothing is going well.
The workers say in a loud voice that their pay is too low and hours are too long.
The old man says sadly that young people no longer visit him. Which word means 'to lament' or 'to complain'?
The line on the temperature chart goes up from 10 to 30 degrees in one week.
The news says that the number of tourists has become much higher this year.
On a bike tour, the road goes up a hill and you start to breathe harder. What is such a going up called? Which word means 'rise' or 'increase'?
In archery, the sportsman pulls the string of the bow and shoots a thin stick with feathers at the target.
On a road sign, there is a symbol that points to the left to show you which way to go.
On the keyboard, there are four keys with a symbol that shows up, down, left and right. What is the symbol shaped like? Which word means 'arrow'?
Your rich uncle never gives anything away. He does not spend even small amounts on gifts.
The shopkeeper counts every cent and does not give any free sample.
Your friend does not use the heating because he does not want to spend money, even if it is cold. Which phrase means 'to be stingy with'?
Your friend cycles through a flat country with windmills, tulip fields and canals. Amsterdam is its capital.
A football fan supports a team in orange shirts. Which country does the team belong to?
On the map of Europe, find the country between Germany and Belgium that borders the North Sea and is known as 'Holland'. What is its name?
The crowd in the stadium is shouting and cheering so loudly that you cannot hear your friend.
The people in the meeting protest with loud voices against the new plan.
A child demands ice cream in the shop in a very loud voice. Which word means 'vociferous' or 'very loud'?

en: time out, time-out, time off, break, hiatus
situations: After years of hard work, a woman takes three months off to travel and rest.
In a basketball game, the coach asks for a short pause to talk to his players.
Your friend feels tired and stressed, so he decides to take a break from social media and work for a while. What is this pause called? Which word means 'time-out'?

en: to take off, to put down, to file, to drop
situations: When you come home, you take your jacket and hat off and hang them on the hook.
The secretary puts the letter into the folder in the right place on the shelf.
A man decides to stop an old bad habit for good. Which word means 'to put down' or 'to file' or 'to drop'?
On a walk in the park, you meet an old friend by chance and talk for a few minutes.
The teacher organizes a day when school children and old people from the town meet and talk.
The two leaders of the countries are going to meet on Friday for talks. What is this coming together of people called? Which word means 'encounter' or 'meeting'?
The doctor says you have a sickness that will not go away and you must take care of it for years.
Your grandfather has had back pain for twenty years. It never fully goes away.
The news says that the town has a problem with no money that lasts for a very long time. Which word means 'chronic'?
On the pizza, you add small red pieces that make your mouth burn and your eyes water.
A cook says: 'Be careful with this red pod. A little bit makes the whole dish very hot.'
In Mexican cooking, a hot red or green pod is used in many dishes. What is it called? Which word means 'chilli'?
In the meeting, your boss says in one sentence that the office will be closed on Friday, but does not go on about it.
The teacher says in passing that the exam may be hard, but says no more.
You speak about your holiday and say, by the way, that you also visited the old castle. Which word means 'to mention'?
The doctor explains that the baby will not come in the normal way, so the baby will be taken out through a cut in the mother's belly.
A woman had a planned operation at the hospital to have her baby, and is now in bed for recovery.
A pregnant woman asks her doctor about the operation that is used to bring a baby into the world through the stomach. What is it called? Which word means 'C-section'?
At the end of the year, the company spent more money than it earned, and there is a gap of 2 million euros.
The state spends more than it earns from taxes, so there is a shortfall in the budget.
In the club cash box, you find that there is less money than expected. What is this shortage called? Which word means 'deficit'?
The police ask a witness to say who was the person in a photo of the crime.
The scientist looks at a plant and works out its name from the book.
The airport officer checks your passport to make sure that you are who you say you are. Which word means 'to identify'?
A father said: 'No sweets before dinner.' And he sticks to it every day, without exceptions.
The coach always follows the same rules for every player, no matter who it is.
The teacher punishes every late student in the same way, always. Which word means 'consistent'?
The teacher explains the basic rule behind how a lever works.
The man says: 'I never lie. It is my firm rule of life.'
The engineer explains the general idea on which the machine is built. What is this basic idea or rule called? Which word means 'principle'?
Your friend says: 'I cannot explain, but I feel that something is wrong with this plan.'
The door will not open, but you say, 'I will find a way to do it, I don't know how.'
How was the movie? You answer in a vague way: 'It was a bit odd, but I liked it.' Which word means 'somehow' or 'kind of'?
At the market, there are fifty different sorts of cheese, from soft to hard.
A school has pupils from many countries, with different languages and cultures.
A forest has many kinds of trees, birds and insects. What is this large number of different things called? Which word means 'variety' or 'diversity'?

en: to skip, to cut, to play hooky
situations: A pupil decides not to go to school today and goes to the park instead, without telling anyone.
Your friend does not go to the lesson because he is not in the mood, and he does not have a reason.
Some students do not turn up for the boring lecture. Which word means 'to skip' or 'to play hooky'?
The old woman slips on ice and lands on the ground. She has to go to the hospital.
The price of oil goes down very fast within a day. The news talks about a big drop.
A climber loses grip and falls down the rock. What is this sudden going down called? Which word means 'fall'?
The football match was exciting: three goals in the last five minutes.
The rescue of the boy from the river was so tense that the whole village held its breath.
The film has a very exciting, emotional ending that makes people cry. Which word means 'dramatic'?
Looking back at your life, you see that the day you met your wife changed everything.
In the football match, the red card for the best player was the moment when the game changed in the other team's favour.
A historian says that this battle was the moment after which the war went in another direction. What is such a moment called? Which word means 'turning point'?
He works so much that he never has time to give attention to his family or friends.
The owner never cleans the garden, and the plants die.
She forgot to do her homework and did not look after her duties for weeks. Which word means 'to neglect'?
The teacher writes the word 'walking' on the board and underlines the last letters, 'ing'.
In English class, you learn that the final letters of a word can change its meaning, for example '-ed' for the past.
At the end of a long word, there are a few letters that are added. These last letters are called what? Which word means 'ending'?
When you start your laptop, a basic program starts first, and on this program you can run all other programs.
A friend says that his phone is old and no longer gets updates for the main program that controls everything.
Windows, macOS and Linux are examples of basic programs that run a computer. What are they called? Which phrase means 'operating system'?

en: to move, to transfer, to relocate, to set, to stand up
situations: The company sends an employee from the Berlin office to the Munich office.
You move the bed from the left to the right side of the room.
She waited for him at the cinema for an hour, but he never came and left her waiting. Which word means 'to move' or 'to transfer' or 'to stand up'?
The story had no new ideas at all. It was just the same as many films before.
The designer made another grey office building like all the others. It had no original thoughts.
Your friend always gives the same gift: socks. He never thinks of something new. Which word means 'unimaginative'?
In a scary story, a red creature with horns and a tail comes from hell.
On a carnival day, a boy wears a red costume with a fork and two horns.
In many religions, the great enemy of God is called what? Which word means 'devil' or 'Satan'?
It is your birthday, so you say: 'Tonight, dinner is on me. I will pay for everyone.'
Your friend offers a coffee to everyone at the table and pays the bill.
At the bar, a stranger pays for your drink as a gift. Which word means 'to treat' or 'to buy' someone something?
The scientist sits in the forest for six hours and writes down how the birds behave.
The police watch a house from a car for days to see who goes in and out.
A teacher notes that a child often looks out of the window in class. What is such a careful looking called? Which word means 'observation'?
He is only interested in money, houses and cars. Things that you can own are more important to him than feelings.
After the flood, the family got help in the form of money and goods, not only words.
A report says the damage was not to people but to things and money. Which word means 'material' or 'financial'?
You visit a country in the west of Europe with a capital called Lisbon and a famous port wine.
A football fan supports a team in red shirts with a player called Ronaldo. In which country does the team play?
On the map of Europe, you find the country next to Spain on the Atlantic coast. What is it called?

en: to extend, to expand, to stretch
situations: The shop wants to sell its goods in more cities. It makes its business bigger.
The government is going to make the area of the park larger next year.
You pull a sweater, and the sleeve gets wider and loose. Which word means 'to expand' or 'to stretch'?
At the petrol station, the driver puts the pump into the big container under the car and fills it with fuel.
A fish owner buys a big glass container for his fish and water.
On a warm day, you find that the big metal container on the roof has no more water. What is such a large container called? Which word means 'tank'?
With a hot sausage, you put a yellow sauce on the side. It tastes a bit sharp.
In the supermarket, you take a small jar of yellow-brown paste to put in a sandwich.
At the German fair, a stand sells sausages and you ask for the sharp yellow condiment. What is it? Which word means 'mustard'?
The juice has no water, no sugar and nothing else. It is just the fruit.
The whisky is served alone, without ice or water.
The child has a look of complete, simple joy on his face. Which word means 'pure' or 'sheer'?

en: to make sense, to be clear
situations: The teacher explains it again, and suddenly you say: 'Oh, now I see why that works!'
Your friend gives a good reason for why he left early, and it seems logical to you.
You listen to the plan and think that the idea is clear and reasonable. Which phrase means 'to make sense'?

en: to come about, to bring about
situations: The two companies talked for months. Finally, a deal was made. How did it happen?
The meeting could not take place because too few people came. It did not happen.
How did this problem start, and how did this result come about? Which word means 'to come about' or 'to bring about'?
In maths class, you draw a shape with four equal sides and four right angles.
A chess board is made up of 64 small shapes with four equal sides.
The picture has the same height and the same width. Which shape is it? Which word means 'square'?
A dog sits when his owner says, and then gets a small snack.
A boy gets a new bike because he had very good marks at school.
The police promise money to anyone who finds the lost child. What is the gift for a good deed called? Which word means 'reward'?
If you take the shortcut, you do not need to walk for another hour. It means you avoid the extra work.
The mother tells her son that she will not make him go through the long talk about his marks.
With the new machine, workers no longer need to do the hard work by hand. Which word means 'to spare'?
On the news, the police say that the man who broke into the shop is a person nobody knows.
A man you have never met before suddenly speaks to you in the street.
In a crime film, a person whose name nobody knows leaves a message. What is such a person called? Which word means 'stranger'?
It looks as if the road is wet, but it is only the light. In reality, it is dry.
The man seems to be rich, but in reality he has a lot of debts.
From far away, the building seems small, but this is just how it looks. Which word means 'apparent' or 'seeming'?
In history class, you learn about a king whose long time as the ruler lasted forty years.
The people were unhappy under the rule of the strict dictator.
A country that was under the control of another country for a hundred years became free. What is such control called? Which word means 'rule' or 'dominion'?

en: to bend, to turn, to curve
situations: The strong man takes a metal bar and slowly makes it curved with his hands.
At the end of the street, the car goes to the right.
You gently make the branch curved but not broken. Which word means 'to bend' or 'to turn'?
The neighbours had a loud and angry talk about the fence between their gardens.
In parliament, two politicians have a long, sharp discussion about taxes.
Two football fans have a disagreement about who is the better player. What is this clash of opinions called? Which word means 'argument' or 'dispute'?
In the fairy tale, Snow White lives with seven small men who work in a mine.
In a garden, there is a small statue of a man with a pointed red hat and a beard.
In stories, a very small man with a beard lives under the mountains and digs for gold. What is he called? Which word means 'dwarf' or 'gnome'?
In a fantasy film, the hero puts on a cloak and nobody can see him anymore.
The wind is something you can feel, but you cannot see it.
Germs are so small that the human eye cannot see them. Which word means 'invisible'?

en: to lay out, to design, to interpret
situations: In the shop, the seller spreads out all the carpets on the floor so that you can see them.
The judge thinks about what the law means in this case and gives his own view of it.
The engineers plan the bridge so that it can carry 50 trucks. Which word means 'to lay out' or 'to design' or 'to interpret'?
After the blood test, the doctor looks at the paper and says: 'The report shows that everything is normal.'
The expert looks at the machine and writes down what he found: a broken part.
The patient waits for the written medical statement about the examination. What is it called? Which word means 'finding' or 'result'?
You sit on the terrace with a cup of fine coffee and a piece of cake and feel real joy in each bite.
The wine expert says: 'This wine is a real treat for the senses.'
Your friend says that listening to music in the evening gives him great delight. Which word means 'pleasure' or 'enjoyment'?
The teacher asks: 'Do you agree with the plan?' The pupil says yes, with clear words.
The priest says in the wedding: 'Do you take her?' and the man says 'yes'.
A woman answers a question with 'yes' and shows that she agrees with it. Which word means 'to affirm'?
The table is made of thick oak wood and will last for fifty years.
A bank gives a loan to a company whose accounts are in good order and reliable.
The old house has thick walls and a strong roof and does not break easily. Which word means 'solid' or 'sturdy'?
In anger, the man closes his fingers tightly into a ball and hits the table.
At the boxing match, the boxer holds his hands in the shape of a tight ball and hits the other boxer.
A child, to show that he is strong, closes his hand and holds it up. What is a closed hand called? Which word means 'fist'?
At the airport, the family waits with flowers and a big sign to welcome their cousin.
At the beginning of the conference, the director says a few friendly words to the guests.
When you meet your boss in the morning, you say 'hello' and shake hands. What is this friendly first act called? Which word means 'greeting' or 'welcome'?
After lunch, the children leave the room and go into the garden to play.
The cost of the project is much higher than planned. It goes over the limit.
The teacher says that your homework is not just good, but goes beyond what was asked. Which word means 'to go out' or 'to exceed'?
He was shocked at the sad news, down to the bottom of his heart.
She is very grateful and says thank you from her deepest feelings.
He says he is very sorry and feels it with all his heart. Which word means 'deeply' or 'profoundly'?
The gardener pulls a tree out of the ground and shows the long brown parts below the soil.
A plant needs water, which it takes from the soil through its underground parts.
In a storm, the old tree falls, and you see the big tangled brown parts that were in the ground. What are they called? Which word means 'root'?
The new manager says: 'The way we have worked up to now will stay the same.'
On the website, you see the changes from the earlier version to the new one.
The company says it will stay with its present supplier, as the experience has been good up to now. Which word means 'previous' or 'so far'?
You get up very early, go to the beach and watch the sun come up over the sea.
In the mountains, hikers start at five in the morning to see the first light of the day.
A photographer waits for the moment when the sun appears at the horizon in the morning. What is this called? Which word means 'sunrise'?

en: to conceal, to hide, to keep secret, to cover up
situations: He never tells his wife about the debts, and he hides the letters from the bank.
The company knows about the fault in the product, but does not tell the public.
A child breaks a vase and does not tell his parents. Which word means 'to conceal' or 'to keep secret'?
The weather report promises a warm day with clear sky and bright light from the sun.
A child draws a picture with a yellow circle and long lines on a happy day.
You say: 'Let's go to the park. The weather is great, with the light of the sun in a clear sky.' Which word means 'sunshine'?

en: to produce, to generate, to create
situations: A power plant uses wind to make electricity for thousands of homes.
The farmer's cows give milk, and the farm makes cheese.
Rubbing two sticks together makes a spark. Which word means 'to produce' or 'to generate'?
On a flight, a voice from the cockpit says: 'Welcome on board, we will land in two hours.' Who is speaking?
A boy dreams of working in the air one day, wearing a uniform and flying big planes.
At the airport, you see a man in a white shirt with four gold stripes who flies the plane. What is his job?
The milk was left in the sun for a week and smells so bad that you feel sick.
The toilet at the station was so dirty that you felt like leaving at once.
There was a hair in my soup, and I felt sick. Which word means 'disgusting'?
The doctor says: 'Take one small amount of this syrup three times a day.'
On a hot day, you take a quick drink from a bottle of water, only a little.
A child takes a drink of juice and then says, 'More!' A small amount of a drink in your mouth at once is called what? Which word means 'sip' or 'gulp'?

en: to question, to scrutinise, to scrutinize, to challenge
situations: A good student does not simply accept what the teacher says, but asks whether it is really true.
The journalist does not trust the official story and asks critical questions about it.
A manager says that you should not just follow old rules, but think about whether they make sense. Which word means 'to question' or 'to challenge'?
On the TV, the countdown goes 3, 2, 1, and then a tall vehicle with fire at the bottom flies up into space.
On New Year's Eve, people light a tube that flies up into the sky and explodes in colours.
A space agency sends a vehicle with an astronaut up to the moon. What is the vehicle that takes people to space? Which word means 'rocket'?
A young man in a green uniform stands guard at the gate of the army base.
At the memorial day, men in uniform march with their guns.
In a history lesson, the teacher says that millions of people in uniform fought in the world wars. What do we call a person in the army? Which word means 'soldier'?
The news of the accident was so shocking that nobody had ever heard of anything like this before.
The manager says: 'I have never seen a problem of that kind before.'
You say: 'I do not want to listen to talk of this type.' Which word means 'such' or 'like that'?
Every year, the number of people in the city becomes bigger.
The pile of papers on your desk is getting bigger and bigger each day.
The river becomes bigger after days of rain. Which word means 'to grow' or 'to increase'?
In a history lesson, you learn about the first people who lived in America before the Europeans came.
In an old film, people with feathers in their hair and horses live in tents on the plains.
A museum shows tools, clothes and art of the original people of North America. What do we call these people? Which word means 'Native American'?
At the market, a seller shows a table with so many fruits and vegetables that you do not know where to start.
The museum has a huge number of paintings, more than you can see in one day.
You say that the garden has an enormous amount of flowers in spring. Which word means 'abundance'?
You forgot to water the flowers for two weeks, and now they hang their heads and turn brown.
The roses in the vase become dry and soft after ten days.
In autumn, the green leaves become dry and fall off. Which word means 'to wither' or 'to wilt'?
The shop wants 500 euros for a plastic cup. Everyone laughs. The price is absurd.
The man wears a very big, strange hat and walks around proudly. People think he looks silly.
The reason he gave for being late was so silly that nobody could believe it. Which word means 'ridiculous'?
In a cinema, someone shouts 'Fire!' and people run to the exit without thinking.
A child is lost in the crowd and starts to scream and cry with fear.
The pilot says all is well, but a passenger is shaking with sudden strong fear and cannot breathe. What is this uncontrolled fear called? Which word means 'panic'?
At a press conference, a man stands in front of the microphones and tells reporters what the company thinks.
On the radio, you hear the person who reads the news every hour.
The class chooses one pupil to talk for the whole group. What do we call this person? Which word means 'speaker' or 'spokesman'?

en: for what, what...for, for which, which...for
situations: Your friend gives you a strange tool. You hold it up and ask: 'What is this used for?' Which question word means 'for what'?
A colleague asks for money. Before you give any, you want to know the reason: 'For what do you need it?'
You see a big box in the hall and want to know its purpose. You ask the question 'What... for?' Which one word means 'for which' or 'for what'?

en: to raise, to afford, to muster, to apply
situations: The village needs 10,000 euros for a new roof, and neighbours collect the money together.
After a hard day, you hardly have any strength left, but you manage to find the patience to listen to your friend.
The family cannot pay the high rent. They cannot come up with the money. Which word means 'to raise' or 'to afford'?
In June, you pick small red fruits with tiny seeds on the outside from plants close to the ground.
A cake with cream on top has many red heart-shaped fruits on it.
At the market, you buy a basket of sweet red fruits and make jam from them. What fruit is it?
You talk about a boy: 'He is an eight-... boy.' You put a word part between 'eight' and 'boy'. Which ending means '-year-old'?
A newspaper says: 'A 70-... man won the marathon.' Which word part means '-year-old'?
A form asks for the age of a child in a compound, such as 'a five-... girl'. Which word part means '-year-old'?
The doctor says: 'You must stay in bed.' This is a clear instruction you must follow.
The designer places the chairs and tables in the room in a nice pattern. This is how everything is set up.
The teacher says how the desks are positioned in rows for the exam. What is this positioning called? Which word means 'arrangement' or 'order'?
You push a lemon hard with your hands to get the juice out.
A child pushes a flower between two pages of a heavy book to dry it.
The worker pushes the metal into a shape with a big machine. Which word means 'to press'?
On the stage, a man in a tight suit moves gracefully to music and lifts his partner.
At the party, a young man moves his feet and body to the rhythm all night long.
A ballet company is looking for new male members who move to music as their job. What is this person called? Which word means 'dancer'?
In a crime film, the detective tries to find out who killed the rich man in the villa.
The newspaper reports a serious crime where a person was killed on purpose, and the police search for the culprit.
A judge says that the crime of taking someone's life on purpose gets the highest punishment. What is the crime called? Which word means 'murder'?
The menu has Italian, Indian, Chinese and Greek dishes, and many different kinds of food.
The job offers many kinds of tasks, from writing to talking to customers.
The city has a rich, mixed culture with many different events. Which word means 'diverse' or 'varied'?

en: to run for, to stand for
situations: A woman puts her name on the list to be chosen as the next mayor.
A man wants to become the head of the club and asks members to vote for him.
A local teacher wants to take part in the election for the town council. Which word means 'to run for' or 'to stand for'?
You drop your phone on the road, and now there is a thin line on the screen.
The new car got a long mark on the door from a key. It is a small damage on the paint.
The cat made a thin line on the table with its claws. What is such a mark called? Which word means 'scratch'?
A chef puts layers of pasta, meat sauce and cheese in the baking dish, one on top of another.
The workers in the factory work in turns: early, late and night. Each such working period is called what?
A cake has a thin sweet part between two other parts. Which word means 'layer'?

en: to regret, to deplore, to be sorry, to feel sorry
situations: You hurt your friend with a stupid joke and you say: 'I am really sorry about what I said.'
The company writes: 'We are sad that your parcel came late.'
He feels bad about his decision and wishes he had chosen differently. Which word means 'to regret'?
The pilot has flown for thirty years and has seen many situations. He knows what to do.
A new family looks for a nurse who has been working with children for twenty years.
The old carpenter knows every trick in his work and teaches the young ones. Which word means 'experienced'?
The mirror shows the picture of the mountain in the lake, upside down.
At the end of the year, you sit alone and think carefully about what you did and what you learned.
A teacher asks the students to write about their own thoughts after the project. Which word means 'reflection' or 'contemplation'?
In the church, the priest stands in front of a big table at the front and prepares the service.
The bride and groom walk up to the front of the church, to the big table with candles.
Flowers and candles stand on a holy table in the middle of the church. What is it called? Which word means 'altar'?

en: to complete, to graduate, to finish, to pass
situations: After four years of study, a student gets the paper that says she has completed her degree.
A young doctor finishes her training programme at a hospital.
The driver has to complete ten lessons and then takes the test. Which word means 'to complete' or 'to graduate'?
In the concert hall, a man in a black suit stands in front of the orchestra and moves a small stick in the air.
All the violins, trumpets and drums follow one person who shows them the speed of the music.
At the opera, a person with his back to the audience leads all the players. What is the person called? Which word means 'conductor'?
The boy is not adopted. The man and the woman are his own parents by birth.
She found her parents who gave birth to her after being adopted as a baby.
In the form, you must write if the child is your own by birth or by adoption. Which word means 'biological'?

en: to step back, to withdraw, to resign
situations: After the scandal, the minister announces that he will leave his post.
The crowd steps backward when the fire gets bigger.
The head of the club says she will give up her job at the end of the month. Which word means 'to resign' or 'to step back'?
On the map, you find a big continent with the Amazon river, the Andes and countries like Brazil and Argentina.
A football fan says that the best players of the world come from this continent: Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay.
You plan a long holiday to see Machu Picchu in Peru and the rainforest. Which continent do you visit?

en: of it, from that, from it, about it, thereof
situations: Your friend says that he has a new bike and you ask: 'Tell me more about it.' Which word means 'about it' or 'of it'?
The cake is on the table, and you say: 'Please take a piece of it.' Which word means 'of it'?
Your mother asks if you heard about the news, and you say: 'No, I know nothing about it.' Which word means 'about it'?
A teenager moves out and starts living alone, doing her own cooking and washing, and not needing help.
A man leaves his office job to start his own business and work for himself.
A country becomes free from another country and decides its own laws. What is this state called? Which word means 'independence' or 'self-employment'?
At the end of a long and boring lecture, many students open their mouths wide because they are tired.
At midnight, the baby opens its mouth wide and closes its eyes.
When you are sleepy, you open your mouth wide and take a deep breath. Which word means 'to yawn'?
Before building the new website, the team makes a first plan with ideas on paper.
The company wants a new idea on how to attract more customers.
The teacher says: 'Please give me your general plan for the project by Friday.' Which word means 'concept' or 'draft'?
Your boss says: 'It is possible to work from home, but let us look at each case.' It is allowed as a basic rule.
The teacher answers: 'Yes, you can retake the exam, if you follow the rules.'
A friend says: 'I basically agree with you, but there are details.' Which phrase means 'in principle'?

en: variety, sort, type, kind, flavour, flavor
situations: At the ice cream shop, the seller asks which taste you want: chocolate, vanilla or strawberry.
At the market, there are twelve kinds of apples with different colours and tastes.
In the supermarket, you can buy several kinds of tea. One kind is green tea and another is black tea. Which word means 'sort' or 'flavour'?
A child sits on a swing and moves forward and back through the air.
The clock's pendulum moves slowly from one side to the other.
The flag moves gently in the wind. Which word means 'to swing'?
Every evening, a girl writes down what happened that day in a small book with a lock, only for herself.
On a long trip, a traveller notes his thoughts and what he sees in a notebook each night.
Anne Frank wrote her private thoughts in a book each day. What kind of book is it? Which word means 'diary'?
The doctor takes your blood and sends it to the lab for a close study.
A company looks very closely at the sales numbers to find out why they dropped.
In chemistry class, you test a liquid to find out what it is made of. This careful study is called what? Which word means 'analysis'?
You wait at the airport for three, four, five hours because the plane is late.
The children play in the garden for many hours without stopping.
The meeting went on and on for hours. Which word means 'for hours'?
The soup tastes of nothing, so you add a small amount of white crystals from the shaker.
Before frying the potatoes, the cook sprinkles some white crystals on them.
In winter, the road workers spread white crystals on the icy road. Which word means 'to salt'?
The teacher explains the steps of the exam from beginning to end.
The manager writes a plan that shows how a customer's order goes through the company.
The date on the yoghurt shows that it can no longer be eaten after that day. The end of this time is called what? Which word means 'expiry' or 'procedure'?
Tourists take photos of the beautiful front of the old building with its many windows and statues.
The workers paint the outside wall of the house facing the street.
The old hotel has a nice front, but inside it is falling apart. What is the outside face of a building called? Which word means 'facade'?
In summer, you travel on a lake in a small boat which is moved only by the wind and a big cloth.
The racing team uses wind to take its boat across the sea.
On holiday, you learn how to steer a boat with a mast and a sail. Which word means 'to sail'?
A teacher's training is about how to teach children best and how to handle a class.
The school has a modern idea about how to educate young people with games and projects.
The kindergarten teacher studied the science of teaching and learning. Which word means 'pedagogical' or 'educational'?
At Christmas dinner in Germany, many families eat a big bird that is roasted in the oven.
On the farm, a big white bird with a long neck walks near the pond and makes a loud noise.
In autumn, a large wild bird flies south in a V-formation. A smaller bird is the duck. What is the larger one? Which word means 'goose'?
At the town meeting, many citizens joined in the talks and gave their opinion.
The company wants all workers to take part in decisions.
Only 20 percent of the people voted. The number of people taking part was low. Which word means 'participation'?
The boy takes your cheek between two fingers and squeezes it a little.
The crab takes your finger with its claw.
Your friend promised to jump from the high board, but at the last moment he says no because he is afraid. Which word means 'to pinch' or 'to chicken out'?
In chemistry class, the teacher shows the table with gold, iron, oxygen and many other basic substances.
A part of a larger system, like one piece of a set, is described as one such thing.
In an old belief, there are four basic things: fire, water, earth and air. What are they called? Which word means 'element'?

en: while doing this, in doing so, on this occasion
situations: The teacher explains how to use a new machine and says: 'While doing this, please wear gloves.'
You tell your friend about the repair work and add: 'In doing so, I broke a cup.'
The cook says: 'First stir the sauce, and while doing this, add some salt.' Which word means 'while doing this' or 'in doing so'?
The lawyer says that the company must pay because it was written in the signed paper between the two sides.
Your job paper says that you have thirty days of holiday. It is an obligation in the agreement.
The worker says his rights from the signed work agreement were not respected. Which word means 'contractual'?
The mouse goes through a small hole in the wall.
At the museum, you read the sign: 'The new exhibition begins on Friday. Doors will be open to the public.'
The doctor puts a tube into a small gap in the skin. What is such a hole or gap called? Which word means 'opening' or 'aperture'?
The judge gives an official command that the man must pay the fine.
The flower seller puts the flowers into a nice pattern in the vase.
The director tells all employees that they must stay home on Monday. Which word means 'to order' or 'to arrange'?
On Saturday afternoon, you have planned to see your friends in a cafe.
The boss calls all the staff to come together in the conference room at ten.
The club members come together once a month in the hall. What is such an event called? Which word means 'meeting'?
The old man does not buy a new coat although he is rich, and he turns off the lights to save a few cents.
The woman will not give a single coin to the poor, and she keeps all her money in the bank.
In a story, a rich man hates to spend even small amounts. This bad quality is called what? Which word means 'stinginess'?
On a new website, you give your name and e-mail so that you can have an account.
The student puts her name on the list for the course at the university.
The police write the licence plate and the time of the car in a list. Which word means 'to register'?
You read the letter quickly and not carefully, only looking at it in a short time.
The sun is only visible for a short moment between clouds. The moment does not last.
The police are looking for a man who has run away from prison. Which word means 'fleeting' or 'cursory' or 'fugitive'?
The country has a large force with tanks, planes and ships to defend it.
In the history museum, you see old uniforms of a country's land forces.
In many countries, young people must serve in the big armed force for some time. What is it called? Which word means 'army'?
At the fair, you buy a hot sausage from a small wooden place where a woman sells food.
The football score is 2:1 at the break. This is the current state of the game.
The news says: 'The level of the river is rising.' You ask for the current state. Which word means 'stand' or 'booth' or 'status'?

en: to list, to record, to register
situations: The company says that it noted a 10 percent growth in sales this year.
The librarian writes every new book in a list.
The weather office records that the temperature this summer was the highest ever. Which word means 'to record' or 'to list'?
Before you read the book, you look at the table of contents to get a quick idea of what is in it.
From the top of the tower, you can see the whole city and all its streets.
The manager asks for a short summary of the project's main points. What is such a short look at the whole called? Which word means 'overview'?
At the wedding, there was more than enough food and drink for everyone, and some was left over.
The farmer says that this year there is plenty of rain, and the harvest will be good.
She gave a very generous tip to the waiter. Which word means 'plentiful' or 'ample'?
The man in the court says: 'It is not true. I did not take the money.'
The politician says that the story in the newspaper is false.
Your brother says that he was not the one who broke the window, even though everyone saw him. Which word means 'to deny' or 'to dispute'?
In summer, small balls of ice fall from the sky and damage cars and gardens.
The farmer is worried that the storm will bring lumps of ice that will harm the fruit trees.
The weather report warns of a thunderstorm with ice balls the size of cherries. What is this called? Which word means 'hail'?
The sign on the shop says: 'After 50 years, we will shut our doors on 31 December.'
The government decides that the old factory will no longer operate, and the workers lose their jobs.
The school will end its work this summer because there are too few pupils. What is this ending of operations called? Which word means 'closure'?
Your grandfather shows you how to play chess, move by move.
The driving instructor helps you learn the rules of the road.
She helps her little brother to learn to ride a bike. Which word means 'to teach'?
The company sends adverts only to women over 40, because they are its main customers.
A good player hits the ball exactly into the corner of the goal.
The teacher gives extra help only to the pupils who need it most, with a clear aim. Which word means 'targeted' or 'purposeful'?
The army stands on a long line where two sides meet and fight.
On the weather map, a line shows the point where warm air and cold air meet.
The shop has a big window on the side that faces the street, and the building has another side at the back. Which word means 'front'?
The doctor says that the heart, the liver and the kidneys are important parts of the body, each with its own job.
A patient waits for a kidney from a donor for a new part in his body.
In biology class, the teacher draws the stomach, lungs and brain. What are such body parts called? Which word means 'organ'?
You say: 'I have been here before. I came two years ago.' Which word means 'previously'?
The teacher says: 'Please read the text first, and then do the exercise. Do this beforehand.' Which word means 'beforehand'?
On the day of the exam, you say: 'I had never been so nervous earlier.' Which word means 'before' in the sense of earlier?

en: to accelerate, to speed up, to hasten
situations: The driver presses the pedal, and the car goes faster and faster on the motorway.
The boss wants the project to be done sooner, so he hires more people.
The authority says that it will make the process quicker. Which word means 'to accelerate' or 'to speed up'?
In an old fairy tale or in the Bible, there is a very old-fashioned word for a woman. Today it can sound rude.
A teacher explains that some old words for 'woman' are no longer polite today, even if they appear in old books.
In a poem from the Middle Ages, you find a very old, now impolite word for a woman. Which word means 'woman' (and is considered derogatory today)?
The clown has a happy face, and the children laugh at his jokes.
The sky is clear and bright with only a few small clouds.
At the party, the guests were in a good mood and laughed a lot. Which word means 'cheerful' or 'bright'?

en: commissioning, start-up, launch, putting into operation
situations: After two years of building, the new power plant starts to work for the first time next week.
The technician sets up the new machine and begins to use it for the first time.
The new underground line will start to run on 1 March. What is this start of operation called? Which word means 'commissioning' or 'start-up'?
In the morning, the sun comes over the hills and the day begins.
The dough in the bowl gets bigger in a warm place because of the yeast.
The door slowly opens by itself in the old house. Which word means 'to rise' or 'to open'?
In a spy film, a man works for a secret government agency and collects information about other countries.
The news says that a state organization that works in secret was watching the foreign visitors.
James Bond works for the government's hidden agency for spies. What is such an agency called? Which word means 'secret service' or 'intelligence'?
The company will present its results for the months of January, February and March.
Each three months, the shop owner must send his tax papers to the office.
A year is divided into four periods of three months each. Each is called what? Which word means 'quarter'?
A teacher says that the main goal of the school is to teach children to read and write.
The most important reason to take the medicine is to lower your fever.
In the first stage of a plan, the most important thing comes first. Which word means 'primary'?
At the door of the club, the guard asks you to show a paper that proves who you are.
The government decides that a foreigner who broke the law must leave the country.
The police send a person out of the country because he has no visa. Which word means 'to expel' or 'to identify (oneself)'?
You go on holiday to a country with Istanbul and Ankara, with beaches on the Mediterranean and a famous kebab.
A tourist visits the Blue Mosque and the Grand Bazaar. In which country is this?
The country lies partly in Europe and partly in Asia, and its flag is red with a white moon and star. What is its name?
The teacher says: 'Sit up straight! Do not hang over your desk.' It is about how you hold your body.
Your boss has a clear opinion on the new rule and does not hide his view.
A dancer stands with a very upright and proud way. What is the way you hold your body called? Which word means 'posture' or 'attitude'?

en: to submit, to file, to lodge
situations: You send your application to the university before the date at the end of this month.
You give your tax papers to the office in an envelope.
The lawyer hands the complaint to the court. Which word means 'to submit' or 'to file'?
At a big conference, a woman sits in a small room with headphones and says in English what the speaker says in Chinese, at the same time.
The foreign minister meets the president, and a person next to him turns his words into the other language during the talks.
At the hospital, a patient does not speak the language, so a person helps by speaking for both sides. What is this person called? Which word means 'interpreter'?
She did it on purpose. It was not an accident.
After the accident, the man was awake and knew what was happening around him.
He knows that smoking is bad for his health. Which word means 'aware' or 'deliberate'?
After running for an hour, drops of water appear on your forehead and your shirt is wet.
In a hot room, the body makes liquid to cool the skin.
The athlete wipes the wet drops from his face with a towel after the match. What is this body liquid called? Which word means 'sweat'?

en: to return, to go back, to come back
situations: After two weeks on holiday, the family goes back to its home.
The soldier came back from the war after two years.
The teacher is ill for a week and then comes back to school. Which word means 'to return'?
On a map, you find a huge continent with the Sahara desert, the Nile river and animals like lions and elephants.
A tourist goes on a safari to see wild animals in Kenya and Tanzania. Which continent does she visit?
Egypt, Nigeria and South Africa all lie on the same continent. Which one?
The chef cooked an amazing meal, better than anything the guests had ever eaten.
The scientist has a very rare gift for mathematics, unlike anyone else.
The boss says the results this year were beyond normal, remarkably good. Which word means 'extraordinary' or 'exceptional'?
In history class, you learn about men from Scandinavia who sailed in long wooden ships and wore helmets with horns in the cartoons.
In a museum in Norway, you see a long old ship used by sea raiders a thousand years ago.
A children's cartoon shows a man with a big beard and an axe who sails to new lands in the north. What is he? Which word means 'Viking'?

en: to open, to raise, to wind, to come up
situations: The shop assistant pulls the curtains apart to let in the light.
A couple raises three children and takes care of them until they are adults.
You turn the key of the old clock to make it run. Which word means 'to wind' or 'to raise' or 'to open'?
On the phone, your mother asks where you are, and you say: 'I am in my own house, not out.' Which word means 'at home'?
After a long trip, you say: 'It's nice to be back in my own house, with my own bed.' Which word means 'at home'?
It rains hard, so you say: 'Let's stay in our own house tonight.' Which word means 'at home'?
In biology, the teacher says that a tiny living thing like a bacterium or an animal is called a living being.
A scientist studies how a living thing like a plant takes in food and grows.
The human body, as a whole living system with all of its organs working together, is called what? Which word means 'organism'?
The restaurant has a very good name among customers. Everyone says it is the best in town.
A person shouts a loud 'Help!' across the street to get attention.
The company worries about what the public thinks of it after the scandal. The opinion others have of you is called what? Which word means 'reputation' or 'call'?

en: to wipe, to swipe, to mop
situations: You take a cloth and clean the table after dinner.
On your phone, you move your finger over the screen to see the next picture.
The cleaner cleans the floor with a wet mop. Which word means 'to wipe' or 'to mop' or 'to swipe'?
Whether a film is beautiful depends on each person and his own taste. There is no right answer.
The judge says that the witness's story is based on personal feelings and not on facts.
A critic says: 'This is just my own opinion, not a fact.' Which word means 'subjective'?
In a fairy tale, a young man from a royal family kisses a sleeping girl and wakes her up.
The queen has a son, who will become king one day. What is he called?
In the story of Cinderella, a young man from the palace finds a glass shoe and looks for its owner. Who is he? Which word means 'prince'?

en: to steal, to nick, to pinch, to swipe
situations: A boy takes sweets from the shop without paying and runs away.
Someone took my bike from the front of the house when I was inside.
In a funny story, a little thief takes a loaf of bread from the baker's table. Which word means 'to steal' or 'to nick'?
The man was in prison for a crime he did not commit. This was a great thing that was not fair.
A child says: 'It is not fair that my sister got more cake than I did.'
The protesters say that the way that the workers are treated is something that is not right. Which word means 'injustice' or 'wrong'?
A father says to his daughter: 'I will come to your birthday, I give you my word.' What is this?
You say to your friend: 'I will keep your secret, I swear.' What do you give?
A politician says before the election that taxes will go down. If he does not do it, people feel cheated. What is such a pledge called? Which word means 'promise'?
A teacher explains that the word 'kid' for 'child' is used in daily talk but not in formal letters.
A dictionary marks some words as the kind that people use in everyday speech, not in formal writing.
'Cool' for 'nice' is not formal. It is the language of everyday talk. Which word means 'colloquial'?
After a long talk, the man says to the police: 'Yes, I did it.'
The boy says to his mother: 'I broke the window. I am sorry.'
The politician says openly that he supports the new law. Which phrase means 'to confess' or 'to admit'?
In the classroom, the children move around and cannot sit still before the holidays.
After the news about job cuts, the workers are worried and nervous.
The city is in a state of upset, and people are protesting in the streets. Which word means 'unrest' or 'restlessness'?
A child grows up in a happy home, with kind friends and a good school. Everything around him is positive.
A new employee says that the people and the atmosphere at the office are very pleasant. It is a good setting.
The doctor says that a person's surroundings in daily life, like family and work, have an effect on health. What is this called? Which word means 'environment' or 'milieu'?
You put a CD into the player and press the button, and the music starts.
On the computer, you click on a video to watch it.
The DJ starts a song at the party. Which word means 'to play' (a recording)?
At the doctor's office, you show a small card, so that the doctor's bill is paid by someone else.
Each month, a part of your pay goes to a company that pays for your treatment when you are ill.
In Germany, every person must have a plan that pays for doctor and hospital costs. What is it called? Which phrase means 'health insurance'?
The road is closed for two days for repairs, and then it opens again.
She has a short job in the summer, and it ends in September.
The pain will go away soon. It is only for a short while. Which word means 'temporary'?
A teacher says that the price of the car is far too high compared to its quality. It is not in balance.
