The scientist shows how two numbers are connected, such as the speed and the time.
The boss says that the salary should be right in comparison with the work that you do. Which word means 'proportion' or 'relation'?

en: to keep from, to prevent, to hold
situations: The rain stopped us from going for a walk. It kept us from leaving the house.
The school holds a big party every summer, and everyone is invited.
The noise from the street prevented me from sleeping. Which word means 'to keep from' or 'to hold'?
A very soft and shiny cloth, made from the thread of worms, is used for expensive scarves and dresses.
The old trade road between China and Europe was named after a very precious cloth.
A woman's blouse feels smooth and cool on the skin and is very costly. It is made from a natural fibre from a small insect. What is it? Which word means 'silk'?
Your friend asks, 'Would you ever lie to me?' You promise that you will not do it at any time in your whole life.
A child asks if she may cross a busy road without looking. You say firmly, 'No, not at any time, under any circumstances!'
Someone offers you a cigarette. You have not smoked once in your life and you will not start at any point in the future. Which word means 'never'?
You open the door and your old school friend, who lives abroad, is standing there. Nobody told you she was coming.
The forecast promised sun, but a heavy storm hits your picnic. Nobody was prepared for it.
A big bill arrives for something you did not know about. Which word describes news you did not see coming, 'unexpected'?
Your sister and her partner have signed the papers at the registry office and are now husband and wife. What do you call this official union?
An old photo shows your grandparents on the day they exchanged rings in front of the whole family. Their union lasted 60 years.
On a form, you must say if you are single or if you are in a legal union with a spouse. Which word means 'marriage'?
You have had the flu for a week with a high fever. The illness makes your body less strong every day.
In a football match, the coach takes off his best player. This makes the whole team less strong. What does the change do to the team?
Which verb means 'to weaken'?
You and your family want to travel through Europe, sleeping and cooking in a vehicle that is like a small house on wheels.
At a campsite you see a big vehicle with a bed, a small kitchen and a toilet inside. It is driven like a car.
For your holiday you rent a large vehicle that you can live in while you travel from place to place.
The doctor says you need a small medical operation tomorrow morning. It only takes twenty minutes. What do you call it?
Your neighbour keeps telling you how to raise your children. You do not want her to get involved in your family matters. You call this unwanted ____.
In a football match, a video review changes the referee's decision. Fans call it an unfair step into the game.
Your little brother takes the skin on your arm between his finger and thumb to tease you. It hurts a little.
Your trousers are too tight and the waistband presses into your belly. It hurts a little.
Your grandmother likes to take your cheek between two fingers and squeeze it. Which verb means 'to pinch'?

en: alleged, supposed, reputed, so-called, putative, ostensible
situations: A friend tells you that a famous singer is secretly moving to your town, but nobody has proven it. How do you describe this news?
The newspaper writes about a man who is said to have stolen a painting, but no court has decided yet. He is the ____ thief.
A market seller says his bag is real leather, but you doubt it. You use a word for 'claimed, but not proven'.
On a messaging app you can show that you are 'online', 'busy' or 'away'. What is this setting called?
You check your parcel on the post office website: it says 'on the way'. You are looking at the current condition of your order.
Which word means 'status'?
You lost your job last month. You go to a public office to register as unemployed and to get help finding new work.
Your neighbour has no work. He gets job offers and some money every month from a government office in town.
You are out of work and need an official place that helps you find a new position. Which word means 'job centre'?
At first, everyone doubted the new plan, but after one year it turned out to be very good. What did the plan do?
A friend did you a big favour. You want to do him a service in return to show him your thanks.
Which verb means 'to prove'?
You are building a bookshelf. You ask the shop assistant for a long, flat piece of wood.
On the old barn floor you walk on flat wooden pieces, and one of them is loose.
Your books stand on a flat piece of wood fixed to the wall of your room. What is it?
In a conversation, only one person talks all the time and the other one never gets a chance to speak.
A newspaper article shows only one side of the story and does not ask the other people. How would you describe it?
A friend says: 'This love is not equal. I like him, but he does not like me.' Which word means 'one-sided'?
You want to learn Spanish in the evenings after work, at a cheap local school for adults in your town.
Your grandmother joins a pottery class run by the town for grown-up learners.
Which place is called an 'adult education centre' in English?
In a TV crime show, a police officer sits with a witness and asks him questions about the night of the accident.
In a silent room you suddenly notice a soft sound. A formal way to say you hear it.
Which verb means 'to question' someone officially?
A tourist guide says: 'One unusual thing about this village is that all the houses are painted blue.' What is that unusual thing?
The doctor asks if your allergy has any special feature that other people's do not have.
Every city has something that makes it different from others. Which word means 'special feature'?
A photographer earns his living with his pictures. He has expert training and top equipment, unlike a hobby photographer.
The company hired a team that did the job very skilfully and in a businesslike way.
Which word means 'professional'?
Your grandfather needs help every day with washing and eating, so a nurse comes to look after him.
You rub oil on your leather shoes and clean them often to keep them in good condition.
A family takes in a child who cannot live with his parents for a while and looks after him like their own.

en: to judge, to assess, to estimate
situations: Before buying a used car, you look at it closely and try to work out how good it really is.
A coach watches the other team and tries to guess how strong they are.
Which verb means 'to assess'?
At the concert, the best song comes at the very end and everybody cheers. It is the most exciting moment.
A friend asks about your holiday. You say the boat trip was the best part of all.
In a film, the most exciting scene comes just before the ending. Which word means 'climax' or 'high point'?

en: if necessary, if applicable, where appropriate
situations: A letter says: 'Bring your passport and, if necessary, a translator.' Which word fits 'if necessary'?
On an application form you are told to add a second paper only in cases where it applies to you.
The teacher says: 'Ask me for help where appropriate.' Which word means 'if applicable'?
In a TV courtroom drama, the lawyer stands up and asks the judge to declare her client not guilty.
At a town meeting, you speak strongly in favour of building a new playground.
Which verb means 'to plead'?
A customer is so angry about a broken product that he takes the company to court.
The hotel room was dirty and noisy, so you write a letter to tell the manager how unhappy you are.
A neighbour goes to court because of a boundary dispute. Which word means 'lawsuit'?

en: diagonal, at an angle, oblique, sloping, slanting
situations: The picture on the wall is not straight. One side is higher than the other.
The roof of the house goes down steeply. It is neither flat nor vertical.
You do not cross the street in a straight line, but at an angle. Which word means 'slanting'?
Before your first day at a new job you feel nervous and doubt yourself.
Nobody knows if the factory will close. The workers do not know anything about their future.
Which word means 'uncertainty'?
The bus driver presses the brake and the bus comes to a halt at the stop.
The good weather went on for the whole week. What did it do?
A police officer raises his hand, and all cars must come to a standstill. Which verb means 'to stop'?
When the driver of a sports car presses the pedal, the car goes from zero to 100 in three seconds. That quick gain of speed is impressive.
In physics class the teacher explains how fast a speed changes over time.
A manager wants to make the whole project faster. Which word means 'speeding up'?
You book a flight and must choose which company, with its own planes and logo, you will fly with.
Your suitcase got lost after the flight. You call the company whose plane you took.
Which word means 'airline'?
Your friend will not walk under a ladder and is afraid of black cats.
A football player always enters the pitch with his right foot first, because he believes it brings luck.
Which word means 'superstitious'?
A young athlete trains hard every day because she dreams of the Olympic Games.
Many students work late every night. They try hard to reach the best grades.
Which verb means 'to strive'?
A driver was caught going far too fast. A judge says he may not drive a car for three months.
In some city centres, old diesel cars are not allowed to enter at all.
Which word means 'driving ban'?
Germany is made up of sixteen regions like Bavaria and Hesse. Each one has its own government.
In school you learn the capital cities of each region of a federal republic.
Which word means 'federal state'?
A feather touches the bottom of your foot and you cannot stop laughing.
Dad lightly touches the baby's belly with his fingers to make her giggle.
Which verb means 'to tickle'?
You put the pizza into the hot appliance in your kitchen and set it to 200 degrees.
Your cake must bake for an hour, so you heat up the big box in the kitchen first.
You are buying kitchen appliances: a fridge, a dishwasher and a hot box for baking bread. Which word means 'oven'?
At first you could not understand any German, but step by step it gets easier.
The sun is rising and the room gets lighter bit by bit.
Which word means 'gradual'?
Your grandmother does not use a mobile phone. She has a phone connected by a cable in the hall.
A phone company offers a package with a mobile plan and a home phone line. Which part is the home line?
Which word means 'landline'?

en: to be alike, to be just like, to equal, to resemble
situations: Your daughter has the same smile as her mother. She looks very much like her.
Two twin brothers stand next to each other. One looks exactly like the other.
Which verb means 'to resemble'?
You buy a bikini and you only need the upper piece, not the bottom.
You go shopping for a new shirt, blouse or sweater. It is clothing for the upper half of your body.
A pair of pyjamas has two parts: trousers and the part you wear on your chest and arms.
After dinner you save the food that is left for tomorrow.
You paid half of the money today. You will pay what is left later.
Which word means 'remaining'?
A boy sees a friend being bullied, but he runs away because he is afraid to help.
In a story, a knight hides in a barn instead of fighting. People say he lacks courage.
Which word means 'cowardice'?

en: to put together, to compile, to arrange, to compose, to assemble
situations: You choose songs and put them together for a party playlist.
For the meeting, you collect figures from several sources into one report.
Which verb means 'to compile'?

en: otherwise, other than that, apart from that
situations: You tell a friend about your trip: the hotel was noisy, but 'apart from that' everything was fine. Which word is it?
Hurry up, or else you will miss the train. Which word means 'otherwise'?
A friend asks how your week was. You had a cold on Monday, but 'other than that' it was good.
The shop assistant smiles, greets everyone warmly and helps patiently.
You thank your neighbour for being so kind and warm every time you meet.
Which word means 'friendliness'?
To make bread or pizza, you mix flour, water and yeast and knead the soft mass.
For pancakes you stir milk, eggs and flour into a thick liquid mixture in a bowl.
Mum rolls out the soft mass to cut out Christmas cookies.

en: to get rid of, to dump
situations: You have lots of old furniture and finally manage to sell the old sofa. Now you do not have it anymore.
You have had a cold for two weeks and you want to be free of it at last.
Which verb means 'to get rid of'?
Your grandfather has no hair left on his head.
In winter the trees have no leaves, only empty branches.
The room has plain white walls with nothing hanging on them. Which word means 'bare'?
At a funeral, six men carry the wooden box with the dead person inside.
In an old vampire film, the vampire sleeps in a long box.
A carpenter makes a long wooden box for a burial. Which word means 'coffin'?
You see your colleague's new sports car and feel bad because you want one too and cannot afford it.
A child looks sadly at another child's toys and wishes they were hers.
Which word means 'envy'?

en: to mobilize, to activate, to enable
situations: You buy a new SIM card and call a number so that it starts working.
The security company tells you how to switch on your home alarm.
A teacher wants sleepy students to get moving and take part. Which verb means 'to activate'?
Your hotel asks when you will arrive. You think about the day you travel to the resort, not the way back.
The festival website explains how to get to the place by train or car before the event begins.
Which word means the journey to your destination, the 'arrival journey'?
A shop assistant checks the shelf and says three sizes are still in stock.
The report says that no old documents can be found. Nothing exists.
Which word means 'available'?
A house needs a strong concrete layer under it to stand on.
The teacher says that grammar is the foundation of learning a language.
The contract is what our cooperation rests on. Which word means 'basis'?

en: to unsubscribe, to sign off, to sign out, to cancel, to deregister
situations: You do not go to the gym anymore, so you tell them to end your membership.
You finish with your email and click a button to leave your account and close your session.
You move to another country and tell the city office that you no longer live at your old address.
In a story, a friend secretly tells your secret to your enemy and you feel deeply hurt.
In a spy film, an agent sells state secrets to another country.
Which word means 'betrayal'?

en: to tear off, to tear down, to demolish, to rip off, to pull off
situations: The old, empty factory is knocked down by a big machine to make space for a new building.
At the end of the month you pull the top sheet off the wall calendar.
Which verb means 'to demolish'?
You change a setting on your phone to make the screen shine more or less.
In the morning the sun fills the room with light.
Which word means 'brightness'?
In a football match, the goalkeeper of the other team makes a great save.
Your team is on one side of the pitch. The team on the other side wants to beat you.
Which word describes the 'opposing' players?
In maths class you measure the space between two lines with a protractor. Ninety degrees is a right one.
A cat hides in the dark spot where two walls meet.
Which word means 'angle'?
The brakes stopped working at the worst moment.
In an exam, you freeze with stress and cannot do what you studied.
The engine does not start. What does the machine do?
Your grandfather worked for 40 years. Now he does not go to work anymore and enjoys his garden.
At 65, many people stop working and receive a pension.
Which word means 'retirement'?
You see wet streets and people with umbrellas. It seems that it rained.
Your colleague is not at his desk and the lights are off. It looks like he has gone home.
Which word means 'apparently'?
A small spider is in the house, but it cannot hurt anybody.
The dog barks a lot, but it is gentle and never bites.
Which word means 'harmless'?
The economy is divided into areas such as farming, industry and services. Each one is called a ____.
A newspaper writes about companies in the technology field.
Which word means 'sector'?
You keep looking at someone with wide eyes and cannot look away.
A child looks at the TV with an open mouth, not blinking.
Which verb means 'to stare'?
A man has just finished university and receives his certificate at the ceremony.
Companies invite people who just finished their studies to apply for jobs. Who are they?
Which word means 'graduate'? Use the male form.
The bathroom floor is covered with small, square, hard, ceramic pieces.
One piece on the kitchen wall is cracked, so you buy a new one to replace it.
Which word means 'tile'?
She goes to church every Sunday and prays every day.
A man fasts and goes to the mosque, deeply believing in God.
Which word means 'religious'?
A bad harvest brings about higher food prices. What does the harvest do to prices?
Heavy rain and strong wind led to the flooding of the street.
Experts say that stress is a factor that brings about many illnesses. Which verb means 'to cause'?
In the garden you dig a hole with a tool that has a long handle and a flat metal end.
In winter you clear the snow from your driveway with it.
On the beach a child plays with a small plastic one and a bucket.
After the main course, the waiter asks if you want something sweet like ice cream.
Mum made chocolate pudding for the end of the meal.
Which word means 'dessert'?

en: to cover, to put on, to overdraw
situations: You spend more money than you have in your bank account. Your balance is below zero.
You put a fresh cover on the pillow.
You put a jumper over your T-shirt because it is getting cold.
A newspaper uses a formal, old-fashioned word for the wife of the mayor.
At a royal dinner, the president arrives with his wife. She is introduced with a very formal word.
Which formal word means 'wife'?
The email says: reply at once, without any delay.
The shop promises to send your order with no waiting time.
Which word means 'immediately'?
In a history lesson you learn about the ideology of Hitler's party and the years 1933 to 1945 in Germany.
A museum shows photos and documents of the dictatorship in Germany during the Second World War.
A TV documentary talks about the Nazi ideology. Which word means 'National Socialism'?

en: to harvest, to reap, to pick
situations: In autumn, the farmer collects the ripe apples from the trees.
The wheat is ready, so a big machine cuts it in the fields.
A family picks strawberries on a field in summer.
During the pandemic, people lost the freedom to travel and meet because of new rules.
After a knee injury, there are many movements you cannot do anymore.
Which word means 'restriction'?
Grandma often says a short wise sentence like 'The early bird catches the worm.'
In English class you learn short, well-known sentences that give advice and have been passed down for generations.
Which word means 'proverb'?
The patient has sudden, severe pain and needs help right now.
There is such a bad water shortage that action is needed immediately.
Which word means 'acute'?
You make a soup, but it is too thin. You put in some more flour.
A cook tells you to put a bit more sugar in the bowl on top of what is already there.
Which verb means 'to add'?
You wake up and it hurts to swallow. You can hardly speak.
At the pharmacy you ask for lozenges because you feel pain in your throat.
Which word means 'sore throat'?
A friend asks, 'Can I borrow your pen?' You answer happily, 'Certainly!' Which word means 'of course'?
Your sister asks, 'Are you coming to my party?' You say you would not miss it. Which word means 'of course'?
A teacher says the exam is hard, but in fact you can pass it with some work. Which word means 'in fact'?
A bird loses a soft light thing from its wing and you pick it up from the path.
Your pillow is filled with soft light things from a goose.
Inside the mattress there is a metal coil that bounces back when you press it.

en: to notice, to say, to add, to observe, to let show
situations: You see from your friend's face that he is sad, even though he says nothing.
In a meeting you politely add one more small remark at the end.
Which verb means 'to observe' something about a person?
The last goal decided the whole match.
The most important thing for getting the job is your experience.
Which word means 'decisive'?
You feel very sad and stressed. You make an appointment with a man who studied the mind and talks with you about your feelings.
On TV, a man explains why people behave the way they do. He studied how the mind works.
Which word means 'psychologist'? Use the male form.
In a car you hold the round wheel with both hands to turn left and right.
On a ship, the captain stands behind the large wheel that turns the vessel.
The driver lets go of the wheel for a second and the car moves to the side.

en: to oblige, to obligate, to engage
situations: A football club signs a new striker by making him sign a contract.
The law says that all drivers must wear seat belts. What does the law do to drivers?
Your work contract makes you work 40 hours a week. Which verb means 'to oblige'?
In rich countries many families have a big house, cars and plenty of money.
Economists measure how well off a country is.
Which word means 'prosperity'?
The farmer grows vegetables without chemical sprays, only with natural materials.
In chemistry class you study compounds with carbon that come from living things.

On a national holiday, tanks and soldiers march through the capital for a big show.
The news says the government will spend more money on its army, navy and air force. Which word means 'military'?

en: to (have a) squint, to be cross-eyed
situations: The little boy's eyes do not look in the same direction, so the eye doctor gives him special glasses.
When you are very tired, you notice that one of your eyes turns slightly inward and you see double.
Your friend does a funny face and makes both eyes look toward his nose. Which word means 'to squint'?
The manager says the project is finished to a large degree, with only a few small tasks remaining.
The mayor announces that the city centre will be changed in a very broad and wide-ranging way.
A report says the new law has brought far-reaching changes to the whole country. Which word means 'extensive'?
At a restaurant, the waiter asks how you would like your thick slice of grilled beef: rare, medium or well done.
Dad lights the barbecue and puts big pieces of beef on the grill, served with fries.
You order the most famous meat dish from a menu of an American-style grill house. Which word means 'beef slice, grilled'?
At the end of the long hike, the little girl is tired, so her father lets her ride on his back with her arms around his neck.
At the playground, your friend jumps on your back and you carry him across the grass for fun.
Two children play a game where one is carried on the other's shoulders and back. Which word means 'piggyback'?
Your mother's mother proudly shows photos of the little girl, the daughter of her son.
At the family party, grandpa says: 'This is my son's daughter, and she is the apple of my eye.'
From the point of view of a grandmother, what do you call her daughter's baby girl? Which word means 'granddaughter'?
Your essay is a mess, so you make an outline with an introduction, three main parts and a conclusion to give it a clear order.
The new manager wants to give the departments a clearer order, with a clear chart showing who reports to whom.
Your desk files are a chaos. You sort them into folders and sections. Which word means 'to structure'?
You offer a package at the post office, and the clerk says, 'The receiving of parcels is at window three.'
A scientist says: 'We start from the idea that the experiment will work, but it is only a guess, not proven.'
The company announced it will no longer say yes to credit cards at the till. Which word means 'acceptance' or 'assumption'?
On a clear night in the desert, you look up and see so many stars that nobody could ever count them.
At the beach, there are so many grains of sand that you cannot give a number.
You have asked your friend the same question a huge number of times. Which word means 'countless'?
Your football team has a short saying on its banner that sums up its spirit: 'Together we are strong.'
The school party has a theme, and invitations say it is a short phrase like 'Night in Paris'.
A company puts its guiding sentence on all posters and says it describes its values. Which word means a short guiding phrase or slogan?

en: to separate, to break up, to part, to split
situations: After ten years together, a couple decides they no longer want to be partners and goes different ways.
At the crossroads, the group of hikers splits up; some go left and some go right.
You and your friends say goodbye at the station because your paths now lead in different directions. Which word means 'to part' or 'to split up'?

en: midpoint, focus, center, centre of focus
situations: At a birthday party, all the guests look at you, because you are the person everything turns around.
On a map of the city, the town hall marks the exact centre of the circle.
In geometry class, the teacher draws a circle and marks the point that is equally far from all edges. Which word means 'center' or 'midpoint'?

en: to meet, to get together, to come together
situations: Once a year, the whole family gathers at grandmother's house for a big dinner.
A rock band's old members will meet again for one night after twenty years.
The club members arrange to get together every Friday evening at the pub. Which word means 'to come together'?
You do not go to the cinema every week, but now and then, maybe once or twice a year.
A colleague says he sometimes works from home, not often, only from time to time.
The weather forecast says there will be rain showers here and there during the day. Which word means 'occasional'?
At night in the village, there are no cars, no voices and no music, and you hear nothing at all.
In the exam room, nobody speaks and you can hear only the clock.
After the storm, the lake is without any waves and the air feels peaceful. Which word means 'silence' or 'stillness'?
The teacher enters the room where thirty children sit at their desks facing the blackboard.
On the first school day, your child cannot find the room for her class on the second floor.
After school, the cleaner washes the floor of the room where lessons take place. Which word means 'classroom'?

en: to accuse, to reproach, to blame
situations: Your sister tells you angrily that it is your fault the cake was burnt, and you feel blamed.
In a TV courtroom show, the lawyer says the defendant is guilty of lying to everyone.
Your boss says you were late again and criticizes you in front of the team. Which word means 'to reproach' or 'to blame'?
You plan a trip to Madrid and Barcelona, so you start an evening course for the language spoken there.
In your class, the teacher asks you to pick French or the language of Mexico and Argentina.
At a restaurant, the waiter asks if you want the menu in English or in the language of Spain.
Pilgrims travel for weeks to a place that the religion treats with great respect and calls special and divine.
In the church, the priest says the bread and wine have a special divine meaning.
Tourists are told to take off their shoes in the temple, because the place is very sacred. Which word means 'holy'?
Your hair is messy after the wind, so you take a small plastic tool with teeth and pull it through your hair.
A rooster has a red fleshy part on top of his head.
At the hairdresser, she uses a small tool with many teeth to part your hair before cutting. Which word means 'comb'?
Your brother sits at the computer all night, typing lines of code to create a new app.
At the technical college, students learn to write instructions in code so computers can do tasks.
A robot arm in the factory does not move by itself; an engineer must write the software for it. Which word means 'to program'?
On a hike, you find a place high in the mountain where clear water comes out of the ground and starts a stream.
Your teacher tells you to write in your essay where you found your facts, such as a book or a website.
A journalist says he cannot name the person who gave him the secret information. Which word means 'source'?
You watch a play at the theatre. The costumes, lighting and way the director shows the story are praised by critics.
The newspaper review says the new opera is a modern way to show the old story on stage.
A famous director shows a classic play in a very unusual way. Which word means 'staging' or 'production'?
You watch a documentary about deep-sea animals and cannot look away, because everything is so interesting and amazing.
The museum guide tells such a gripping story about the old ruins that everyone listens closely.
Your friend describes a magician's trick that left everybody speechless. Which word means 'fascinating'?
A neighbor shouts that he will call the police if you do not stop the noise, and he waves his finger.
Dark clouds gather, and the forecast says a big storm is coming and may cause danger.
The company says there is a danger of closing the factory if sales do not improve. Which word means 'to threaten'?
Your friend says: 'I almost live at the gym, I am there so often.' He means 'practically'.
You finished the project, but only a tiny part remains, so you say you are 'virtually done'.
A shop assistant says the old model is 'as good as sold out', only two are left. Which word means 'almost' or 'virtually'?
The streets are full of posters and the politicians give speeches in every town, because the election is in a month.
On TV, two candidates argue to win more votes before polling day.
The news says the parties are spending millions on the weeks of trying to win votes. Which word means 'election campaign'?
While chopping onions, you slip and get a small wound on your finger.
The film editor says the final result of the film depends on how the scenes are joined together.
You ask the hairdresser for a new haircut, a short style with layers. Which word means 'cut'?

en: to switch off, to turn off, to shut down
situations: Before going on holiday, you press the button on the TV and the computer so they stop working.
After a long stressful week, you want to stop thinking about work and relax completely.
The engineer says that the old power plant will be stopped and shut down next year. Which word means 'to switch off'?
You climb the steep stairs to the space just below the roof, where old boxes, toys and Christmas decorations are stored.
In the old house, there are spiders and dust in the room above the top floor, under the roof.
The family keeps grandfather's old suitcases in the room right under the roof tiles. Which word means 'attic'?
Before the exam, your shoulders are stiff, your heart beats fast and you cannot relax.
After the argument, the atmosphere at the dinner table is uncomfortable and nobody smiles.
A doctor touches your muscles and says they are very stiff and hard. Which word means 'tense'?
Your uncle started a small shop that now has fifty employees and sells products across the country.
On the news, it says a large firm will open a new factory and hire workers.
A bank asks if you want a loan for your own business. Which word means 'company' or 'enterprise'?

en: to pass, to hand on, to hand down
situations: You read a great book and then give it to your friend so she can read it as well.
In the office, you receive a message from the boss and send it on to your colleagues.
Grandma gives her old recipe to her granddaughter, and she will give it to the next generation. Which word means 'to pass on'?
A small black insect keeps buzzing around your food at the picnic, and you wave it away.
At the wedding, the groom wears a black suit with a small cloth tie shaped like a butterfly at his neck.
On a summer evening, a tiny buzzing insect lands on your window. Which word means 'fly'?
Your grandfather worked in the same factory for many, many years, long before he retired.
After a long wait of years, the family finally gets a flat in the city.
The scientist did research for years before finding a result. Which word means 'lasting for years'?
In the football match, the team runs forward to score a goal, and the commentator shouts about the strong forward move.
In an old film about soldiers, the army moves forward to take the castle.
In a chess game, you move your queen to threaten the other player's king. Which word means 'attack'?

en: to cover, to meet, to satisfy
situations: Before dinner, you put plates, forks and glasses on the table.
The insurance will pay for the costs of your broken car, so the damage is covered.
It is cold, so you put a blanket over the sleeping baby. Which word means 'to cover'?
Your neighbor comes from Rome, speaks fast and loves pasta. He is a man from the boot-shaped country.
At the next table, a tourist from Milan orders an espresso and says he is from Italy.
The waiter asks which restaurant you prefer: Greek, Chinese or a man from Naples who owns a pizzeria. Which word means 'Italian' (a man)?
The exam is over, and the teacher hands out the marks. You want to know your outcome.
After the football match, the screen shows 2:1 as the final score.
The doctor calls you about your blood test. You wait for what the lab found. Which word means 'result'?
You are so happy that you struggle to find the right words, but you try to say what you feel.
A painter shows her sadness through dark colours, putting her feelings into a picture.
In a letter, you write thanks to your friend, telling her exactly what you think. Which word means 'to express'?
Your friend says: 'I mean it from my heart, I am really sorry.' You can see he is not lying.
At the wedding, the best man gives an honest and heartfelt speech, with no empty words.
A colleague tells you openly what he thinks, even when it is not pleasant. Which word means 'sincere'?
On the news, a reporter stands in Kyiv, the capital of the large Eastern European country with a blue and yellow flag.
In a geography class, the teacher points to the country between Poland and Russia, famous for its wheat fields.
Your neighbor comes from the country whose capital is Kyiv, and she cooks borscht for the party.
In the forest in summer, you pick small round red or blue fruits from a bush and eat them.
Your mother makes jam from small sweet fruits like strawberries and raspberries from the garden.
A bird sits on a bush and eats small sweet blue fruits. Which word means 'berry'?
The big dog shows his teeth and makes a low, angry sound when a stranger comes near.
You skipped breakfast, and now your stomach makes a low noise during the quiet class.
A grumpy old man mumbles an unfriendly answer under his breath. Which word means 'to growl'?
Instead of an electric oven, you use the usual old way of cooking with fire and a pot, as people always did.
The shop sells normal milk and also a new plant-based kind. You choose the usual kind.
A museum shows how farmers worked the land in the old standard way, before machines. Which word means 'conventional' or 'traditional'?
On the mountain farm, a small animal with horns and a beard gives milk for cheese.
A child at the petting zoo feeds a small animal that says 'meh' and likes to climb on rocks.
A shepherd has sheep and a female animal with a bell around her neck that makes milk. Which word means 'goat'?
A small baby bird has fallen out of the nest and cannot do anything to help itself.
You are lost in a foreign city, you do not speak the language and you do not know what to do.
The old man falls on the ice and cannot get up and nobody is near. Which word means 'helpless'?

en: to evaluate, to analyse, to analyze, to assess
situations: After the survey, the students collect all the answers and calculate what they mean.
The doctor looks at the lab data from your blood test and works out what it shows.
The company studies last year's sales figures to see which products sold best. Which word means 'to evaluate' or 'to analyze'?
The juggler throws five balls in the air and catches every one, showing how clever his hands are.
A surgeon needs steady hands and fine control to do a delicate operation.
At the fair, a game tests how well you can move a ring on a wire without touching it. Which word means 'skill' or 'dexterity'?
In a fairy tale, a man with a noble title lives in a castle and has many servants and land.
On a historical TV show, a nobleman who ranks below a duke arrives at the royal court.
A castle tour guide says the old owner was a nobleman with a title like 'earl'. Which word means 'count' in this noble sense?
At yoga class, the teacher says: 'Breathe in deeply, now let the air out slowly.'
On a cold day, you let air out of your mouth and see a white cloud in front of you.
The doctor listens to your lungs and says: 'Breathe in, and now breathe out.' Which word means 'to exhale'?
During the storm, a big part of the tree fell off and landed in the garden.
A little bird builds its nest on a thick part of an oak that grows out from the trunk.
The children climb the tree and sit on the strong part that sticks out from the trunk. Which word means 'branch'?
The teacher says that the year the war ended is a very important date to remember because it changed everything.
The scientists made a discovery that will have a great influence on future medicine.
The manager says the meeting is of great meaning for the company. Which word means 'significant'?
In a history lesson, you learn how the people of France rose up and replaced the king with a new system.
The news says a sudden and complete change has taken place in how people use phones, a total upheaval.
A whole old order of a country falls, and the people create a completely new one in the streets. Which word names this great upheaval?

en: to hurt, to ache, to pain, to be painful, to smart
situations: After running a marathon, your legs feel sore every time you take a step.
You hit your finger with a hammer, and it throbs badly.
The dentist says your tooth has a hole, which explains why it is so painful when you drink cold water. Which word means 'to hurt' or 'to ache'?
The company has an open job, and you apply for the position of sales manager.
At the night, a person stands at the gate of the building and watches who comes in.
The accountant looks at one single entry on the bill, such as 'office supplies 120 euros'. Which word means 'item', 'post' or 'guard'?
In the lab, the students mix two liquids in tubes, and the colour changes because of a reaction.
The label on the cleaning product says it contains strong substances made in factories, not natural ones.
A factory pollutes the river with waste from the production of dyes. Which word means 'chemical'?
You have a cough, so you go to a shop with a green cross, where a person in a white coat gives you medicine and advice.
The doctor gave you a prescription, and the person behind the counter reads it and prepares your tablets.
Which word means the person who sells medicines in a pharmacy?

en: to settle sth, to mediate, to arbitrate, to reconcile
situations: Two neighbors argue about a fence, so a calm person from the town hall helps them find an agreement.
A union and a company cannot agree on pay, so an independent person is asked to help end the dispute.
Two children fight about a toy, and the teacher helps them make peace. Which word means 'to mediate' or 'to settle a dispute'?

en: big city, large city, large town
situations: You grew up in a small village, but now you move to a place with millions of people, tall buildings and busy subways.
In a geography quiz, Berlin, Paris and Tokyo are all examples of this kind of place.
Your friend complains that life in a very large town is noisy and expensive. Which word means 'big city'?
Your grandmother gives you a gentle kiss on the soft part of your face under the eye.
When you are embarrassed, this part of your face turns red.
A baby smiles and you softly pinch the round part of his face. Which word means 'cheek'?

en: to lead, to head, to quote, to cite
situations: In a marathon, one runner is in front of all the others and leads the group.
In his essay, the student writes the exact words of a famous author and says whose they are.
The captain walks first and the whole team follows him onto the field. Which word means 'to lead' or 'to quote'?
The teacher says your essay has a good idea but needs improvement in the way the words and grammar are used.
A job advert says the candidate must have skills regarding foreign languages.
A research paper looks at differences between dialects. Which word means 'linguistic' or 'in terms of language'?
In a fantasy film, a strange creature with green skin and big ears appears from the forest.
Your teacher says you have a kind character, because your inner nature is friendly.
In a philosophy class, the teacher asks about the core nature of a human being. Which word means 'being' or 'creature'?
At the restaurant, the waiter asks if you want to pay together or apart, each person on his own bill.
You pack the shoes in their own bag, not inside the suitcase with the clothes.
The hotel offers breakfast, but the price is not included in the room and is charged on its own. Which word means 'on its own' or 'apart'?
Your neighbor goes to church every Sunday and follows the teachings of Jesus. What do you call him?
At the Sunday ceremony, the priest speaks to the people who follow the religion of the Bible's New Testament.
In a religion class, you learn about Muslims, Jews, Buddhists and followers of Jesus. Which word names a follower of Jesus?
The young pianist plays so well that the whole audience is amazed, and the jury is deeply moved.
You want to make a good impression on your new boss with your excellent work on the first day.
The magician's trick leaves the children with their mouths open. Which word means 'to impress'?
In physics class, the teacher says that everything in the universe, like stones, water and air, is made of tiny particles.
The professor explains the topic of the lesson and says it is a difficult field of study.
A scientist speaks about matter and anti-matter. Which word means 'matter' or 'substance'?
In the ice-cream shop, you cannot decide between chocolate and vanilla and keep changing your mind.
A voter still does not know which party to vote for, just days before the election.
Your friend says 'maybe yes, maybe no' for every question. Which word means 'undecided'?
You live in a small village just outside the big city, and every day you drive into the city to work.
The weather report says: 'In the city it is sunny, and in the areas around the city, there will be some clouds.'
The bus line connects the city centre with the villages and towns around it. Which word means 'surrounding area'?

en: to supply, to provide, to look after, to take care
situations: While your mother is in hospital, you look after your little brother, give him food and put him to bed.
The water company makes sure that every house in the town has clean water and electricity.
A nurse takes care of a patient's wound and gives him medicine. Which word means 'to supply' or 'to look after'?
In a scary movie, a pale man with long teeth wears a black cape and drinks blood at night.
At the Halloween party, your friend wears fake long teeth and says he is a creature of the night that fears garlic and sunlight.
In an old legend from Transylvania, Count Dracula sleeps in a coffin during the day. Which word names this kind of monster?
The government says that children should go to school and university, because learning is the key to success.
Your parents tell you that school and training are the most important things for your future.
A politician speaks about spending more money on schools and teachers. Which word means 'education'?
You visit your old school after twenty years and find that everything looks exactly the same as before.
The shop's opening times are the same as last year, with no change at all.
The doctor says your blood values are still the same as last time. Which word means 'unchanged'?

en: to transform, to convert, to change, to turn into
situations: In the fairy tale, the witch uses her magic to turn the prince into a frog.
The builder takes an old barn and makes it into a modern home.
In the lab, water changes into ice when it is very cold. Which word means 'to transform' or 'to turn into'?
During the lesson, a student says a short thing about the text, and the teacher thanks him for his comment.
The teacher writes a short note in red in the margin of your homework.
At the end of the meeting, your colleague makes a funny little statement that makes everybody laugh. Which word means 'remark' or 'comment'?
On TV, two politicians discuss and argue about the new tax law in front of the audience.
In the school class, students argue for and against school uniforms, with a teacher leading the talk.
A public talk is organized where people with different opinions discuss climate change. Which word means 'debate'?

en: to rule, to govern, to reign
situations: A king sat on the throne for fifty years and decided what happened in his land.
After the election, the winning party will lead the country for the next four years.
In a history class, you learn that a queen ruled the empire for sixty years. Which word means 'to rule' or 'to govern'?
The old farmer's hands feel rough, not soft, from years of hard work.
He answered your polite question in an impolite, unfriendly way, and everyone was shocked.
The sandpaper is not fine but has large, rough grains. Which word means 'coarse' or 'rude'?
You open a bottle of sparkling mineral water and hear a fizz as little bubbles rise up.
You like water without bubbles, so you ask the waiter for the kind without the fizzy gas.
The soda goes flat because the gas that makes bubbles has escaped. Which word means the gas in sparkling drinks (carbonic acid)?

en: to show up, to come up, to appear, to surface, to emerge
situations: A submarine rises from deep in the sea and breaks the water's surface.
You thought you lost your keys, but they suddenly appeared in your coat pocket.
At the party, your friend arrives unexpectedly after you thought he would not come. Which word means 'to show up' or 'to emerge'?
Your new washing machine breaks after one month, so the shop must repair or replace it because the law gives you this protection.
The seller promises in writing that the laptop will work properly for two years and he will fix any fault.
On the receipt, a note says the seller is responsible for faults in the product for a set time. Which word means 'warranty'?
The teacher says: 'Forget the past and the future, think about this very moment, the time we live in right now.'
A historian talks about the Middle Ages, then compares them with our time today.
A grammar book shows the tense used for 'I eat', not 'I ate' or 'I will eat'. Which word means 'present' (time)?
Before learning algebra, children need to know the simplest, most basic skills such as adding and subtracting.
The teacher says reading is a fundamental skill, a basic need for every subject.
In physics, a particle that cannot be split any further is called this kind. Which word means 'basic' or 'fundamental'?
You are angry at the broken toy and toss it in the trash can with force.
At the party, a child throws a snowball at his friend across the garden.
The goalkeeper picks up the ball and hurls it far across the pitch. Which word means 'to throw' or 'to chuck'?
The postman rings the bell and you walk down the hall to open the entrance of your house.
You come home late at night and search your pocket for the key to the main entrance.
A salesman knocks at the entrance of your house, and you see him through the small window. Which word means 'front door'?

en: as soon as possible, as quickly as possible
situations: Your boss writes in an email: 'Please send me the report with the greatest speed you can.'
The mechanic says he will repair your bike at the earliest moment he can.
You write to the bank: 'Please answer me quickly, as soon as ever possible.' Which word means 'as soon as possible'?
At the supermarket, there are a huge number of different cereals on the shelves.
A museum shows a great number of old paintings from many different artists.
The report says a large variety of reasons led to the company's problems. Which word means 'multitude'?

en: to consider, to take into consideration, to take into account, to bear in mind
situations: When planning the party, you think about the fact that your friend is vegetarian and choose food for her.
The teacher says she will take your illness into account when she marks your test.
The architect must keep in mind the budget when designing the house. Which word means 'to take into consideration'?
The squirrel hides a hard-shelled food in the forest for winter, and you crack it open with a tool.
At Christmas, a bowl on the table is filled with walnuts and hazelnuts.
A person with an allergy must not eat the little hard seed from a tree, like an almond or hazelnut. Which word means 'nut'?
Your new colleague loves to talk, explains everything clearly and keeps everyone informed.
A job advert looks for a person who is good at speaking and listening to others.
The manager says a good team leader should be open and easy to talk to. Which word means 'communicative'?
Your teacher says: 'It's raining cats and dogs' is a fixed saying that you cannot translate word by word.
In the language course, you learn a fixed group of words with a special meaning, like 'to break the ice'.
A foreign friend does not understand a common saying you used. Which word means 'idiom' or 'saying'?

en: to include, to comprise, to cover, to consist of
situations: The book has a thousand pages and contains all the poems of the author from three centuries.
The tour package contains flights, hotel and meals, all in one price.
The course consists of five modules, each lasting a week. Which word means 'to include' or 'to comprise'?
In the museum, there is an old clay pot from ancient Greece used to hold oil or wine.
A chemist pours the liquid into a glass container for the experiment.
Your blood moves through the body in thin tubes, like pipes. Which word means 'vessel' or 'container'?

en: car, passenger car, motor car, auto
situations: On the street, you see lorries, buses, motorbikes and a normal vehicle with four wheels for a family.
The tax office asks for the registration number of your private vehicle, not a lorry.
The parking sign says: 'Only for private vehicles for people, not for trucks.' Which short word means 'passenger car'?
You ordered a steak and got a cold one, so you complain to the waiter because you are not happy with the service.
Your colleague is not content with his salary and often says he wants more.
After the match, the fans leave with long faces because the team played badly. Which word means 'dissatisfied'?

en: to tell sb to do sth, to dictate, to stipulate
situations: The school sets a rule: all students must wear a uniform, and nobody can decide differently.
The law says that every car must have winter tyres in snow, and drivers have no choice.
A strict father tells his son exactly what he must study. Which word means 'to dictate' or 'to stipulate'?
The man in the story wants more and more money and cannot stop, even though he is already rich.
A child eats sweets so fast and wants even more, and cannot control his strong wish.
A teacher explains that the wish to have more and more is an unhealthy feeling. Which word means 'greed'?
When you move to a new country, you change your habits to fit the new culture and weather.
The tailor changes your new trousers a little to make them fit.
The company has to modify its software to the needs of a new customer. Which word means 'adjustment' or 'adaptation'?

en: to turn off, shut down, to park, to put down
situations: You arrive at the shop and leave your car in a space near the entrance.
Before you leave the house, you press the button so that the cooker no longer runs.
You come home with heavy bags and set them down on the floor in the hall. Which word means 'to park' or 'to turn off'?
The prices of houses go up without a break, year after year, at the same speed.
A doctor says your heartbeat is regular and does not jump up and down.
The river flows without stopping and always at the same pace. Which word means 'steady' or 'continuous'?
On the train, you put small speakers over your ears so you can listen to music without disturbing others.
At night, your roommate sleeps, so you wear something over your ears while you watch a film.
A gamer talks to his friends through a device with a microphone and earpieces. Which word means 'headphones'?
The union and the company sit at one table for hours to find a deal on pay.
On a TV crime show, the judge starts the session in the courtroom and the lawyers speak.
You and the seller discuss the price of the used car and try to agree. Which word means 'negotiation' or 'trial'?
While cooking soup, the recipe says to put a little more salt and pepper into the pot.
The teacher says everybody should put some money in for the class gift.
You taste the sauce and decide it needs more cream, so you pour some in as well. Which word means 'to add'?
At the circus, a funny person with a red nose, big shoes and colourful clothes makes the children laugh.
At a child's birthday party, a man with a painted face and a squeaky horn does tricks with balloons.
In a scary film, a creepy person with white face paint and a wig stands at the end of the street.

en: from what, from which, about what
situations: Your friend says: 'I had a long talk with the boss.' You ask: 'About what?' You want to know the subject.
You hear someone mention a mysterious plan, and you ask the speaker what it was about.
You ask where something came from: 'Which thing are you talking about?' Which question word means 'about what' or 'from what'?
In the cinema, you do not want to sit at the front, so you choose a seat at the back.
The kids sit in the last row of the bus, away from the driver.
The mechanic opens the part of the car where the luggage goes, at the end of the car. Which word means 'rear'?
Your boyfriend looks at another girl, and you feel a burning anger because you do not want to lose him.
Your little brother feels sad when your parents give more attention to the new baby.
A friend gets the new bike you wanted, and you feel upset about it. Which word means 'jealousy'?
A mosquito bit your arm last night, and now your skin feels like it needs to be scratched.
Your new wool sweater makes your neck want to be scratched all day.
The dog scratches behind his ear again and again because of fleas. Which word means 'to itch'?
On your phone you switch the setting so that no calls come through and the screen is dark, called 'night' something.
In a video game, you choose between easy way and hard way to play.
The washing machine has different settings for cotton and delicate clothes. Which word means 'mode'?
You want to see the northern lights and deep fjords, so you plan a trip to the Scandinavian country whose capital is Oslo.
The country that is famous for its salmon, Vikings and cold winters sends many skiers to the Olympics.
In a geography quiz, you must name the northern country between Sweden and the North Sea.

en: to cover, to uncover, to clear
situations: After cooking, you put a lid over the pot so the food stays warm.
Before painting the room, you put plastic sheets over the furniture to protect it.
After dinner, a waiter takes the plates and glasses off the table. Which word means 'to cover' or 'to clear'?
The milk was old and has a terrible smell that makes your stomach feel bad.
You ate too much cake and now you feel sick and nasty.
The weather turned out awful, with cold rain and strong wind. Which word means 'nasty' or 'foul'?
At the club meeting, the person who leads the discussion and speaks first is a woman or man chosen by the members.
The head of the board of the company opens the meeting and thanks everyone.
The leader of the football association welcomes the guests in his speech. Which word means 'chairperson'?
The bill is long, and the waiter says the total comes to forty euros.
The distance between the two villages is only five kilometres.
A teacher says the class size is thirty students. Which word means 'to amount to'?
The company enters all new customers into the computer system, so their data is saved.
The police camera records number plates of cars driving into the city.
The shop does a count of the stock at the end of the year and stores the numbers in a database. Which word means 'recording' or 'capture' of data?
The state says by law that every worker must have at least twenty days of holiday per year.
Before you buy the car, you check that the insurance is the one required by law.
A lawyer says the minimum wage is fixed by law. Which word means 'legal' or 'statutory'?
Your little brother watches a famous footballer and wants to be like him in every way.
A teacher shows students a perfect essay as something to follow.
Your grandmother worked hard all her life and you want to copy her way of living. Which word means 'role model'?
In your essay, you write the exact words of a famous writer and add his name.
The journalist repeats exactly what the minister said, using the same words.
In your thesis you must list the sources of each sentence you took from another author. Which word means 'to quote' or 'to cite'?
You live in a quiet area with parks, on the edge of the city, while your friend lives in the old centre.
The mayor visits different areas of the city to talk with people from each neighbourhood.
On the city map, Kreuzberg and Mitte are examples of this. Which word means 'district' or 'part of town'?
After school, your cousin spends three years learning to be an electrician, working in a firm and going to a school.
Your parents want you to learn a trade after school instead of going to university.
A baker's apprentice learns the craft in a company and at a special school for three years. Which word means 'vocational training'?
The tour to the castle is described as taking two hours; you say it is a two-... tour.
A teacher says: 'We will have a three-hour exam.' You describe the exam as lasting three hours.
A film that lasts four hours is called a four-... film. Which word ending means '-hour' in a compound like 'two-hour'?
The city decides that cars may only drive 30 kilometres per hour, to keep the speed low.
The teacher says each student has only five minutes to speak, so no one can go over.
You set a maximum amount of money you can spend on your holiday. Which word means 'to limit' or 'to restrict'?
You bring red roses wrapped in paper for your girlfriend's birthday.
At the zoo, the biggest bird in the world, which cannot fly but runs very fast, stands near the fence.
A florist ties flowers together with ribbon. Which word means 'bouquet' or 'ostrich'?
In the painting, there is a tree in the part closest to the viewer, and mountains far behind.
A photographer wants the child to be sharp and the background blurry, so the child is in the front part of the picture.
A politician says the most important topic should be at the front of attention. Which word means 'foreground'?
The hotel is cheap. Also, it is near the beach, which is another good point.
The flat is large, and what is more, it has a nice balcony.
You list reasons for choosing the car: it is cheap, and besides, it uses little fuel. Which word means 'moreover' or 'in addition'?
The boss approves the new product, and now it can be sold to customers.
You let your friends see your photos online, so they can open the album.
The police open the road again after the accident. Which word means 'to release' or 'to share'?
You sign a paper with your new company that states your tasks, pay and holiday. It is the legal link between you and your boss.
The lawyer says your contract of work ends in March, and then your link with the firm will end.
After ten years in the same firm, your link with the employer is still very good. Which word means 'employment relationship'?
The accountant says there are advantages for your company when it comes to what you pay to the state on income.
You can get money back from the government on your income because of this kind of reasons.
The new law has changes about the money people pay to the state from their earnings. Which word means 'tax' (adjective), 'related to taxes'?
The athlete was getting better, but a knee injury forced him to stop training for months and slowed him down.
The company lost a big customer, which was a problem on its way to success.
After good progress, the patient gets a fever and the recovery goes backwards. Which word means 'setback'?
The boy stands at the edge of the diving board for a long time, not sure whether to jump.
You hold the phone but wait before you press the button to call, because you are unsure.
Do not wait too long; if you pause and delay before answering, you lose your chance. Which word means 'to hesitate'?
As a new university student in a foreign city, you rent a small room in a big building with other students and a shared kitchen.
A nurse lives in a building where many people have their own room, but they share bathrooms.
The city builds a large house with many small rooms for young people who study. Which word means 'dormitory'?
After the questionnaire, the researchers study all the answers and write a report.
The coach looks at the video of the match to check what went wrong.
The lab sends you a document with the study of your test numbers. Which word means 'evaluation' or 'analysis'?
At the wedding, the bride wears a quiet pale lipstick and simple jewellery, nothing loud.
The waiter coughs softly to let you know the bill is ready, not disturbing anyone.
The room has soft lighting and a light, gentle perfume. Which word means 'discreet' or 'subtle'?
After the operation, your grandfather walks with a stick that helps hold his weight.
Strong walls hold up the roof of the old house so it does not fall.
Your parents help you with money while you study. Which word means 'to support'?
In a crime film, a child is taken away by strangers who demand money from his parents.
The news reports that masked men took a plane under their control and forced it to land elsewhere.
A woman is taken away by force in a thriller. Which word means 'kidnapping' or 'abduction'?
Someone hit your car in the car park, and now there is a small hollow in the metal door.
The tin can fell on the floor and has a little hollow on its side.
Your bicycle fell, and the metal mudguard now has a small hollow in it. Which word means 'dent'?
The fox ran away just in time and the hunter could not catch him.
You are so busy that a small mistake in the text does not get noticed by you.
The thief managed to get away from the police. Which word means 'to escape' (to slip away from)?
The manual of the new machine has several hundred pages and covers every detail.
The company made a very large and thorough plan for the new office.
The report is long and includes a lot of information. Which word means 'extensive'?

en: misconception, misbelief, erroneous belief, mistaken belief
situations: Many people believe that we use only ten percent of our brain, but scientists say this is not true.
A teacher says it is a wrong belief that lightning never strikes the same place twice.
Your grandfather thinks that cold weather itself gives you a cold, a widespread mistaken idea. Which word means 'misconception'?
Your new shoes are too tight and give you a blister on the back part of your foot.
A ballet dancer lifts her foot and stands on her toes, and the back part touches the air.
The doctor presses on the back of your foot and asks if it hurts. Which word means 'heel'?
Snow falls all night and lies over the whole field in the morning.
A mother puts a blanket over her child to keep him warm.
A cloth lies on the table, spread over the whole surface. Which word means 'to cover'?
Every spring you fill in a form for the government about how much money you earned last year.
Your accountant says you must send in your papers about income before the end of July.
You get a refund because you handed in a form to the tax office about your earnings and costs. Which word means 'tax return'?
At the language school, the teacher asks you to speak the language of London and New York.
On the menu, there is a breakfast with bacon, eggs and beans of the country whose capital is London.
The book is not German or French, but written in the language of Shakespeare. Which word means 'English'?
The newspaper says that a man stole a lot of money and hurt someone. The police are looking for him.
In a detective series, the inspector has to find out who did the illegal deed.
Murder, robbery and fraud are all examples of this. Which word means 'crime'?
You meet a friend at a cafe and talk about nothing special for an hour, relaxed and friendly.
The neighbors stand at the fence and chat about the weather and the children.
At a party, you have a light conversation with people you just met. Which word means 'to chat'?
The cinema is nearly full; only two seats are free.
The project is almost finished, with just a few small details missing.
You say: 'I have virtually no money left in my wallet.' Which word means 'almost' or 'nearly'?
At the swimming pool, a boy goes up to the high board and does a big leap into the water.
A long jumper flies through the air and lands in the sand pit.
You notice a thin line in your window glass, a small crack. Which word means 'jump' or 'crack'?

en: to hop, to jump, to skip, to bounce, to leap
situations: The little girl moves around on one foot in the playground, playing a game on the pavement.
A rabbit moves across the meadow with short quick leaps.
Children bounce up and down on the trampoline with joy. Which word means 'to hop' or 'to skip'?
A man calls the referee a very rude name in front of everyone, and he gets a red card.
In an argument, your neighbor says hurtful things about your family, and you feel offended.
A lawyer says the words used in the angry email were a rude attack on someone's honour. Which word means 'insult'?
The architect says the building is not only useful, but also pleasing to the eye and beautifully designed.
You choose the vase because of its lovely shape and the pretty way it looks.
The art teacher talks about what makes a painting beautiful. Which word means 'aesthetic'?
On the news, people walk through the streets with signs and shout slogans for a cause.
A man in a crowd holds a banner against the closing of the hospital.
The police talk to a woman who stands in a protest march. Which word means 'demonstrator'?
The mechanic puts a tool against the screw to begin turning it.
The company sets the price for the house at about 300,000 euros, as an estimate.
The teacher plans two hours for the exam and fixes the time. Which word means 'to position' or 'to estimate'?
In a horoscope, the sign shown by a man carrying a jug of water, for people born in late January or February, is described.
Your friend was born on 5 February and reads that this star sign is creative and independent.
In the zodiac, the sign that follows Capricorn is shown as a person pouring water. Which word means 'Aquarius'?
The Pope lives in the smallest country in the world, inside the city of Rome.
Tourists queue to visit St Peter's Basilica and the Sistine Chapel, which are in the tiny state in Rome.
The head of the Catholic Church lives in a small independent state surrounded by Italy. Which word means 'Vatican'?
The champion plays so much better than his opponent that the match is easy for him.
The new phone is better in every way than the old model.
Your team has stronger players, and you are sure of winning. Which word means 'superior'?
The scientist says that smoking and lung disease have a link, and one is linked to the other.
Your headache and the lack of sleep are probably related to each other.
The two events in the story are tied together somehow. Which word means 'to be connected' or 'to correlate'?
Joy, anger, fear and sadness are all examples of strong feelings that you can show with your face.
At the film's end, the actor cried and showed his deep feeling, and the audience felt it too.
A psychologist asks you to talk about your inner feelings. Which word means a strong feeling like joy or anger?
The hikers cross rough land with hills and stones and need strong boots.
A company buys a big piece of land on which it will build a factory.
The school owns a large area including a sports field and a garden. Which word means 'terrain' or 'grounds'?
In the morning, you stand in front of the mirror and run a small tool with teeth through your wet hair.
The mother carefully pulls the tool through her daughter's long hair to remove knots.
The barber arranges your hair before cutting it. Which word means 'to comb'?
The winner receives a medal that shines yellow and is made of a precious metal.
On the ring, the colour of the wedding band is like the sun.
In autumn, the field of wheat looks like the colour of shiny yellow treasure. Which word means 'gold' (coloured or made of gold)?
The doctor puts a cuff on your arm and takes a reading of your blood pressure.
The weatherman uses instruments to find out how hot the air is, and writes the numbers down.
The engineer checks the length of the room with a tape. Which word means 'measurement'?
Two countries sign a paper to stop trading fees on each other's goods.
After long talks, the companies arrive at a written deal about the sharing of profit.
A treaty between nations is signed in a big hall. Which word means 'agreement'?
It is raining, so you tell the visitor at the door: 'Please step inside, do not stand outside.'
The teacher says: 'Knock first, and then enter the room quietly.'
A customer walks through the shop door and the bell rings. Which word means 'to come in'?
After the earthquake, people suffer and lose their homes, and the charity wants to reduce their pain.
A grandmother says: 'I have seen so much sadness and pain in my life.'
A kind person tries to help those who are suffering. Which word means 'sorrow' or 'suffering'?

en: on top of each other, on each other, after each other
situations: The children build a tower by putting one block over another, higher and higher.
The two cars drove one right after the other, very close.
At the party, they look at each other and smile; the guests stack their coats on top of each other. Which word means 'on top of each other' or 'on each other'?
The teacher says: 'Only write information that matters for the question; do not add things that do not matter.'
The lawyer says this document is important for the case and connected to it.
For your job application, you should list only experience that fits the job. Which word means 'important for the topic' or 'connected to the matter'?
The singer's surprise wedding caused a big stir in the newspapers.
A strange new building in the city makes everyone talk and look.
The scientist's discovery created a great public excitement. Which word means 'sensation' or 'stir'?

en: to surround, to enclose, to encircle
situations: A high wall goes all the way around the garden.
The castle has a deep ditch full of water on all sides.
Mountains stand on all sides of the small village. Which word means 'to surround'?
The golfer wins the tournament and receives a big cheque for coming first.
The talent show gives the winner 10,000 euros as a reward.
A chess player says he plays only for the money he will receive when he wins. Which word means 'prize money'?

en: foreign minister, Secretary of State, Foreign Secretary
situations: On the news, the person in the government who deals with relations with other countries meets his colleagues abroad.
The politician who travels around the world to discuss peace talks and trade with other nations arrives at the airport.
Which word names the government minister responsible for foreign affairs?
You have a cold, and you take a tissue and clean your nose with a loud noise.
The nurse hands you a tissue because your nose is running.
In a quiet restaurant, you turn aside and use a handkerchief on your nose. Which word means 'to blow one's nose'?
The woman shows her pass and says she has the right to enter the staff area.
Your complaint about the cold room is fair and reasonable, and the hotel agrees.
Only people with a licence are allowed to drive the bus. Which word means 'entitled' or 'justified'?
On the envelope, you write the street, house number, postcode and town where the person lives.
The form asks for your name, and below that, the place where you live so they can send letters.
The company asks where to send the invoice. Which word means 'address' (formal, mailing)?
Before the snowstorm, you buy lots of rice, pasta and cans, and keep them in the cellar.
A squirrel collects nuts during autumn, so he has food for winter.
The shop says it has a large amount of goods left in the warehouse. Which word means 'supply' or 'stock'?

en: to prove, to document, to demonstrate, to occupy
situations: The student shows receipts and documents to prove that the money was spent on books.
At the bakery, you put cheese and ham on the bread.
At university, you sign up for a course and take a place on it. Which word means 'to prove' or 'to occupy'?
The teacher explains that water, oil and wood are things a country can use, but they are limited.
The company says it has little money and few workers, so it lacks things it needs to complete the project.
Climate experts say we must not waste natural materials like gas and metals. Which word means 'resource'?
The puzzle has all of its pieces, and none is missing.
Please fill in the form so that every field is filled; nothing is left empty.
The list shows every single name, with no one left out. Which word means 'complete'?
After the flood, neighbours from other towns brought food and clothes and stood together with the victims.
The workers stop work for a day to support their colleagues who lost their jobs.
People wear the same colour ribbon to show they stand together with a cause. Which word means 'solidarity'?

en: to stand out, to become apparent, to draw, to initial
situations: Dark clouds show that a change in the weather is becoming visible on the horizon.
The sketching student copies a drawing by tracing it on a thin paper.
The manager signs the document with his initials to show he has seen it. Which word means 'to become apparent', 'to draw', or 'to initial'?
At the factory, workers and machines make thousands of shoes every day.
The bakery's making of bread starts at four o'clock in the morning.
The book says how the making of cheese works, from milk to the finished product. Which word means 'production' or 'manufacture'?
Your friend comes from London and drinks tea with milk. He is from the island country with the Union Jack flag.
On a quiz show, they ask which royal family and which currency, the pound, belong to the country with Big Ben and double-decker buses.
At the market, you see sweets and biscuits that were made in England, Scotland or Wales. Which word means 'British'?

en: to turn off, to switch off
situations: Before you leave the room, you press the button so the light is no longer on.
The film is over, so you press the button on the remote to stop the TV.
During take-off, the flight attendant asks you to stop your phone. Which word means 'to switch off'?
In the garden, a small shiny insect with a hard shell crawls over a leaf.
A child proudly shows a black insect with six legs and a round back that she found under a stone.
A famous old small Volkswagen car is named after this little insect. Which word means 'beetle'?
In a record shop, the shelves are sorted into styles like rock, jazz, pop and classical.
Your friend asks: 'What kind of music do you like best?' You answer 'hip hop'.
A radio channel plays only one style, such as reggae, all day long. Which word means 'music genre'?

en: either, optionally, alternatively, selectively, as desired
situations: On the menu, it says that the dish comes with rice or alternatively with potatoes, as you like.
The hotel offers breakfast in your room or, if you prefer, in the restaurant.
The machine can be run on battery or, as desired, plugged in. Which word means 'optionally' or 'alternatively'?
After washing the dishes, you take a cloth and rub the plates until they are no longer wet.
After a shower, you use a towel on your hair and body.
It stopped raining, and you wipe the wet bench before you sit. Which word means 'to dry'?
The company's sales this year are higher than in the twelve months before.
The news says the unemployment figure is lower than in the year before this one.
Your teacher says the exam was easier than in the last year. Which word means 'previous year'?
You bought a gadget that does not do anything helpful and now it just lies in a drawer.
The umbrella is broken and has no use in the rain.
All the effort was without result, and everybody agrees it was pointless. Which word means 'useless' or 'futile'?
In the police station, the officer opens a folder with papers about the case.
The doctor's office keeps a folder with all information on each patient.
In the office, a clerk pulls a thick folder with documents about your tax case from the cabinet. Which word means 'file' or 'record'?
It is a cold winter day, so you hold your hands over a cup of hot tea to make them less cold.
You put the leftover soup on the cooker to make it hot again.
The sun makes the stones at the beach hot. Which word means 'to warm up' or 'to heat'?
You live abroad and feel a deep wish to be home with your family again.
A song talks about a strong feeling of wanting something far away that you cannot have.
The sailor stares at the sea and feels a painful wish for his home. Which word means 'longing' or 'yearning'?
After ten years, your friend moves to a different company, and it is a big new step for him.
The traffic light goes from red to green; there is a switch of colours.
In football, the coach takes a player off and sends another on. Which word means 'change' or 'shift' (replacement)?

en: temporal, chronological, in terms of time
situations: Your boss says the project will be hard, not because of money but because of the hours and deadlines.
A historian puts events in the order in which they happened.
The timetable is tight and there is a problem with the schedule, not the cost. Which word means 'chronological' or 'in terms of time'?
Two roads meet at a point and go over each other, forming an X.
You meet an old friend by chance and your paths come together in the street.
A ship sails across the sea back and forth without a clear destination. Which word means 'to cross' or 'to intersect'?
The engineer explains that the engine is made up of many separate parts, and this one is the most important part of the system.
A computer is built from several parts, like the processor and the memory, each doing its own job.
The recipe has several elements, and you need to know each part. Which word means 'component'?
At the university, a scientist studies energy, light, gravity and the movements of particles.
