Albert Einstein is a famous example of a man who studied the laws of nature like relativity.
Your uncle works in a lab and studies how matter and force behave. Which word means 'physicist'?

en: to clarify, to illustrate, to explain, to make sth clear
situations: The teacher draws a picture on the board to help the students see more clearly what the rule means.
The speaker uses an example so the audience can understand the idea.
To show how large the number is, the presenter compares it to the population of a city. Which word means 'to clarify' or 'to illustrate'?
After sitting all day at a desk, you do sports in the evening to make up for it.
The seller gives you some money back to make up for the damage.
A seesaw is balanced when two children of the same weight sit on each end. Which word means 'balance' or 'compensation'?

en: helpless, perplexed, at a loss, clueless
situations: You stand at the train station and nobody can tell you which platform to go to, and you do not know what to do.
The teacher asks a difficult question, and the students look at each other with empty faces.
The detective has no clue and does not know what to try next. Which word means 'at a loss' or 'clueless'?
The mining company digs coal out of the ground in the north of the country.
The firm announces that it will cut hundreds of jobs and make the staff smaller.
After the festival, workers take down the stage piece by piece. Which word means 'dismantling', 'reduction' or 'mining'?
You open a big map and lay it flat across the whole table.
A fire moves quickly through the dry forest and reaches more and more land.
The disease moves from town to town over the weeks. Which word means 'to spread' or 'to spread out'?
After the opening night, a man writes a newspaper article saying what he thinks was good and bad about the play.
On a TV show, an expert judges the new film and gives it two stars.
A person who writes reviews about restaurants and food for a magazine is called this. Which word means 'critic'?

en: single parent, single mother, single father
situations: Your neighbor raises her two children on her own without a partner, and works full time.
The government offers extra help for a father who looks after his kids alone.
Nobody helps Sara with her daughter at home; she is the only parent. Which word means 'single parent'?
You wake up at night, sweating, because you dreamed that a monster was chasing you.
The exam is tomorrow and you have not studied at all; for you this is the worst scene you can imagine.
A child cries in the dark because of a bad dream. Which word means 'nightmare'?
He won a lot of money in the lottery and spent it all on parties and cars within a year.
She inherited a fortune and wasted everything on silly things.
The prince threw away his money on luxury and nothing was left. Which word means 'to squander'?
The shop is closed on Sundays, and today is Sunday, so you cannot buy anything. You say: 'And so, we cannot buy bread.'
In maths, the teacher writes a long proof and ends with: 'Therefore, the result is correct.'
The train is cancelled, so you will be late for work. Which word means 'thus' or 'consequently'?
Everybody in the office says the boss will leave, but nobody knows if it is true.
A story goes around the school that the teacher is getting married, but no one has proof.
In the village, people whisper something about a neighbor, though no facts are known. Which word means 'rumour'?
After your operation, the hospital invites you to regular check-ups to see how you are recovering.
After the cancer treatment, the doctor makes a plan for further visits and care later.
A clinic offers support to patients after they have left the hospital. Which word means 'aftercare'?
You pull a rope tight between two trees to hang a hammock.
Before playing, the guitarist turns the screw to make the strings tighter.
The tailor pulls the fabric over a frame so there are no folds. Which word means 'to stretch' or 'to tighten'?
You see your partner laugh with someone else, and you feel angry and afraid of losing him.
The little girl is upset because her friend plays with another child.
When your friend wins a prize you wanted, you feel a sting of envy and resentment. Which word means 'jealous'?
At the restaurant, you ask the waiter where you can wash your hands, and he points to the room at the end of the hall.
At home, someone stays in the small room for a long time and the others are waiting outside.
A friend says casually: 'I need to go to the loo.' Which informal word means 'toilet'?
As soon as you enter the cosy cafe, you feel the warm and friendly mood in the room.
Scientists say that the layer of gases around the Earth protects us from the sun's harmful rays.
The party had a great feeling, with soft music and candles. Which word means 'atmosphere'?

en: to close, to lock, to seal
situations: Before you leave, you turn the key twice so that nobody can enter your home.
You put a lid on the jar and screw it tightly so that no air gets in.
The nurse seals the envelope with the lab test. Which word means 'to lock' or 'to seal'?
In the park, a small animal with a bushy tail and red-brown fur climbs up a tree with a nut.
In autumn, the small animal buries nuts under the ground and later forgets where.
Children throw crumbs to a quick little animal that jumps from branch to branch. Which word means 'squirrel'?
You order sushi, miso soup and tea at a restaurant that serves food from Tokyo.
In the bookshop, you want a comic book called manga, translated from the language spoken in Tokyo.
At the language school, you see a course for the language of the island nation in East Asia. Which word means 'Japanese'?
After a hard year of studying, you pass the difficult exam and feel proud.
The climber gets to the top, despite a dangerous storm, and manages the challenge.
The little boy learns to ride a bike after many falls and finally can do it perfectly. Which word means 'to master' or 'to overcome'?
At rush hour in the morning, thousands of cars, buses and bikes move along the streets of the city.
The police give a talk to children about safety when they cross the road with cars passing.
The government wants to reduce the number of accidents on roads with new rules. Which word means 'road traffic'?
You dream of a holiday in the country with high mountains, cheese, chocolate and banks, with its capital Bern.
In a quiz, you must name the neutral European country with a red flag with a white cross.
Your friend works in Zurich and Geneva, in a small country in the Alps that does not belong to the European Union.

en: to paint, to varnish, to lacquer
situations: You put a new coat of red colour on your old car in the garage.
A carpenter covers the wooden table with a shiny clear liquid to protect it.
Your sister paints her nails with a glossy colour. Which word means 'to varnish' or 'to lacquer'?
The news says more and more people have been moving to the city in recent years.
Because of the cold weather, there have been a higher number of colds recently.
The shop notes a bigger interest in electric bikes. Which word means 'increased'?
A website asks you to confirm that you are over eighteen before showing certain adult content.
The law says that sexually explicit material must not be shown to children on TV.
A parent installs a filter on the computer to block adult websites that show explicit content. Which word names this kind of content?
The restaurant buys its vegetables from a farm that brings them every Monday.
A factory gets its raw materials from a company in another country.
The supermarket changes the firm that provides its milk. Which word means 'supplier'?

en: to administer, to manage, to run
situations: The caretaker looks after the whole building, collects rent and organises repairs.
A bank employee takes care of your savings and investments.
The town hall handles the records of all citizens. Which word means 'to administer' or 'to manage'?
After a long walk in new shoes, you have a small bump filled with liquid on your foot.
The doctor says you need to go to the toilet often because the organ that stores urine is irritated.
A child blows through a ring and makes a floating ball of soap. Which word means 'bubble', 'blister' or 'bladder'?
Your sister loves painting, drawing and designing, and has many creative skills.
The school offers a course with a focus on music and drama and creative work.
The photographer's style shows imagination and a special view on beauty. Which word means 'artistic'?
The ball goes from your side of the fence to the neighbor's garden, and you say: 'It flew to the other side.'
You see a nice cafe on the other side of the street and say: 'Let's go to the other side.'
The bridge allows you to cross from one bank to the other side. Which word means 'over' or 'across' (away from you)?
The lights in the kitchen go out, so you go to the cellar and replace a small part in the electric box.
Before the update, you save a copy of all your files in case something goes wrong.
The climber attaches a rope to the rock to make sure he will not fall. Which word means 'fuse' or 'backup'?

en: to pass, to get past, to come by, to drop in
situations: A friend sends you a message: 'I will be in your area, so I will visit you for a short time on my way.'
The street is narrow and the bus cannot go by the parked lorry.
You say to your neighbor: 'Drop in whenever you like for a coffee.' Which word means 'to come by' or 'to drop in'?
The minister said something in an interview that made many people angry, and now the newspapers quote it.
Your teacher asks for a short spoken comment about the text from each student.
The company published an official statement about the accident. Which word means 'remark' or 'statement'?
After years of hard work, your boss thanks you in front of everyone and says how good your work is.
Your foreign university degree is officially accepted as valid in the new country.
The artist finally gets praise and respect for her paintings. Which word means 'recognition' or 'appreciation'?
The doctor says that there is no medicine that can make the illness go away completely.
The old man has a disease that doctors cannot cure, but they can ease his pain.
In the 1800s, many illnesses had no cure at all. Which word means 'incurable'?

en: to assess, to rate, to judge, to evaluate
situations: After the test, the teacher reads your answers and gives you a mark.
On a website, you give the hotel five stars and write a short review.
At the talent show, the jury gives points to each singer. Which word means 'to rate' or 'to judge'?

en: national league, national division, federal division, German soccer league
situations: On Saturday afternoon, millions of fans watch the top football teams in Germany, like Bayern Munich and Dortmund.
At the pub, men talk about the table positions of the best football clubs in the country.
Which word means the highest professional football league in Germany?
A film crew closes the street for a week, and cameras, lights and actors fill the square.
The actress says the work on the set was hard, with early mornings and long days.
A director says the camera work on his new movie will start in May. Which word means 'filming' or 'shooting'?

en: to build, to build up, to set up, to establish
situations: You open a box from the furniture shop and put the shelf together with a screwdriver.
After the war, the people had to make their city again, brick by brick.
The circus workers put up the big tent in the morning. Which word means 'to set up' or 'to build up'?
Before the election, citizens decide which group of politicians with a common programme they will vote for.
A woman becomes a member of the group that has a programme for the environment and takes part in its meetings.
In parliament, there are groups with different colours, like red, green and black. Which word means '(political) party'?
You hear a heavy sound through the wall, and cannot tell what it is.
He has a vague pain in his back, not sharp, but always there.
The voice from behind the door sounds muffled and not clear. Which word means 'dull' or 'muffled'?
At the casino, people put money on cards and the roulette wheel, hoping for luck.
Your friend lost his savings by betting on dice and lottery tickets, and now he needs help.
The law says that games where money is won by chance can only be offered with a licence. Which word means 'gambling'?

en: to assume, to presuppose, to take for granted, to require
situations: The job advert says that the applicant must have a university degree.
In your talk, you start from the idea that the audience already knows the basics.
The teacher says: 'I take it for granted that you did your homework.' Which word means 'to presuppose' or 'to assume'?
In ancient Greece, a man named Socrates asked deep questions about life, truth and good and evil.
A thinker writes books about the meaning of life and what it means to be human.
Your uncle studies the ideas of Plato and Kant at the university. Which word names a person who thinks and writes about big questions of life and existence?
The student's grades are far better than those of most of the class.
The company's profit this year is much higher than usual for the industry.
Her salary is higher than what most people in her job earn. Which word means 'above-average'?
The doctor says your arm or leg is hurt, and this part of the body is called by a general term.
A chain is made of many small rings, and each one is connected to the next.
A finger has three small parts bending between the bones. Which word means 'limb', 'joint' or 'link'?
The teacher says that students can use dictionaries in the exam, so she lets them.
The sign says that dogs are not allowed in the shop, so the shop owner does not let them.
A father says to his daughter: 'I will let you go to the party.' Which word means 'to allow' or 'to permit'?
In the fridge, you find yoghurt, cheese, butter and cream, all made from the white drink of cows.
A person who cannot digest lactose must avoid food like cheese and yoghurt.
At the supermarket, there is a section with milk, cream and curd. Which word means 'dairy product'?
You see your friend buy a huge ladder, and you ask: 'What is it for?'
Your colleague wants a big budget, and you ask him for what purpose he needs it.
Your child asks why you need a hammer. Which question word means 'what for' or 'why'?
At the restaurant, the waiter asks: 'Still or with bubbles?' You choose the one with bubbles.
You open a cold bottle and hear a hiss, and small bubbles rise to the top of the water.
In the south of the country, people say a short word for the fizzy mineral water. Which word means 'sparkling water'?
The milk in the fridge is old, and the date on the carton passed yesterday.
Your passport will no longer be valid after next month because its time is over.
The sand in the hourglass is almost all at the bottom; the time is finishing. Which word means 'to expire' or 'to run out'?
You buy cheese from a farm in your own village, not one far away.
The weather report says there will be rain in some parts of the region, not everywhere.
The doctor gives you an injection that numbs only one small part of your body. Which word means 'local' or 'locally'?
A colleague gives you a helpful idea for how to improve the website, and you take it into account.
Coffee in the morning gives your body a push and makes you more awake.
The customer leaves a short note in the box saying what the shop could do better. Which word means 'suggestion' or 'stimulus'?
You take a small leather thing out of your pocket and pay for the bread with coins and notes.
Someone stole it on the bus, and with it your cards and your cash.
In your handbag, you keep a small case with your banknotes, coins and bank card. Which word means 'wallet' or 'purse'?
When planning the school trip, the teacher also asks the students for their wishes and makes them part of the plan.
The report must also cover the costs for the transport, not only the hotel.
The manager takes the opinion of all workers into account in the decision. Which word means 'to include'?
You write an email to the hotel to ask whether there are free rooms in August.
A journalist sends a question to the ministry and waits for an answer.
The company gets a message from a customer asking for the price of a product. Which word means 'inquiry' or 'request'?
Your colleague has the flu, and the manager says to stay away because you could catch it from him.
Yawning is something that spreads from one person to the next, and laughing can too.
The doctor says the rash is a disease that passes easily from child to child at school. Which word means 'contagious'?

en: to explore, to research, to investigate
situations: Scientists travel to the deep ocean to find out what lives there and study the unknown.
A historian digs through old papers to learn more about the life of a king.
Children go into the forest and look at every corner to discover new things. Which word means 'to explore' or 'to research'?
Your pen runs out of ink, so you take a new small tube and push it inside.
The printer shows a message saying that the black ink container is empty.
In a western film, the cowboy puts a small metal piece with powder in the gun. Which word means 'cartridge'?
At the market, the seller puts the tomatoes on a device to find out how many kilos they are.
In the bathroom, you step on a flat device to see how much you weigh.
In the horoscope, the sign shown by two plates hanging from a stick is for people born in autumn. Which word means 'scales' or 'Libra'?
Your doctor tells you to eat less salt to lower your blood pressure.
The city wants to make less rubbish and cut the amount every year.
The company wants to bring down its costs this year. Which word means 'to reduce' or 'to decrease'?
The company checks that every worker follows the safety rules in the factory.
The inspector comes to see if the restaurant obeys the hygiene laws.
Fines are given to drivers who do not stick to the speed limit; the police watch for this. Which word means 'compliance' or 'observance'?
The government cuts the budget by half in one year, a very strong and severe measure.
The doctor tells him to make a big and sharp change in his diet or he will become ill.
Prices of petrol went up very sharply overnight. Which word means 'drastic'?
In art history, you learn about the time at the start of the twentieth century when new styles appeared and old traditions ended.
A museum shows paintings from the era that began after the nineteenth century, with abstract art.
Architecture from the time of glass and steel buildings is part of this age. Which word means 'modern age' or 'modernity'?

en: to tremble, to shake, to shiver
situations: You stand outside in winter without a coat, and your whole body moves quickly because of the cold.
Before the big speech, your hands shake because you are nervous.
The old man's hand moves slightly while he holds the cup. Which word means 'to tremble' or 'to shake'?

en: artwork, work of art, piece of art
situations: In the museum, you stand in front of a beautiful painting for a long time.
A sculptor spends two years making a statue and it is shown in the town square.
An exhibition shows paintings, statues and drawings, and critics praise each single piece. Which word means 'work of art'?
You say on the phone: 'Sorry, I cannot talk now, I have a lot to do.'
The restaurant is full, and the waiters run around between tables.
The doctor has no time to see more patients today. Which word means 'busy'?
The weather report says there will be rain, snow or hail in the north tomorrow.
Farmers need enough water from the sky during the growing season.
A meteorologist measures how many millimetres of water fell in a month. Which word means 'precipitation' or 'rainfall'?
You want to laugh in the serious meeting but you hold it back with great effort.
A dictator does not allow the people to speak freely and treats them cruelly, according to the history book.
You try to hide your anger when the waiter is rude. Which word means 'to suppress' or 'to oppress'?

en: beforehand, in advance, to begin with
situations: The organisers send you the programme by email before the event so you can read it ahead of time.
You pay a part of the price before the trip starts.
The teacher says: 'To start with, I want to say something.' Which word means 'beforehand' or 'in advance'?
Thanks to the neighbors' hands during the move, you finished in two hours.
The police found the thief with the help of a witness who gave information.
The teacher thanks the parents for their support in organising the school party. Which word means 'help' or 'assistance'?
After working all day at the computer, the back part of your neck feels stiff and sore.
The massage therapist presses the muscles between your head and shoulders.
A mother kisses her baby on the soft back part of the neck. Which word means 'neck' (back of the neck)?

en: to rent (out), to lend (out), to award
situations: The shop lets you use a power drill for a day for a small fee.
The mayor gives a medal to the brave firefighter at the ceremony.
You allow your friend to use your bike for the weekend. Which word means 'to rent out', 'to lend' or 'to award'?
The famous singer lives in a small flat and never boasts about her success.
Your grandparents live a simple life and do not need many things.
The winner says: 'I was just lucky,' and does not brag about his skills. Which word means 'modest' or 'humble'?
In the fairy tale, an old woman with a pointed hat flies on a broom and makes magic drinks.
At Halloween, children dress up as a woman with a black hat and a cat.
In the story 'Hansel and Gretel', the old woman lives in a house made of sweets and wants to cook the children. Which word means 'witch'?
In a theatre play, the first big part is over and the curtain falls before the break.
In an art gallery, there is a painting of a person without clothes, and the sign explains the category.
The programme says the play has three big parts. Which word means 'act' or 'nude'?

en: to tear open, to rip open
situations: You are hungry and quickly pull the paper off a pack of biscuits with force.
He tears the envelope with the exam result in a hurry.
The child cannot wait for her birthday and tears the paper off the present. Which word means 'to tear open' or 'to rip open'?
In a large company, a person leads a team, sets goals and decides about budgets.
A football club hires a person to organise contracts and the business side, not the training.
The boss of a department makes plans and gives tasks to employees. Which word names a person who leads a department or team?
Your doctor knows exactly what to do and answers all your questions with confidence, because he has great skill and knowledge.
The new mechanic fixes your car in one hour and explains clearly what was wrong.
A teacher who knows her subject well and is able to teach it is described this way. Which word means 'competent'?
Before the football match, the fans wave a piece of cloth in the national colours.
On the town hall, a piece of cloth moves in the wind on a pole.
The Olympic team enters the stadium behind its country's colours. Which word means 'flag'?
After years of study, she finally gets her university degree.
The country gained independence after a long struggle.
He wants to reach a high position in the company through hard work. Which word means 'to obtain' or 'to attain'?
Your friend owns a part of the company, ten percent, and gets money from the profit.
The pie chart shows which part of the budget goes to housing and food.
In the mixture, the proportion of sugar is only a small part. Which word means 'share' or 'proportion'?
Every four years, national football teams meet in one country to fight for the golden cup, and the whole world watches.
The tournament, in which athletes from many nations compete for a global title, starts next month.
The news announces that the global competition for ice hockey begins on Friday. Which word means 'world championship'?
The show on TV was so funny and lively that you did not look at your watch once.
The teacher's lesson was never boring, with many jokes and stories.
The book is light and a pleasure to read, with a lot of fun. Which word means 'entertaining'?
Your little sister did not get the toy, so she sits in the corner with a closed mouth and a sad face and says nothing.
After the small argument, your friend crosses her arms, turns away and ignores everybody.
A child pushes his lip forward when told it is bedtime. Which word means 'to pout' or 'to sulk'?

en: seed, stone, core, nucleus, essence, pit
situations: You eat a peach and find a hard thing in the middle that you must not swallow.
The scientist says the centre of an atom holds most of its mass.
Your teacher says: 'Tell me the main idea, the very heart of the story.' Which word means 'core', 'pit' or 'nucleus'?
Your car number plate shows the area where you live, which is bigger than a town but smaller than a state.
The local office for the whole rural area around the town is called by this administrative name.
On the map of Germany, a state is divided into smaller administrative areas. Which word means 'county' or 'district'?

en: to enter, to walk into, to step into, to set foot
situations: A sign on the grass says you may not walk on it.
You put your foot into the room for the first time and see the new office.
The astronaut is the first person to set foot on the moon. Which word means 'to enter' or 'to step into'?
The doctor says: 'We need a fast decision.' The healing of the wound is very quick.
The runner crosses the finish line in a swift movement.
The company reacts in a speedy way to the news. Which word means 'quick' or 'swift'?
At the vegetable stall, you buy a big round green vegetable with many leaves to make soup or salad.
Your grandmother cooks a big pot of the white or green round vegetable, often eaten with sausages or in sauerkraut.
A rabbit in the garden eats leaves of the round vegetable. Which word means 'cabbage'?
Your friend says the plan is not good, and you ask him: 'In what way is it a problem?'
The teacher asks: 'To what extent do you agree with the author?'
You do not understand how the two ideas are connected, so you ask for details. Which question word means 'in what way' or 'how far'?
The company burns thousands of old papers so that nothing is left.
In a film, a giant monster wipes out an entire city.
Pests can completely destroy a farmer's whole harvest. Which word means 'to destroy' or 'to annihilate'?
Your GPS shows the place on the map where you stand right now.
At work, you apply for a higher job in the company.
A chess player thinks about where each piece stands on the board. Which word means 'place' or 'item' in a list, or 'standing'?
The child asks for another sweet, and the mother answers with the opposite of 'yes'.
In the vote, there are many who say yes and some who give the word of refusal.
When the shop assistant asks if you need a bag and you do not, you say a short word of refusal. Which noun means 'no' (the answer)?
The film ends with the hero's death, and the audience cries because it is very sad.
The news tells of a terrible accident that took the lives of many people.
In a Greek play, the story ends with great sorrow and loss. Which word means 'tragic'?
After the flood, you send money to a charity to help people who lost their homes.
Every year, many people give blood at the hospital for those in need.
At school, children collect clothes and toys for poor families. Which word means 'to donate'?
In a laboratory, a person works for years to find a cure for a disease.
In the nineteenth century, a person travelled to the jungle to discover unknown plants and rivers.
A scientist at the university studies the stars and publishes papers. Which word means 'researcher' or 'explorer'?
Many tourists in summer lie on the beaches of Spain, Italy and Greece, where the sea is warm and blue.
The sea between Europe and Africa, with islands like Crete and Sicily, is a popular holiday place.
In the geography class, the teacher shows the sea that lies between southern Europe and North Africa. Which word means 'Mediterranean'?
The parents give a name to their new baby daughter.
The scientist gives a new plant a Latin name.
The company chooses a new head for the department and names him in a letter. Which word means 'to name' or 'to designate'?
The doctor says you have a serious health problem in your lungs and you must stay at home.
The company says that many workers are away because of a bad flu this week.
A report lists heart problems and diabetes as the most common health conditions. Which word means 'illness'?
The newsreader says: 'The situation at this time is difficult for the economy.'
The shop manager says that the stock available right now is small.
The minister speaks about the situation as it is today. Which word means 'current' or 'present'?
The teacher gives every child the same chance and does not favour anyone. Everyone says that is how it should be.
In a court, the judge wants everybody to be treated equally and correctly according to the law.
The protesters want a society where rich and poor are treated in the same way. Which word means 'justice' or 'fairness'?
You let your friend have your seat on the bus, and you give him your place.
The boss gives the decision to his team and does not decide himself.
She gives her flat to her cousin for the summer while she is away. Which word means 'to leave' (to someone) or 'to hand over'?
You sign up on a shop's website, and every Monday you get an email with the latest offers.
The company sends a short regular email to its customers about news and events.
A school sends parents a monthly email with news about the school. Which word means a regular news email?
In a history lesson, the teacher speaks about the time of the Renaissance, a long time period with its own character.
A new age began when the printing press was invented.
The Stone Age and the Iron Age are examples of long periods in history. Which word means 'epoch' or 'era'?
At Christmas and Easter, the traditions come from a religion based on the teachings of Jesus.
The old charity belongs to a church and works with values taken from the Bible.
A school run by the church teaches in the spirit of the New Testament. Which word means 'Christian'?
The soldiers in the old film raise a white flag and give up the fight.
In the game, the player knows he is lost and gives in to the opponent.
The thief sees the police on all sides and puts up his hands. Which word means 'to surrender'?
Your friend says: 'I bet you ten euros that our team will win', and you shake hands.
At the races, people put money on the horse they think will come first.
You and your brother agree that the loser pays for the pizza. Which word means 'bet'?
Before going on stage, the actress puts powder, lipstick and eyeshadow on her face.
In the bathroom drawer, your sister has many colours for the eyes and lips.
Women in the shop buy mascara, foundation and lipstick. Which word means 'make-up'?

en: by the name of, called, named
situations: A man you do not know comes to the door and says: 'I am looking for a woman with the name of Anna.'
The teacher says: 'We have a new student called Paul.'
On the phone, you say: 'I have a friend by the name of Peter, can you help him?' Which word means 'named' or 'called'?

en: to wait, to wait for, to wait and see
situations: The doctor says you should not take medicine yet, but first see how the symptoms develop.
You do not know what to do about the problem, so you stay calm and watch for a few days.
The investor does not buy the shares now and waits to see if the price falls. Which word means 'to wait and see'?
The athlete has won the gold medal not once but many times.
The company has contacted the customer repeatedly by phone.
The form is needed in several copies, not just one. Which word means 'multiple' or 'repeated'?
The doctor writes on the prescription that you must take 500 of a very small weight unit, one thousandth of a gram.
On the medicine box, the amount of the active ingredient is given in a tiny unit.
A chemist weighs a tiny amount of powder on a very exact scale. Which word means 'milligram'?
In spring, people queue at stands to buy long white or green stalks, which they cook and eat with butter and potatoes.
A restaurant offers a seasonal dish with long thin stalks that are harvested from April to June.
In Germany, white stalks of a vegetable are very popular at the beginning of summer. Which word means 'asparagus'?
The driver goes much too fast on the motorway, and the police stop him.
A child runs very fast across the field and his mother worries.
The train races through the countryside at great speed. Which word means 'to speed' or 'to race'?
You make a green dip for the party by mashing a soft pear-shaped fruit with a big stone, adding lemon and salt.
At breakfast, you spread a creamy green fruit on your toast.
At the market, you press a dark green fruit to see if it is ripe. Which word names this fruit?
The contract is signed, so both sides must keep to what it says.
The waiter is warm and kind to every guest, in a pleasant way.
The teacher says that the deadline is fixed, no exceptions. Which word means 'binding' or 'friendly'?
The basic law of a country is a document that sets out the rights of citizens and how the state works.
The doctor asks about your health and says you are in good physical shape.
The team played badly because their mental state was bad. Which word means 'constitution' or 'condition'?
At dinner, the host lifts the bottle and fills your glass with wine.
The waiter fills the cups with hot coffee from a pot.
Grandma pours milk into the glasses for the children. Which word means 'to pour' (a drink)?
Before going to bed, you pull a long piece of cloth across the window so the light of the street does not come in.
At the theatre, the heavy cloth in front of the stage goes up and the play begins.
In the bathroom, you pull a plastic sheet around the shower. Which word means 'curtain'?
It is cold, and your jumper has long parts for your arms, so your hands stay warm.
The shirt is too short in the part that covers your arm, and you buy a bigger size.
In summer, you roll up the part of your shirt that covers your arm. Which word means 'sleeve'?
After years of division, the two parts of the country become one again.
Two small companies join their forces into one big firm.
The rivers meet and flow together into the sea. Which word means 'to unite'?
The surprise party is ready, and the birthday child is coming home without any idea of what awaits him.
The tourist walks into a dangerous area, not knowing that he should not be there.
A child asks a simple question because he knows nothing about the topic. Which word means 'clueless' or 'unsuspecting'?
In a western film, the cowboy holds a long weapon with both hands.
The hunter carries a long weapon through the forest in the early morning.
At the fair, you win a prize by shooting at targets with a long toy weapon. Which word means 'rifle'?
After washing your hair in the morning, you use a hot machine that blows air to get it dry quickly.
The hairdresser uses a loud machine with hot air to style your hair.
In winter, you do not want to go out with wet hair, so you dry it with warm air. Which word means 'to blow-dry'?
In the meeting, one colleague writes down everything that is said and sends it to everyone afterwards.
The police officer writes a report of the accident with all the details.
In the school, the secretary writes a record of what was decided in the staff meeting. Which word means 'minutes' or 'protocol'?
The doctor says a disease can be passed on from parents to children through genes.
Scientists study DNA to find out why people look alike in a family.
A test shows that the eye colour is decided by the information in the cells you inherit. Which word means 'genetic'?
You wipe the top part of the table with a cloth to clean it.
The ice on the lake has a smooth top layer where children skate.
A diver comes up from the deep and reaches the top of the water. Which word means 'surface'?
Your eyelid moves by itself a little because you are tired.
When someone asks you a question you do not know, you lift both shoulders and say 'who knows?'
The sleeping dog moves its leg slightly in his dream. Which word means 'to twitch' or 'to shrug'?
At a big company, the group of people at the top who make the most important decisions is called this.
A student studies how to run firms and lead teams at business school.
The staff complain that those who lead the firm do not listen to them. Which word means the leadership of a company?

en: to this, for this purpose, concerning this
situations: In a meeting, the boss says: 'I want to add something about this topic.'
At the end of the letter, it says: 'You will find more information about this in the attached file.'
The teacher asks a question: 'What do you think about this?' Which word means 'to this' or 'concerning this'?
In the school gym, the ball flies from your hand towards the basket, and you try to score.
The cat gave birth to five kittens, and the baby animals born together are called this.
In a javelin competition, the athlete's long toss is measured. Which word means 'throw' or 'litter'?

en: to worry, to be worried, to be concerned
situations: Your child is late and does not answer the phone, so you feel afraid that something has happened.
The mother lies awake at night because she fears for her son's health.
You are anxious about the exam results. Which word means 'to worry'?
The detective explains his reasoning step by step, and everything makes sense.
The maths teacher says your answer follows a clear and reasonable path.
If A is bigger than B, and B is bigger than C, then A is bigger than C, of course. Which word means 'logical'?
The neighbor comes from Moscow and speaks a language with Cyrillic letters. He is a man from the biggest country in the world.
At the chess tournament, a man from the country whose capital is Moscow wins the final.
A tourist in a hotel says he is from St Petersburg. What do you call a man from that country?
On Saturday night, you buy tickets to see actors perform a story on a stage in front of an audience.
At school, the drama group practises a performance for the end of the year.
Shakespeare wrote many famous ones, like Hamlet, to be acted in a theatre. Which word means 'play'?

en: to stimulate, to revive, to enliven
situations: The mayor wants to bring life back to the empty town centre with markets and events.
A cup of strong coffee makes you more awake and active in the morning.
The doctor tries to bring the patient back to life after he stops breathing. Which word means 'to revive' or 'to stimulate'?
In the museum, a person stands for a long time in front of a painting and looks at it carefully.
The painter says the picture changes depending on who looks at it.
A critic writes that a good photograph speaks to the person who looks at it. Which word means 'viewer' or 'observer'?
You stand in a long queue and keep looking at your watch, wanting to move on quickly.
The child cannot wait for the cake and keeps asking: 'Is it ready yet?'
The customer taps his foot because the waiter takes too long. Which word means 'impatient'?
On your computer, you open a place that holds all the files of one project.
At the back of the book, there is a list of names and subjects with page numbers.
The town hall keeps an official list of all the businesses in the area. Which word means 'directory' or 'register'?

en: to force one´s way in, to penetrate, to enter, to intrude, to invade
situations: A burglar breaks through the window and enters the house without permission.
The water goes through the old roof into the attic.
The army marches into a neighbouring country in a history book. Which word means 'to intrude', 'to penetrate' or 'to invade'?
The philosopher sits in the garden and thinks deeply about life for hours.
The scientist makes a careful look at the sample under the microscope.
The report offers a closer look at the economic situation. Which word means 'contemplation' or 'consideration'?
You want to see Santa Claus's village and take a sauna in the northern country whose capital is Helsinki.
In a quiz, you must name the country with thousands of lakes next to Sweden and Russia.
Your friend says the country famous for Nokia, saunas and the best schools is cold in winter.
The researcher checks every sample in the same order, one after another, with a clear method.
The students write their notes in a careful and ordered way, with a plan.
The police search the whole area in an organised way, row by row. Which word means 'systematic'?
The prices go up again, and you cannot change it, so you just live with it.
He does not like the decision but accepts it without a complaint.
The team has lost the match and has to take the defeat. Which word means 'to accept' (something unpleasant)?
To start a new company, you need money to invest, and the bank asks how much you have.
An economist talks about money and property that can be used to make more money.
The investor puts a large sum into the business. Which word means 'capital' or 'asset'?
The little girl plays the piano perfectly without any lessons. People say she has a natural gift.
Your teacher says you have a special ability for languages.
A boy draws beautiful pictures at the age of five. Which word means 'talent' or 'gift'?
The story of the film is set in Paris in the 1920s.
The reporter describes the scene that happened in front of the building last night.
The police ask what happened in the street. Which word means 'to take place'?
You forgot his birthday, so you send him your good wishes a week afterwards.
The new rule was added after the contract was signed.
The teacher accepts your homework later than the deadline. Which word means 'belated' or 'subsequent'?
The doctor listens to your chest with a cold tool and asks you to breathe deeply.
A smoker is told that this organ in the chest can be badly damaged by cigarettes.
When you breathe in, air goes to the organ inside your chest that takes oxygen. Which word means 'lung'?
Your friend says he is waiting for something, and you ask: 'For what?'
The teacher says: 'You must take care of one thing.' You ask: 'On what should I focus?'
You do not understand what the sentence refers to. Which question word means 'on what' or 'on which'?
The travel brochure shows a white beach, palm trees and clear water, and says it is a perfect place.
In the Bible, Adam and Eve lived in a beautiful garden before they had to leave.
After a stressful year, you think of a quiet island as a dream place. Which word means 'paradise'?

en: to sway, to stagger, to fluctuate, to vary, to waver
situations: The small boat moves from side to side on the waves.
The price of oil goes up and down every week, and is not stable.
The voter cannot decide between two parties and keeps changing his mind. Which word means 'to sway' or 'to fluctuate'?
The teacher explains the difference between two words so that students can tell them apart.
The law makes a clear split between adults and children.
The doctor says it is important to separate the two kinds of illness in your diagnosis. Which word means 'distinction' or 'differentiation'?
Your cousin works at a university and writes long papers for journals.
The job needs a university degree and years of study.
The professor speaks in a very scholarly way that is hard to follow. Which word means 'academic'?
You want to buy a house but do not have enough money, so the bank gives you money that you must pay back with interest.
A student gets money from the state to study and repays it later.
Your friend asks you for a sum and promises to return it next month. Which word means 'loan'?

en: to organize, to organise, to host, to arrange, to hold
situations: The school plans a big summer party with music and games, and invites everyone.
The city holds a marathon every year and sells tickets.
Your friends put together a surprise birthday party for you. Which word means 'to organize' or 'to host'?
After eating strawberries, your skin gets red spots that itch.
The baby has little red spots on the face, and the doctor says it is harmless.
In a measuring device, the needle moves far to the right. Which word means 'rash' or 'deflection'?
It surprises you that your quiet neighbor suddenly plays loud music at night.
It does not surprise me that he is late; he always is.
The magician's trick leaves the whole room wondering. Which word means 'to astonish' or 'to surprise'?
The newspaper says there are more thefts and robberies in the city than last year.
The politician promises to fight against the number of illegal acts in the area.
Police statistics show that the number of offences has gone down. Which word means 'crime' (in general) or 'crime rate'?
The teacher explains that water boils at 100 degrees because of the laws of nature, not because of chemistry.
A scientist studies the movement of particles and energy in an experiment.
The exam asks about gravity, speed and force. Which word means 'physical' (of physics)?
The boss is on holiday, so another person takes over his job for two weeks.
The president cannot come to the meeting and sends a person to act in his place.
The school headmaster has a person who replaces him when he is away. Which word means 'deputy' or 'substitute'?
The police say that the man did something illegal when he stole the car.
The town marks its 800th anniversary with a big festival.
The student made a serious mistake in the exam. Which word means 'to commit' or 'to celebrate'?
In the song, the last words of two lines sound the same, like 'cat' and 'hat'.
The poet writes verses where the endings match in sound.
A child learns a little poem where the line ends sound alike. Which word means 'rhyme'?
In the hotel room, there is a small metal box in the wardrobe where you can lock your passport and money.
In a bank film, the thieves try to open the heavy steel door of the room where gold is kept.
At home, your parents keep important papers and jewellery in a locked metal box. Which word means 'safe'?
The woman has dark brown hair, not blonde or red.
On the police description, it says the girl has brown hair and brown eyes.
At the hairdresser, she wants to dye her hair a dark brown colour. Which word means 'brunette'?
The earthquake makes all the buildings move strongly from side to side.
The sad news about the accident shocks the whole country deeply.
The explosion made the windows tremble. Which word means 'to shake' or 'to rock'?
Your father's father proudly shows a photo of your little brother as the boy of his son.
At the family party, the grandmother says: 'This is my daughter's boy, and he is a great footballer.'
From the viewpoint of a grandfather, what do you call his son's young boy? Which word means 'grandson'?
Before buying the new machine, the company asks what advantage it will bring.
The teacher asks what use it is to learn old poems by heart.
The study shows the gain for patients is large. Which word means 'benefit' or 'use'?

en: for the time being, for the moment, for the present
situations: The shop is closed now, and you say you will not buy a new phone, at least for now.
The manager says that the old rule stays in place until further notice.
I will not make a decision just yet; let us see what happens, for the moment. Which word means 'for the time being'?

en: to pretend, to use as an excuse, to set in advance
situations: The child lies down and acts as if he is asleep so his mother does not call him.
The man uses a headache as an excuse not to go to the meeting.
The teacher sets the topic of the essay in advance for the students. Which word means 'to pretend' or 'to set in advance'?
You talk about the weekend that has just ended: 'Last weekend, we went hiking.'
The teacher says: 'Remember what we learned in the time before now.'
The previous year was warmer than this one. Which word means 'past' or 'last'?
When you walk by a bakery, you notice the nice thing that comes into your nose.
The milk in the fridge went off, and a bad thing in the air tells you not to drink it.
The flower garden has a sweet scent in the evening. Which word means 'smell'?
At a film shoot, a person sits in a chair and says 'Action!' and tells the actors what to do.
The theatre hires a person to plan how the play will look on the stage and guide the actors.
At the film festival, the person who made the movie receives an award for the best direction. Which word means 'director'?

en: to emphasize, to emphasise, to highlight, to prove to be, to turn out
situations: The speaker wants to make one point clear and puts it in the centre of attention.
At first the plan seemed good, but it turned out to be a mistake.
The report shows that the new method is better and brings it to the fore. Which word means 'to emphasize' or 'to turn out'?
When you open the coffee jar, a rich and pleasant scent fills the kitchen.
The tea is described as having a fine fruity taste.
The chef adds herbs to give the soup a stronger taste. Which word means 'flavour' or 'pleasant scent'?
Your grandfather has a clock with hands, not one with numbers on a screen.
The old record player plays music from a vinyl disc, not from a digital file.
The two situations are similar in the way they work. Which word means 'not digital' or 'similar in kind'?
After switching to a cheaper phone plan, you keep fifty euros every year.
The family puts money in the bank every month for the holiday.
The company says the new software leads to lower costs, so there are money gains. Which word means 'saving' or 'savings'?
You write to the office to get a copy of your birth certificate sent to you.
The police ask for more officers to come to the place.
The doctor orders the results of your blood test from the lab. Which word means 'to request' (officially)?
You study for the exam, but your phone keeps buzzing and you cannot focus.
After a sad week, a nice trip is just what you need to think of something else.
In football, the ball hit the defender and went in a different direction. Which word means 'distraction' or 'diversion'?
Two families have not spoken for years, and they feel a very strong dislike for each other.
The politician says that online comments full of anger against other groups must stop.
Love and the opposite feeling, a deep wish for someone to suffer, are part of the human life. Which word means 'hatred'?
At the mountain top, you take a deep breath and fill your lungs with fresh air.
The yoga teacher says: 'Now take air in slowly through your nose.'
The doctor listens to your chest and says: 'Breathe in, then breathe out.' Which word means 'to inhale'?
The teacher says that your essay has good grammar, but as for what is written in it, it is weak.
The editor checked the book for the story and facts, not for spelling.
The two reports are the same in terms of what they say. Which word means 'in terms of content'?
On a hot summer day, you wear open shoes with straps and no closed front.
At the beach, you take off your flip-flops and put your feet in the water.
In the shop, you try on light open shoes for your holiday in the sun. Which word means 'sandal'?
You wrap a birthday present and tie the ribbon on top into a pretty knot with two decorative ends.
In a computer program, a short piece of code runs again and again until a counter reaches ten. What do you call this repeating part?
On a roller coaster, the train goes up, turns completely upside down in a circle, and comes back down. What is that circular part of the track called?

en: to interfere, to intervene, to butt in, to meddle, to mix in
situations: Two colleagues are talking about their own project. You suddenly start telling them what to do, although it has nothing to do with you.
Your neighbour is quarrelling with her son, and you walk over to give your opinion, although nobody asked you.
Which verb means 'to butt in' to other people's business?
A young soldier in uniform serves in the national army, navy and air force of Germany. What is the name of this organisation?
A news report says that soldiers are filling sandbags to help a town during a flood in Germany.
Your classmate turns 18 and says he wants to join the national armed forces after school.
Your teacher never allows phones in class, with no exceptions, and punishes everyone who breaks the rule.
Your doctor says you must follow the diet exactly and must not cheat even once. What word describes his rules?
Your boss demands that every report arrives on time, to the minute, and he never makes an exception.
A museum exhibition explains how the first cities came into being thousands of years ago.
A scientist talks about how the moon came to exist, billions of years ago.
A teacher explains how a thunderstorm forms, step by step. Which noun means 'origin' or 'emergence'?

en: to break out, to escape, to erupt, to burst
situations: The lights suddenly go off in the stadium and panic starts among the crowd.
In a film, a prisoner digs a tunnel to get out of his cell.
The volcano on the island suddenly starts to throw out ash and hot lava.
Your friend shows you a timetable. You draw a conclusion from what is written there and start your sentence with a little linking word before 'the last train has left'.
A newspaper article lists several facts. Then the writer starts the next sentence with a word that means 'therefore' to draw a conclusion.
At work the boss reads the sales numbers and says a conclusion based on them, starting with an adverb meaning 'according to this'.
A city has good roads, railways, bridges, power lines and water pipes. What do you call this basic system of public facilities?
A news report says the country must spend money on its roads, trains and internet cables.
A company wants to build a factory in a village, but the village has no proper roads, no power and no fast internet.
You taste your grandmother's apple cake and say it is wonderfully tasty.
At a restaurant the soup smells great and tastes truly excellent. How do you describe it?
Which adjective means 'delicious'?

en: to install, to build in, to fit, to integrate
situations: An electrician puts a new oven into the kitchen cabinet so that it fits tightly.
A car mechanic fits a new radio into the dashboard of your car.
Your boss wants a new function to be built into the app's design. Which verb means 'to install' or 'to build in'?
On an old round clock, the thin part that points at the numbers moves around the dial.
On a bathroom scale with a dial, the thin part moves round and points to your weight.
On the computer screen, a little arrow moves when you move the mouse.
Firefighters race to a house where flames and smoke come out of the windows.
The newspaper says a huge blaze destroyed an old barn last night, but nobody was hurt.
Which noun means 'fire' in the sense of a big, destructive blaze?
Long ago, farmers came to the empty valley and began to build homes and live there.
The city wants technology companies to come and establish themselves in a new business park.
Biologists release wolves into a forest so they can make a home there again.
The signs at the airport are unclear and everyone walks around not knowing where to go.
You get three different answers from three people and you do not know what to think.
Which noun means 'confusion'?
You press the button of the lift, but nothing happens. A sign says it is out of order.
You bought a hairdryer, but at home it will not turn on, so you take it back to the shop.
A mechanic checks your car and says a part is broken and must be replaced.
In a country, all adult citizens can vote freely in elections to choose who governs them.
A history teacher explains that ancient Athens was where the system of government by the people began.
Which noun means 'democracy'?
A woman sits at a big wooden loom and makes cloth by crossing threads over and under each other.
A craft museum shows how people once made fabric by hand from wool threads.
Which verb means 'to weave'?
For breakfast you pour batter into a hot pan, flip the thin flat cake and eat it with syrup.
At a cafe you order a stack of thin, round, flat cakes with maple syrup and butter.
Which noun means 'pancake'?
On the front page of the newspaper, big bold letters tell the main story of the day.
Your phone shows the big title of a news story: 'Heavy snow closes airport'.
Which noun means 'headline'?
Your uncle has thick dark hair all over his arms and chest.
You see a spider with long thin legs covered with lots of tiny hairs.
At the swimming pool, a man has very thick hair on his legs. Which adjective describes him?
While cooking, the recipe says to put a bit more salt into the soup.
In a document, you write one more sentence at the end of the paragraph.
You save a new phone number into your list of contacts. Which verb means 'to add'?
A hospital is looking for a qualified nurse with training and experience.
A factory advertises a job for a trained worker with special skills, such as an electrician.
Which noun means 'skilled worker' or 'specialist'?
In tennis, the serve is so fast that your opponent cannot even touch the ball. It is a winning serve.
In a card game, the highest card has just the number one on it and beats the king.
Which noun means 'ace'?

en: to trigger, to cause, to set off, to provoke
situations: Burnt toast makes the smoke alarm start ringing.
A bee sting causes a strong allergic reaction in a boy.
A surprising speech by the manager provokes a loud discussion in the office.
You watch a football match live on TV from a stadium in another city.
A doctor explains how a virus passes from one person to another.
Which noun means 'broadcast' or 'transmission'?
Your car's speed stays exactly at 100 km/h the whole way, never changing.
The temperature in the fridge always stays at four degrees.
Your teacher says your marks have been steady and unchanging all year.
After a long discussion about where to go on holiday, you say what the result was: '... we chose the beach.'
Your friend tried many jobs, but what came out at the very end of all that was a career as a teacher. Which adverb starts that sentence?
Which adverb means 'in the end'?
Your hotel booking ends tomorrow. It is the day you pack your suitcase and leave.
On the hotel form there is a box for the date when you will go home.
The travel agency email says: 'Arrival: 3 June. ... : 10 June.' What is the missing noun?

en: to cooperate, to work together, to collaborate
situations: Two companies join forces on a new product and share their ideas.
In class, the teacher asks you and your partner to do the project as a team.
Two scientists from different countries work on the same experiment together.
On a hike you see water falling from a high cliff with a loud roar.
A travel brochure for Iceland shows water crashing down over black rocks into a pool.
Which noun means 'waterfall'?
A bakery sells baguettes and croissants in the style typical of Paris. Which adjective describes this style?
You study the language spoken in Paris and Lyon, so you take a class in it.
Your friend comes from Lyon. Which adjective describes his nationality?
The school builds a new wing onto its building to get more classrooms.
You buy extra memory so that your computer becomes bigger and faster.
A shop owner takes over the shop next door to make her store larger.

en: to get over, to come through, to survive
situations: After a hard illness, you finally feel better and know the worst is behind you.
You get through a very difficult exam week and are relieved that it is over.
A small boat comes through a bad storm without damage.
At the market you buy a big round fruit with green skin and sweet, red, juicy flesh inside.
In an old English film, a man wears a round, hard, black hat.
Which noun means 'melon'?
You accidentally break your friend's favourite cup and tell him you feel sad and sorry about it.
A letter from the airline says: 'We express our deep sorrow that your flight was cancelled.' Which noun fits?
Years later he still feels sad about not having studied. This feeling of wishing he had acted differently is called what?
A teacher asks you to explain exactly what a word means.
In a contract, the lawyer must state exactly what each term means.
A scientist sets out the precise meaning of a new term at the start of his paper.
The medicine works well and your headache is gone in ten minutes.
A new rule reduces traffic accidents a lot. It is a very good measure.
Which adjective means 'effective'?
You do not have exact numbers, but you guess that about 500 people came to the party.
A house expert looks at your flat and says it is worth about 200,000 euros, an approximate value.
A mechanic gives you a rough price for the repair before he starts.
You stir a spoon of sugar into your tea until the sugar has completely disappeared into the liquid. What noun names this process?
On a new computer monitor, the picture is very sharp because it has many tiny pixels. What is this quality called?
A band announces that it will stop playing together. The group is breaking up.

en: to see, to realize, to look into, to understand, to accept
situations: After an argument, you finally admit that your friend was right.
A lawyer asks to read the case files at the court office to look into them.
You made a mistake, and now you understand and accept it.
At the doctor's, a nurse measures how tall you are from head to toe in centimetres.
On a form there is a box asking how tall you are, with 'cm' next to it.
A basketball scout writes down how tall each young player is.
A neighbour always offers to carry your shopping bags up the stairs.
At work, a colleague is happy to help anyone who has a problem.
A stranger on the street stops to help an old man pick up the things he dropped.
Looking at the dark clouds and a falling barometer, you can tell a storm will come before it happens.
The boss says it is not yet possible to see how the market will develop.
It is hard to say when the road works will end. There is no end in sight.
At your grandmother's house you look at an old photo of your great-great-grandfather from the year 1900.
A family tree shows the men and women from whom you descend, long before your parents.
Which noun means 'ancestor'?
At university you choose one main area to concentrate on, such as marketing.
A magazine has a main theme this month: the climate.
In physics, the point where an object balances perfectly: you balance a ruler on your finger.
Your friend is on time every time, never once late, in all the years you have known him.
A shop's promise says that its staff are friendly to everyone, every time, without exception. Which formal adverb fits?
Which adverb means 'always' or 'constantly' in a more formal way?
You put your savings into shares of a company, hoping they will grow.
The city spends millions on new schools and trams for the future.
You spend a lot of time and energy on learning a language because it will pay off later.
Your friend said something rude about your cooking, and now you cross your arms and do not speak to him.
A boy's sister called him stupid, so he goes to his room with a sulky face.
Which adjective means 'offended'?
You see a car accident and need an ambulance quickly. Which short phone number do you dial?
A poster in your hotel lists the number to call for the police, the fire brigade or an ambulance.
Your child learns at school which short phone number to call when in danger.
You decide to give up sugar for the whole of Lent.
A sportsman announces that he will not claim the prize money and signs a paper.
Which noun means 'renunciation', the act of doing without something?

en: to come up, to arise, to pay for
situations: A new fashion starts to appear among teenagers, and suddenly everyone has it.
After the accident, the insurance company must pay for the damage.
A rumour starts to spread in the office and doubts arise in people's minds.
Under a microscope, the biology teacher shows you a single tiny living cell that can cause infections.
The doctor says your throat infection is caused by a tiny organism and gives you antibiotics.
Which noun means 'bacterium'?
You cannot visit the office, so you book your appointment by calling them.
The hotel says you can reach them in this way or by e-mail.
Which adjective means 'by phone'?
A student asks what the expression 'carbon footprint' means. It is a technical word she does not know.
A professor explains 'inflation', a key word in economics.
Which noun means 'concept' or 'term'?

en: to get by, to get along, to get on, to manage
situations: With a small salary, you manage to live without borrowing money.
You and your new flatmate get on well, with no fights.
You have no milk, but you manage with just water.
A new machine bakes the same number of loaves with much less electricity and time.
Your boss wants to improve how much work gets done per hour with the same team.
Which noun means 'efficiency'?
A marathon runner keeps going even though her legs hurt, because she can push on for a long time.
You study for months and never quit, however hard it gets.
Which noun means 'stamina' or 'perseverance'?
A dog barks, shows its teeth and jumps at everyone who comes close.
A driver shouts, honks and drives right behind other cars.
A football player pushes and shouts at his opponents all the time. Which adjective describes him?
You have tried to fix the computer for five hours and nothing works. You feel you will lose all hope.
A student fails the same exam again and again and starts to lose hope.
A man searches for his lost dog all night and begins to give up hope.
Look at one single black or white line on a zebra's coat. What is it?
You cut a long, narrow piece of paper to use as a bookmark.
The police car has a wide blue band along its side. What do you call it?
In chemistry class you learn that all matter is made of tiny particles, each too small to see, with a nucleus and electrons.
A water molecule has two hydrogen ones and one oxygen one.
Which noun means 'atom'?
The teacher asks you all to make a circle in the playground.
A good school aims to educate young people so that they learn to think.
At work, a few colleagues come together to start a new team.
A steel beam in the ceiling holds up the whole floor above it.
The newspaper says the winner of the prize, the person who now holds it, will speak tonight.
A thin strap over the shoulder holds up a summer dress. What do you call this strap?
You order pizza and pasta, food typical of Rome and Naples. Which adjective describes it?
Your neighbour comes from Milan. Which adjective describes his nationality?
In a language class you learn the language spoken in Florence.
You take a paper pad with sheets glued together at the top to write notes.
A city map shows a square area of houses between four streets, and you walk all the way around it.
In the freezer, a big solid piece of ice sits in the corner.
A cleaner takes the stain off the carpet so that it is gone.
The city removes graffiti from the wall.
Engineers find a problem in the software and get rid of it.
It is raining heavily, but you go for a run all the same. Which adverb fits in 'It rained, ... we went to the park'?
You are very tired, but you still finish the work. Which adverb means 'nevertheless'?
Which adverb means 'nonetheless' or 'still'?
Every Tuesday morning, a man in an orange vest empties the bins into a big truck.
At 6 am you are woken up by a loud truck and the man who collects the household rubbish.
A child dreams of a job where he rides on the back of the truck and lifts the bins.
Your grandpa still uses a phone with a dial and a typewriter, things from long ago.
Your sister laughs at your hat and says nobody wears such things any more.
A restaurant has curtains and furniture in the style of 1950. How does it look?

en: course of study, degree course, degree programme, degree program
situations: At university you apply for a three-year programme in business.
On the university website you can choose between law, physics or medicine. Each one is called what?
Which noun means 'degree programme'?
You get a new app and test it to see how it works.
In a store, you taste a small sample of a new ice cream flavour.
You cook a new recipe for the first time to see if it works.
The shop's sales get smaller every month. What noun describes this?
A building inspector checks the new house and officially approves it before the family moves in.
A news report talks about a fall in the number of customers.
Before a trip to Africa, a nurse gives you an injection in your arm to protect you from disease.
Parents take their baby to the doctor to get a protective injection.
Which noun means 'vaccination'?

en: to deny, to negate, to say no
situations: A witness in a courtroom TV show is asked 'Were you there?' and answers with a firm 'No'.
A boy is asked whether he took the cookie, and he says no and denies it.
Which verb means 'to deny' or 'to say no'?
After a long bus ride, your neck and legs cannot move easily and feel hard.
The cold has made the washing on the line hard and rigid like a board.
The man stands very straight and awkward, not relaxed, at the formal dinner.
A real estate agent sells houses and flats, and each one is a ... ?
You want to buy a flat as a way to keep your money safe over many years.
A bank asks what building you want to buy with the loan.

en: to survive, to outlive, to outlast
situations: A man is lost in the desert for days but is found alive.
A plant stays alive through a very cold winter.
Grandma lived ten years longer than her husband.
Bangladesh and Japan are both in this continent, the largest in the world.
You fly to Tokyo and Bangkok. Both cities are on the same continent.
Which noun is the name of the continent that includes China and India?
A rich man leaves his money to start an organisation that gives scholarships to poor students.
A charity organisation, set up with a large gift, pays for children's schools.
A museum is run by an institution that was started with a donation long ago.
At a job interview you wear a suit and use polite, careful language.
A letter to the mayor starts with 'Dear Sir or Madam'. This is the correct, official style.
Which adjective is the opposite of 'casual'?

en: to take, to grab, to seize
situations: A child sees a ball rolling away and quickly grabs it.
A good job offer appears and you do not hesitate to take the opportunity.
The school decides to take action against bullying.

en: small thing, little something, trifle, snack, bite
situations: You bring a little something as a gift for the host, nothing big.
Your friend thanks you for a huge favour, and you say 'It was nothing, just a tiny thing'.
Before dinner you have a quick small snack to stop being hungry.
There are many ways to cook rice, and each person does it in his own style.
He answered in a rude manner.
Which noun means 'way' or 'manner'?
After paying all the bills, there are only 20 euros left of your money.
After the storm, only a few trees were left in the garden.
Which verb means 'to remain'?
The club president says he feels proud and happy to welcome such a guest: 'It is my ...'.
A young athlete receives a medal in front of the crowd, a great sign of respect.
Which noun means 'honour'?
The weather, the wind and the water temperature are all perfect for sailing.
You find the best possible solution, and no better one exists.
Your boss says the team's setup could not be better.
She is a mother and a doctor, doing both at the same time.
Two buses arrive at the same moment.
Which adverb means 'at the same time'?
A famous footballer is shown in the newspaper taking secret money, and everyone talks about it, shocked.
A famous chef is caught secretly using cheap ingredients, and the news spreads all over the country.
Which noun means 'scandal'?

en: to stir, to move, to touch
situations: You use a spoon to move the soup around in the pot so that it does not burn.
A sad film makes everyone cry because the story deeply touches them.
Which verb means 'to stir'?
You throw away half the food from your plate every day. What a terrible thing to do with food!
The lights stay on in empty offices all night and use electricity for nothing.
Buying a book and never opening it is a bad use of money. Which noun means 'waste'?
In English, 'big' and 'large' mean almost the same. Which adjective describes such words?
Your teacher asks you to find another word with the same meaning as 'happy'.
The dictionary says 'glad' and 'pleased' mean the same. Both words are ... ?
You invite friends to your flat for dinner and cook for them. What are you?
The country where the Olympic Games take place welcomes teams from all over the world.
At a party, the man who welcomes people at the door and gives them drinks is the ... ?

en: to radiate, to emit, to exude, to broadcast
situations: The TV channel shows the film tonight at 8 pm.
The sun gives off heat and light.
She walks in, and everybody feels her calm and happiness. She gives off confidence.
At the supermarket you carry a plastic box with twelve bottles of water to your car.
After the party you take the empty bottles back to the shop in a plastic box.
Which noun means 'drinks crate'?
At the beach in northern Germany, you climb a hill of sand covered with grass.
In the Sahara, wind forms big hills of sand.
A camel walks slowly over a high hill of sand in the desert.
A snail slowly moves over the garden path, leaving a slimy trail.
In a training exercise, a soldier moves forward on his belly under a low net.
Traffic is so slow in a jam that cars barely move forward.
The teacher tells you to sit with your back straight, not slouching.
A tree stands tall and vertical after the storm.
Penguins walk on land standing straight on two legs.
Your hotel room is dirty, so you go to reception and say you are not happy.
A customer writes a letter to the shop manager about bad service.
A neighbour tells you he is annoyed about loud music late at night.
A company launches a website where sellers and buyers meet online.
A video-sharing app is a place where many people upload and watch films.
Workers stand on a flat, raised surface on the side of a building.

en: to look at, to regard, to view, to consider, to watch
